\PYG{l+m+mi}{7} \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.00}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.50}      \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{95}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.000000}      \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.948187}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{8} \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.40}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.30}      \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{30}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.400000}      \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.228342}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The first row holds the input sequence, the successive list the local
minima ascending in energy. The meaning of the first 5 columns is as follows
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
label (number) of the local minima (1=MFE)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
structure of the minimum

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
free energy of the minimum

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
label of deeper local minimum the current minimum merges with (note that the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{MFE}} has no deeper local minimum to merge with)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
height of the energy barrier to the local minimum to merge with

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
numbers of structures in the basin we merge with

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of basin which we merge to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
free energy of the basin

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
number of structures in this basin using gradient walk

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gradient basin (consisting of all structures where gradientwalk ends in the minimum)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{barriers}} produced two additional files, the \sphinxstyleemphasis{PostScript} file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tree.eps}}
which represents the basic information of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{barseq.bar}} file visually:

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.500\linewidth]{{tree}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and a text file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rates.out}} which holds the matrix of transition probabilities
between the local minima.


\subsubsection{Simulating the Folding Kinetics}
\label{\detokenize{tutorial/barriers_treekin:simulating-the-folding-kinetics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The program \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{treekin}} is used to simulate the evolution over time of the
population densities of local minima starting from an initial population
density distribution \(p0\) (given on the command\sphinxhyphen{}line) and the transition
rate matrix in the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{rates.out}}.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} treekin \PYGZhy{}m I \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}p0 5=1 \PYGZlt{} barseq.bar | xmgrace \PYGZhy{}log x \PYGZhy{}nxy \PYGZhy{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.550\linewidth]{{FOO}.png} \sphinxincludegraphics[width=0.400\linewidth]{{FOO_dp}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The simulation starts with all the population density in the open chain
(local minimum 5, see \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{barseq.bar}}). Over time the population density of
this state decays (yellow curve) and other local minima get populated.
The simulation ends with the population densities of the thermodynamic
equilibrium in which the MFE (black curve) and local minimum 2 (red curve)
are the only ones populated. (Look at the dot plot of the sequence created
with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNAsubopt}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNAfold}}!)


\section{Other Utilities}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started:other-utilities}}
\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Utilities}
\label{\detokenize{utilities:utilities}}\label{\detokenize{utilities::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We also ship a number of small utilities, many of them to manipulate the
PostScript files produced by the structure prediction programs {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAfold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAfold}}}}
and {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAalifold}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Most of the \sphinxtitleref{Perl 5} utilities contain embedded \sphinxtitleref{pod} documentation. Type e.g.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
perldoc\PYG{+w}{ }relplot.pl
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
for detailed instructions.


\subsubsection{Available Tools}
\label{\detokenize{utilities:available-tools}}

\begin{savenotes}\sphinxattablestart
\sphinxthistablewithglobalstyle
\centering
\begin{tabular}[t]{*{2}{\X{1}{2}}}
\sphinxtoprule
\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tool Name
&\sphinxstyletheadfamily 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Description
\\
\sphinxmidrule
\sphinxtableatstartofbodyhook
\sphinxAtStartPar
ct2db
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Produce dot bracket notation of an RNA secondary structure
\item[] given as mfold \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.ct}} file
\end{DUlineblock}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
b2mt.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Produce a mountain representation of a secondary structure
\item[] from it’s dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation, as produced by {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAfold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAfold}}}}.
\item[] Output consists of simple \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x y}} data suitable as input to a
\item[] plotting program. The mountain representation is a xy plot with
\item[] sequence position on the x\sphinxhyphen{}axis and the number of base pairs
\item[] enclosing that position on the y\sphinxhyphen{}axis.
\end{DUlineblock}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatimintable}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
RNAfold\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZlt{}\PYG{+w}{ }my.seq\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }b2mt.pl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{|}\PYG{+w}{ }xmgrace\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}pipe
\end{sphinxVerbatimintable}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{5smnt}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
cmount.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Produce a PostScript mountain plot from a color dot plot as
\item[] created by {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAalifold}}}} \sphinxhyphen{}p or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alidot \sphinxhyphen{}p}}. Each base pair
\item[] is represented by a trapez whose color encodes the number of
\item[] consistent and compensatory mutations supporting that pair:
\item[] Red marks pairs with no sequence variation; ochre, green, turquoise,
\item[] blue, and violet mark pairs with 2,3,4,5,6 different types of pairs,
\item[] respectively.
\end{DUlineblock}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatimintable}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
cmount.pl\PYG{+w}{ }alidot.ps\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }cmount.ps
\end{sphinxVerbatimintable}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{TAR_ss}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
coloraln.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Reads a sequence alignment in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{CLUSTAL}} format and a consensus
\item[] secondary structure (which it extracts from a secondary structure
\item[] plot as produced by {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAalifold}}}}), and produces a postscript figure
\item[] of the alignment annotated using the consensus structure, coloring
\item[] base pair using the same color scheme as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cmount.pl}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAalifold}}}}
\item[] and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{alidot}}.
\end{DUlineblock}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatimintable}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
coloraln.pl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}s\PYG{+w}{ }alirna.ps\PYG{+w}{ }file.aln\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }coloraln.ps
\end{sphinxVerbatimintable}

\noindent{\hspace*{\fill}\sphinxincludegraphics{{TAR_aln}.png}\hspace*{\fill}}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
colorrna.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Reads a consensus secondary structure plot and a color dot plot
\item[] as produced by {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAalifold}}}} \sphinxhyphen{}p, and writes a new secondary
\item[] structure plot in which base pairs a colored using the color

Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatimintable}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\end{sphinxVerbatimintable}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
mountain.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Similar to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b2mt.pl}}, but produces a mountain plot from the
\item[] pair probabilities contained in a PostScript dot plot. It write
\item[] 3 sets of x y data, suitable as input for a plot program. The
\item[] first two sets containing the mountain representation from pair
\item[] probabilities and MFE structure, the third set is the
\item[] “positional entropy” a measure of structural well\sphinxhyphen{}definedness.
\end{DUlineblock}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatimintable}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

&
\sphinxAtStartPar
Refold using consensus structure as constraint

&

rotate\_ss.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Reads a postscript secondary structure plot as produced by
\item[] {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAfold::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{RNAfold}}}} and produces a new rotated and/or mirrored
\item[] structure plot.
\end{DUlineblock}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatimintable}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
rotate\PYGZus{}ss.pl\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}a\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{30}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }foo\PYGZus{}ss.ps\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZgt{}\PYG{+w}{ }foo\PYGZus{}new\PYGZus{}ss.ps
\end{sphinxVerbatimintable}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
switch.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Design sequences that can adopt two different structure, i.e.
\item[] design RNA switches. The program will sample the set of sequences
\item[] compatible with two input structures in order to find sequences with
\item[] desired thermodynamic and kinetic properties. In particular it is
\item[] possible to specify two different temperatures such that structure
\item[] 1 is favored at T1 and structure 2 at T2 to design temperature
\item[] sensitive switches (RNA thermometers). The desired height of the
\item[] energy barrier separating the two structures, thus determining
\item[] the refolding time between meta\sphinxhyphen{}stable states.
\end{DUlineblock}
\\
\sphinxhline
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAdesign.pl
&
\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] Flexible design of multi\sphinxhyphen{}stable RNA molecules. An initially random
\item[] sequence is iteratively mutated and evaluated according to an
\item[] objective function (see Option: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}optfun}}). Whenever a better
\item[] scoring sequence has been found, the mutation is accepted, the
\item[] algorithm terminates once a local minimum is found. This script
\item[] makes heavy use of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA::Design}} sub\sphinxhyphen{}package that comes
\item[] with the ViennaRNA Package \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Perl 5}} interface.
\end{DUlineblock}
\\

\chapter{Manpages}
\label{\detokenize{manpages:manpages}}\label{\detokenize{manpages::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ViennaRNA Package comes with a number of executable
programs that provide command line interfaces to the most
important algorithms implemented in \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib}.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA2Dfold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute MFE structure, partition function and representative sample structures
of k,l neighborhoods

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program partitions the secondary structure space into (basepair)distance
classes according to two fixed reference structures. It expects a sequence and
two secondary structures in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation as its inputs. For each
distance class, the MFE representative, Boltzmann probabilities and Gibbs free
energy is computed. Additionally, a stochastic backtracking routine allows one
to produce samples of representative suboptimal secondary structures from each
partition

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAaliduplex:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAaliduplex 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Predict conserved RNA\sphinxhyphen{}RNA interactions between two alignments

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads two alignments of RNA sequences in CLUSTAL format and
predicts optimal and suboptimal binding sites, hybridization energies and the
corresponding structures. The calculation takes only inter\sphinxhyphen{}molecular base pairs
into account, for the general case use RNAcofold. The use of alignments allows
one to focus on binding sites that are evolutionary conserved. Note, that the
two input alignments need to have equal number of sequences and the same order,
i.e. the 1st sequence in file1 will be hybridized to the 1st in file2 etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The computed binding sites, energies, and structures are written to stdout, one
structure per line. Each line consist of: The structure in dot bracket format
with a “\&” separating the two strands. The range of the structure in the two
sequences in the format  “from,to : from,to”; the energy of duplex structure
in kcal/mol.
The format is especially useful for computing the hybrid structure between a
small probe sequence and a long target sequence.

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAaliduplex:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAaliduplex:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAaliduplex:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the

pairs, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-nsp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp=}}}}}”\sphinxhyphen{}GA”  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAalifold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate secondary structures for a set of aligned RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
Read aligned RNA sequences from stdin or file.aln and calculate their minimum
free energy (mfe) structure, partition function (pf) and base pairing
probability matrix. Currently, input alignments have to be in CLUSTAL,
Stockholm, FASTA, or MAF format. The input format must be set manually in
interactive mode (default is Clustal), but will be determined automagically
from the input file, if not expplicitly set. It returns the mfe structure in
bracket notation, its energy, the free energy of the thermodynamic ensemble and
the frequency of the mfe structure in the ensemble to stdout.  It also produces
Postscript files with plots of the resulting secondary structure graph
(“alirna.ps”) and a “dot plot” of the base pairing matrix (“alidot.ps”).
The file “alifold.out” will contain a list of likely pairs sorted by
credibility, suitable for viewing  with “AliDot.pl”. Be warned that output
file will overwrite any existing files of the same name.

\subsubsection{I/O Options:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:i-o-options}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options for input and output (pre\sphinxhyphen{})processing
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}f@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}f@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}f}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}input\sphinxhyphen{}format@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}input\sphinxhyphen{}format}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}input\sphinxhyphen{}format@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}input\sphinxhyphen{}format}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-f}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-input-format}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}input\sphinxhyphen{}format}}\DUrole{p}{=}C|S|F|M}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
File format of the input multiple sequence alignment (MSA).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, the input is considered to be in a particular file
format. Otherwise, the program tries to determine the file format
automatically, if an input file was provided in the set of parameters. In
case the input MSA is provided in interactive mode, or from a terminal (TTY),
the programs default is to assume CLUSTALW format.
Currently, the following formats are available: ClustalW (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}), Stockholm 1.0
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}), FASTA/Pearson (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F}}), and MAF (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}).

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}mis@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}mis}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}mis@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}mis}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-mis}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}mis}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Output “most informative sequence” instead of simple consensus: For each column of the alignment output the set of nucleotides with frequency greater than average in IUPAC notation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-jobs}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=number\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads as computation cores are available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
alignment at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many alignments in the input in parallel. RNAalifold will
create as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input
alignments of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this
increases memory consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory
until an empty compute slot is available and each running job requires its
own dynamic programming matrices.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-unordered}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not try to keep output in order with input while parallel processing is in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When parallel input processing ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}}}} flag) is enabled, the order in which
input is processed depends on the host machines job scheduler. Therefore, any
output to stdout or files generated by this program will most likely not
follow the order of the corresponding input data set. The default of
RNAalifold is to use a specialized data structure to still keep the results
output in order with the input data. However, this comes with a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off in
terms of memory consumption, since all output must be kept in memory for as
long as no chunks of consecutive, ordered output are available. By setting
this flag, RNAalifold will not buffer individual results but print them as
soon as they have been computated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-noconv}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not automatically substitute nucleotide “T” with “U”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}n@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}n}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}n@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}n}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-n}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-continuous-ids}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}n}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use continuous alignment ID numbering when no alignment ID can be retrieved from input data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Due to its past, RNAalifold produces a specific set of output file names for
the first input alignment, “alirna.ps”, “alidot.ps”, etc. But for all
further alignments in the input, it usually adopts a naming scheme based on
IDs, which may be retrieved from the input alignment’s meta\sphinxhyphen{}data, or
generated by a prefix followed by an increasing counter. Setting this flag
instructs RNAalifold to use the ID naming scheme also for the first
alignment.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each alignment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAalifold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input alignment if the input file format allows to do that. Alignment IDs
are, for instance, usually given in Stockholm 1.0 formatted input. If this
flag is active, RNAalifold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and
automatically generates an ID for each alignment.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-id-prefix}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”alignment”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each alignment will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:
“prefix\_xxxx\_ss.ps” (secondary structure plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp.ps”
(dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_aln.ps” (annotated alignment), etc. where xxxx is
the alignment number beginning with the second alignment in the input. Use
this setting in conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-n}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}}}} flag to assign IDs
beginning with the first input alignment.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiter between prefix and increasing number for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\_”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the default delimiter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_}} between the
prefix string and the increasing number for automatically generated ID.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-id-digits}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the first number in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignment IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, usually starting with 1. Using this parameter, the first number can

Note: Setting this parameter implies continuous alignment IDs, i.e. it

Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}



\subsubsection{Algorithms:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:algorithms}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select additional algorithms which should be included in the calculations.
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-p}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-partfunc}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=INT\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the partition function and base pairing probability matrix in addition to the mfe structure. Default is calculation of mfe structure only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the MFE structure we print a coarse representation of the pair
probabilities in form of a pseudo bracket notation, followed by the ensemble
free energy, as well as the centroid structure derived from the pair
probabilities together with its free energy and distance to the ensemble.
Finally it prints the frequency of the mfe structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An additionally passed value to this option changes the behavior of partition
function calculation:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p0}} deactivates the calculation of the pair probabilities, saving about 50\%
in runtime. This prints the ensemble free energy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG=\sphinxhyphen{}kT ln(Z)}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-betaScale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\DUrole{p}{=}DOUBLE}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the scaling of the Boltzmann factors. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument provided with this option is used to scale the thermodynamic
temperature in the Boltzmann factors independently from the temperature of
the individual loop energy contributions. The Boltzmann factors then become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(\sphinxhyphen{} dG/(kTn*betaScale))}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} is the Boltzmann constant, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG}} the
free energy contribution of the state, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} the absolute temperature and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{n}}
the number of sequences.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-S}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-pfScale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}S}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}}\DUrole{p}{=}DOUBLE}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the calculation of the pf use scale*mfe as an estimate for the ensemble free energy (used to avoid overflows).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.07”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default is 1.07, useful values are 1.0 to 1.2. Occasionally needed for
long sequences.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-MEA}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=gamma\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute MEA (maximum expected accuracy) structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expected accuracy is computed from the pair probabilities: each base pair
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i,j)}} receives a score \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2*gamma*p\_ij}} and the score of an unpaired base is
given by the probability of not forming a pair. The parameter gamma tunes the
importance of correctly predicted pairs versus unpaired bases. Thus, for
small values of gamma the MEA structure will contain only pairs with very
high probability. Using {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-MEA}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}}}} implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} for computing the pair
probabilities.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Structure Constraints:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:structure-constraints}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options to interact with the structure constraints feature of
this program
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the maximum base pair span.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\sphinxhyphen{}1”)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}C@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}C@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}C}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-C}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-constraint}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=filename\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate structures subject to constraints. The constraining structure will be read from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stdin}}, the alignment has to be given as a file name on the command line.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=””)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads first the sequence, then a string containing constraints on
the structure encoded with the symbols:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}} (no constraint for this base)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}} (the corresponding base has to be paired

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} (the base is unpaired)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textgreater{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textless{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
and matching brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} (base i pairs base j)

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the exception of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, constraints will disallow all pairs conflicting
with the constraint. This is usually sufficient to enforce the constraint,
but occasionally a base may stay unpaired in spite of constraints. PF folding
ignores constraints of type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-batch}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use constraints for all alignment records. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually, constraints provided from input file are only applied to a single
sequence alignment. Therefore, RNAalifold will stop its computation and quit
after the first input alignment was processed. Using this switch, RNAalifold
processes all sequence alignments in the input and applies the same provided
constraints to each of them.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enforceConstraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enforceConstraint}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enforceConstraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enforceConstraint}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-enforceConstraint}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}enforceConstraint}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Enforce base pairs given by round brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} in structure constraint.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}SS\_cons@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}SS\_cons}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}SS\_cons@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}SS\_cons}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-SS_cons}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}SS\_cons}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use consensus structures from Stockholm file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#=GF SS\_cons}}) as constraint.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Stockholm formatted alignment files have the possibility to store a secondary
structure string in one of if (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\#=GC}}) column annotation meta tags. The
corresponding tag name is usually \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SS\_cons}}, a consensus secondary structure.
Activating this flag allows one to use this consensus secondary structure
from the input file as structure constraint. Currently, only the following
characters are interpreted:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} {[}mathing parenthesis: column i pairs with column j{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} {[}matching angular brackets: column i pairs with column j{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All other characters are not interpreted (yet).
Note: Activating this flag implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-C}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shape@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shape}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shape@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shape}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-shape}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shape}}\DUrole{p}{=}file1,file2}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use SHAPE reactivity data to guide structure predictions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple shapefiles for the individual sequences in the alignment may be
specified  as a comma separated list. An optional association of particular
shape files to a specific  sequence in the alignment can be expressed by
prepending the sequence number to the filename,  e.g.
“5=seq5.shape,3=seq3.shape” will assign the reactivity values from file
seq5.shape to  the fifth sequence in the alignment, and the values from file
seq3.shape to sequence 3. If  no assignment is specified, the reactivity
values are assigned to corresponding sequences in  the order they are given.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the method how to convert SHAPE reactivity data to pseudo energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, the only data conversion method available is that of to Deigan et
al 2009.  This method is the default and is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in
the provided parameter, i.e.:  {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting.
The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}} and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a  non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if
necessary. Otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6 as stated in the paper mentionen
before.  To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7, use a  parameter
string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also provide only one
of the two  parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Db\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”.

Create a multi\sphinxhyphen{}Stockholm formatted output file. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”RNAalifold\_results”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default file name used for the output is “RNAalifold\_results.stk”.
Users may change the filename to “prefix.stk” by specifying the prefix as
optional argument. The file will be create in the current directory if it
does not already exist. In case the file already exists, output will be
appended to it. Note: Any special characters in the filename will be replaced
by the filename delimiter, hence there is no way to pass an entire directory
path through this option yet. (See also the “\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select the layout algorithm that computes the nucleotide coordinates.
Currently, the following algorithms are available:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}}: simple radial layout

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1}}: Naview layout (Bruccoleri et al. 1988)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2}}: circular layout

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3}}: RNAturtle (Wiegreffe et al. 2018)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{4}}: RNApuzzler (Wiegreffe et al. 2018)

\end{fulllineitems}


\sphinxAtStartPar
Caveats:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sequences are not weighted. If possible, do not mix very similar and dissimilar
sequences. Duplicate sequences, for example, can distort the prediction.


\subsection{REFERENCES}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:references}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{If you use this program in your work you might want to cite:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
R. Lorenz, S.H. Bernhart, C. Hoener zu Siederdissen, H. Tafer, C. Flamm, P.F. Stadler and I.L. Hofacker (2011),
“ViennaRNA Package 2.0”,

\sphinxAtStartPar

“Fast Folding and Comparison of RNA Secondary Structures”,
Monatshefte f. Chemie: 125, pp 167\sphinxhyphen{}188

\sphinxAtStartPar
R. Lorenz, I.L. Hofacker, P.F. Stadler (2016),
“RNA folding with hard and soft constraints”,
Algorithms for Molecular Biology 11:1 pp 1\sphinxhyphen{}13

\sphinxAtStartPar
The algorithm is a variant of the dynamic programming algorithms of M. Zuker and P. Stiegler (mfe)
and J.S. McCaskill (pf) adapted for sets of aligned sequences with covariance information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ivo L. Hofacker, Martin Fekete, and Peter F. Stadler (2002),
“Secondary Structure Prediction for Aligned RNA Sequences”,
J.Mol.Biol.: 319, pp 1059\sphinxhyphen{}1066.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Stephan H. Bernhart, Ivo L. Hofacker, Sebastian Will, Andreas R. Gruber, and Peter F. Stadler (2008),
“RNAalifold: Improved consensus structure prediction for RNA alignments”,
BMC Bioinformatics: 9, pp 474

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{The energy parameters are taken from:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
D.H. Mathews, M.D. Disney, D. Matthew, J.L. Childs, S.J. Schroeder, J. Susan, M. Zuker, D.H. Turner (2004),
“Incorporating chemical modification constraints into a dynamic programming algorithm for prediction of RNA secondary structure”,
Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA: 101, pp 7287\sphinxhyphen{}7292

\sphinxAtStartPar

“NNDB: The nearest neighbor parameter database for predicting stability of nucleic acid secondary structure”,
Nucleic Acids Research: 38, pp 280\sphinxhyphen{}282


\subsection{EXAMPLES}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:examples}}

A simple call to compute consensus MFE structure, ensemble free energy,
base pair probabilities, centroid structure, and MEA structure for a
multiple sequence alignment (MSA) provided as Stockholm formatted file
alignment.stk might look like:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAalifold \PYGZhy{}p \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}MEA alignment.stk
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, the first line is written to \sphinxstyleemphasis{stderr} and simply states the number of sequences and
the length of the alignment. This line can be suppressed using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-q}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}quiet}}}}} option.
The main output then consists of 7 lines, where the first two resemble the FASTA header
with the ID as read from the input data set, followed by the consensus sequence in the
second line. The third line consists of the consensus secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket
notation followed by the averaged minimum free energy in parenthesis. This energy is
composed of two major contributions, the actual free energies derived from the Nearest
Neighbor model, and the covariance pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}energy term, which are both displayed after
the equal sign. The fourth line shows the base pair propensity in pseudo dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket
notation followed by the ensemble free energy dG = \sphinxhyphen{}kT ln(Z) in square brackets.
Similarly, the next two lines state the controid\sphinxhyphen{} and the MEA structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket
notation, followed by their corresponding free energy contributions, the mean distance
(d) to the ensemble as well as the maximum expected accuracy (MEA). Again, the free
energies are split into Nearest Neighbor contribution and the covariance pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}energy
term.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Furthermore, RNAalifold will produce three output files: ACA59\_ss.ps, ACA59\_dp.ps, and
ACA59\_ali.out that contain the secondary structure drawing, the base pair probability
dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot, and a detailed table of base pair probabilities, respectively.


\subsection{THE ALIOUT FILE}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:the-aliout-file}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When computing base pair probabilities ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}}}} option), RNAalifold will produce
a file with the suffix \sphinxtitleref{ali.out}. This file contains the base pairing probabilities between
different alignment columns together with some detailed statistics for the individual
sequences within the alignment. The file is a simple text file with a two line header that
states the number of sequences and length of the alignment. The first couple of lines
of this file may look like:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{l+m+mi}{3} \PYG{n}{sequence}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{length} \PYG{n}{of} \PYG{n}{alignment} \PYG{l+m+mi}{84}
\PYG{n}{alifold} \PYG{n}{output}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{14}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{36}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{92.7}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.212} \PYG{n}{CG}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}    \PYG{n}{UA}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{13}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{37}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{92.7}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.218} \PYG{n}{GU}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}    \PYG{n}{AU}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{12}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{38}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{92.7}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.231} \PYG{n}{CG}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{15}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{35}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{91.9}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.239} \PYG{n}{UG}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{16}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{34}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{85.2}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.434} \PYG{n}{UA}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}    \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{8}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{42}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{80.7}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.526} \PYG{n}{AU}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}   \PYG{o}{+}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{9}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{41}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{80.4}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.542} \PYG{n}{CG}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}   \PYG{o}{+}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{7}    \PYG{l+m+mi}{43}  \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{80.1}\PYG{o}{\PYGZpc{}}   \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.541} \PYG{n}{CG}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}   \PYG{o}{+}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Starting with the third row, there are at least six and at most 13 columns separated by
whitespaces stating: (1) the i\sphinxhyphen{}position and (2) the j\sphinxhyphen{}position of a potential base pair
(i, j), followed by (3) the number of counter examples, i.e. the number of sequences in
the alignment that can’t form a canonical base pair with their respective sequence positions.
Next is (4) the base pair probabilitiy in percent, (5) a pseudo entropy measure
S\_ij = S\_i + S\_j \sphinxhyphen{} p\_ij ln(p\_ij), where S\_i and S\_j are the positional entropies for the
two alignment columns i and j, and p\_ij is the base pair probability. Finally, the last
columns (6\sphinxhyphen{}12) state the number of particular base pairs for the individual sequences in
the alignment. Here, we distinguish the base pairs “GC”,”CG”,”AU”,”UA”,”GU”,”UG”, and
the special case “\textendash{}” that represents gaps at both positions i and j.
Finally, base pairs that are not part of the MFE structure are marked by an additional
“+” sign in the last column.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAcofold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate secondary structures of two RNAs with dimerization

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program works much like RNAfold, but allows one to specify two RNA
sequences which are then allowed to form a dimer structure. RNA sequences are
read from stdin in the usual format, i.e. each line of input corresponds to one
sequence, except for lines starting with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} which contain the name of the next
sequence.
To compute the hybrid structure of two molecules, the two sequences must be
concatenated using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} character as separator.
RNAcofold can compute minimum free energy (mfe) structures, as well as
partition function (pf) and base pairing probability matrix (using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}
switch)
Since dimer formation is concentration dependent, RNAcofold can be used to
compute equilibrium concentrations for all five monomer and (homo/hetero)\sphinxhyphen{}dimer
species, given input concentrations for the monomers.
Output consists of the mfe structure in bracket notation as well as PostScript
structure plots and “dot plot” files containing the pair probabilities, see
the RNAfold man page for details. In the dot plots a cross marks the chain
break between the two concatenated sequences.
The program will continue to read new sequences until a line consisting of the
single character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} or an end of file condition is encountered.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-j}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-jobs}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=number\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads as computation cores are available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
sequence pair at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many sequence pairs in the input in parallel. RNAcofold will
create as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input
sequences of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this
increases memory consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory
until an empty compute slot is available and each running job requires its
own dynamic programming matrices.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-unordered}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not try to keep output in order with input while parallel processing is in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When parallel input processing ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}}}} flag) is enabled, the order in which
input is processed depends on the host machines job scheduler. Therefore, any
output to stdout or files generated by this program will most likely not
follow the order of the corresponding input data set. The default of
RNAcofold is to use a specialized data structure to still keep the results
output in order with the input data. However, this comes with a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off in
terms of memory consumption, since all output must be kept in memory for as
long as no chunks of consecutive, ordered output are available. By setting
this flag, RNAcofold will not buffer individual results but print them as
soon as they have been computated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-auto-id}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAcofold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAcofold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-id-prefix}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequence will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:
“prefix\_xxxx\_ss.ps” (secondary structure plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp.ps”
(dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp2.ps” (stack probabilities), etc. where xxxx is
the sequence number. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the default delimiter “\_” between the
prefix string and the increasing number for automatically generated ID.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-id-digits}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}. This option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the first number in automatically generated IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When sequence IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, usually starting with 1. Using this parameter, the first number can
be specified to the users requirements. Note: negative numbers are not
allowed.
Note: Setting this parameter implies to ignore any IDs retrieved from the
input data, i.e. it activates the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} flag.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001\_ss.ps” for secondary structure
plots. With this flag set, no truncation of the output filenames is done,
i.e. output filenames receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note,
however, that invalid characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by
a delimiting character or simply removed, (see also the parameter option
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\end{fulllineitems}



\subsubsection{Algorithms:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:algorithms}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select additional algorithms which should be included in the calculations.
The Minimum free energy (MFE) and a structure representative are calculated
in any case.
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-p}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-partfunc}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=INT\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the partition function and base pairing probability matrix in addition to the mfe structure. Default is calculation of mfe structure only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the MFE structure we print a coarse representation of the pair
probabilities in form of a pseudo bracket notation, followed by the ensemble
free energy, as well as the centroid structure derived from the pair
probabilities together with its free energy and distance to the ensemble.
Finally it prints the frequency of the mfe structure, and the structural
diversity (mean distance between the structures in the ensemble).
See the description of pf\_fold() and mean\_bp\_dist() and centroid() in the
RNAlib documentation for details.
Note that unless you also specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}}, the partition function and mfe
calculations will use a slightly different energy model. See the discussion
of dangling end options below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An additionally passed value to this option changes the behavior of partition
function calculation:

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to calculate the partition function but not the pair probabilities

\sphinxAtStartPar
use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p0}} option and save about

\sphinxAtStartPar
50\% in runtime. This prints the ensemble free energy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG=\sphinxhyphen{}kT ln(Z)}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}a@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}a@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}a}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-a}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-all_pf}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=INT\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the partition function and free energies not only of the hetero\sphinxhyphen{}dimer consisting of the two input sequences (the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AB dimer}}), but also of the homo\sphinxhyphen{}dimers AA and BB as well as A and B monomers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output will contain the free energies for each of these species, as well
as 5 dot plots containing the conditional pair probabilities, called
“ABname5.ps”, “AAname5.ps” and so on. For later use, these dot plot files
also contain the free energy of the ensemble as a comment. Using {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-a}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}}}}
automatically switches on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} option. Base pair probability computations
may be turned off altogether by providing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{0}} as an argument to this
parameter. In that case, no dot plot files will be generated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-betaScale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\DUrole{p}{=}DOUBLE}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the scaling of the Boltzmann factors. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument provided with this option is used to scale the thermodynamic
temperature in the Boltzmann factors independently from the temperature of
the individual loop energy contributions. The Boltzmann factors then become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(\sphinxhyphen{} dG/(kT*betaScale))}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} is the Boltzmann constant, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG}} the free
energy contribution of the state and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} the absolute temperature.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

long sequences.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}centroid@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}centroid}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}centroid@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}centroid}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}centroid}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the centroid structure. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Additionally to the MFE structure, compute the centroid representative of the
structure ensemble. Here, we apply the base pair distance as distance
measure, and report the structure that minimizes its Boltzmann weighted base
pair distance to the rest of the ensemble. Computing the centroid structure
requires equilibrium base pair probabilities. Therefore, this option implies
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} switch. For historical reasons, the centroid structure output is
deactivated by default.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-MEA}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=gamma\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute MEA (maximum expected accuracy) structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expected accuracy is computed from the pair probabilities: each base pair
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i,j)}} receives a score \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2*gamma*p\_ij}} and the score of an unpaired base is
given by the probability of not forming a pair. The parameter gamma tunes the
importance of correctly predicted pairs versus unpaired bases. Thus, for
small values of gamma the MEA structure will contain only pairs with very
high probability. Using {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-MEA}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}}}} implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} for computing the pair
probabilities.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the threshold/cutoff for base pair probabilities included in the postscript output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1e\sphinxhyphen{}5”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By setting the threshold the base pair probabilities that are included in the
output can be varied. By default only those exceeding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1e\sphinxhyphen{}5}} in probability
will be shown as squares in the dot plot. Changing the threshold to any other
value allows for increase or decrease of data.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Structure Constraints:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options to interact with the structure constraints feature of
this program
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}
