Set the maximum base pair span.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\sphinxhyphen{}1”)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}C@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}C@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}C}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-C}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-constraint}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=filename\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate structures subject to constraints. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=””)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads first the sequence, then a string containing constraints on
the structure encoded with the symbols:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}} (no constraint for this base)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}} (the corresponding base has to be paired

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} (the base is unpaired)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textgreater{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textless{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
and matching brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} (base i pairs base j)

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the exception of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, constraints will disallow all pairs conflicting
with the constraint. This is usually sufficient to enforce the constraint,
but occasionally a base may stay unpaired in spite of constraints. PF folding
ignores constraints of type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use constraints for multiple sequences. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually, constraints provided from input file only apply to a single input
sequence. Therefore, RNAcofold will stop its computation and quit after the
first input sequence was processed. Using this switch, RNAcofold processes
multiple input sequences and applies the same provided constraints to each of
them.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select SHAPE reactivity data incorporation strategy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE reactivities into pseudo
energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Convert by using the linear equation according to Deigan et al 2009.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Derived pseudo energy terms will be applied for every nucleotide involved in
a stacked pair. This method is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in the provided
parameter, i.e.: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting. The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}}
and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if necessary,
otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6. To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7,
use a parameter string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also
provide only one of the two parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Db\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}: Convert SHAPE reactivities to pseudo energies according to Zarringhalam

\sphinxAtStartPar
et al 2012. SHAPE reactivities will be converted to pairing probabilities by
using linear mapping. Aberration from the observed pairing probabilities will
be penalized during the folding recursion. The magnitude of the penalties can
affected by adjusting the factor beta (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Zb0.8”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}}: Apply a given vector of perturbation energies to unpaired nucleotides

\sphinxAtStartPar
according to Washietl et al 2012. Perturbation vectors can be calculated by
using RNApvmin.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-shapeConversion}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select method for SHAPE reactivity conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”O”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter is useful when dealing with the SHAPE incorporation according
to Zarringhalam et al. The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE
reactivities into the probability for a certain nucleotide to be unpaired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}: Use linear mapping according to Zarringhalam et al.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}: Use a cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}approach to divide into paired and unpaired nucleotides
(e.g. “C0.25”)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}: Skip the normalizing step since the input data already represents
probabilities for being unpaired rather than raw reactivity values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}: Use a linear model to convert the reactivity into a probability for
being unpaired (e.g. “Ls0.68i0.2” to use a slope of 0.68 and an intercept
of 0.2)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{O}}: Use a linear model to convert the log of the reactivity into a
probability for being unpaired (e.g. “Os1.6i\sphinxhyphen{}2.29” to use a slope of 1.6
and an intercept of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.29)

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}m}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=STRING\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow for modified bases within the RNA sequence string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”7I6P9D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat modified bases within the RNA sequence differently, i.e. use
corresponding energy corrections and/or pairing partner rules if available.
For that, the modified bases in the input sequence must be marked by their
corresponding one\sphinxhyphen{}letter code. If no additional arguments are supplied, all
available corrections are performed. Otherwise, the user may limit the
modifications to a particular subset of modifications, resp. one\sphinxhyphen{}letter
codes, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}mP6}} will only correct for pseudouridine and m6A bases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently supported one\sphinxhyphen{}letter codes and energy corrections are:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}: 7\sphinxhyphen{}deaza\sphinxhyphen{}adenonsine (7DA)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{I}}: Inosine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}}: N6\sphinxhyphen{}methyladenosine (m6A)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}: Pseudouridine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}}: Purine (a.k.a. nebularine)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Dihydrouridine

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar

2) pairs.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAdistance:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAdistance 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate distances between RNA secondary structures

\sphinxAtStartPar
This program reads RNA secondary structures from stdin and calculates one or
more measures for their dissimilarity, based on tree or string editing
(alignment). In addition it calculates a “base pair distance” given by the
number of base pairs present in one structure, but not the other. For
structures of different length base pair distance is not recommended.

\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAdistance accepts structures in bracket format, where matching brackets
symbolize base pairs and unpaired bases are represented by a dot \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}},
or coarse grained representations where hairpins, interior loops,
bulges, multiloops, stacks and external bases are represented by
(H), (I), (B), (M), (S), and (E), respectively. These can be optionally
weighted. Full structures can be represented in the same fashion using
the identifiers (U) and (P) for unpaired and paired bases, respectively.
We call this the HIT representation (you don’t want to know what this means).
For example the following structure consists of 2 hairpins joined by
a multiloop:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}       \PYG{n}{full} \PYG{n}{structure} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{usual} \PYG{n+nb}{format}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{U}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{U2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{U3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{P3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{U2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{U2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{P2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{P2}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{n}{HIT} \PYG{n}{structure}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{o+ow}{or}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{S}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{H}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{S}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{M}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{S}\PYG{p}{)}              \PYG{n}{coarse} \PYG{n}{grained} \PYG{n}{structure}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{H3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{S3}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{H2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{S2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{M4}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{S2}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{E2}\PYG{p}{)}    \PYG{n}{weighted} \PYG{n}{coarse} \PYG{n}{grained}\PYG{o}{.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program will continue to read new structures until a line consisting
of the single character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} or an end of file condition is encountered. Input
lines neither containing a valid structure nor starting with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} are ignored.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the distance representation to be used in calculations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”f”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the full, HIT, weighted coarse, or coarse representation to calculate the
distance. Capital letters indicate string alignment otherwise tree editing is
used.
Any combination of distances can bespecified.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}X@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}X}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}X@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}X}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAdistance:cmdoption-X}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAdistance:cmdoption-compare}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}X}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}compare}}\DUrole{p}{=}p|m|f|c}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the comparison directive. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”p”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Possible arguments for this option are: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xp}} compare the structures pairwise
(p), i.e. first with 2nd, third with 4th etc.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xm}} calculate the distance matrix between all structures. The output is
formatted as a lower triangle matrix.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xf}} compare each structure to the first one.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xc}} compare continuously, that is i\sphinxhyphen{}th with (i+1)th structure.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapiro@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapiro}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapiro@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapiro}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAdos:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAdos:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAdos:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAduplex:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAduplex 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the structure upon hybridization of two RNA strands

\sphinxAtStartPar
reads two RNA sequences from stdin or \textless{}filename\textgreater{} and computes optimal and
suboptimal secondary structures for their hybridization. The calculation is
simplified by allowing only inter\sphinxhyphen{}molecular base pairs, for the general case
use RNAcofold.
The computed optimal and suboptimal structure are written to stdout, one
structure per line. Each line consist of: The structure in dot bracket format
with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} separating the two strands. The range of the structure in the two
sequences in the format  “from,to : from,to”; the energy of duplex structure
in kcal/mol.
The format is especially useful for computing the hybrid structure between a
small probe sequence and a long target sequence.

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAduplex:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAduplex:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAduplex:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the
first character is a “\sphinxhyphen{}” then AB will imply that AB and BA are allowed
pairs, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-nsp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp=}}}}}”\sphinxhyphen{}GA”  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAeval 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Determine the free energy of a (consensus) secondary structure for (an
alignment of) RNA sequence(s)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluates the free energy of a particular (consensus) secondary structure for
an (an alignment of) RNA molecule(s). The energy unit is kcal/mol and contains
a covariance pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}energy term for multiple sequence alignments ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-a}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}msa}}}}} option)
and corresponding consensus structures.
The program will continue to read new sequences and structures until a line
consisting of the single character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} or an end of file condition is
encountered.
If the input sequence or structure contains the separator character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} the
program calculates the energy of the co\sphinxhyphen{}folding of two RNA strands, where the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} marks the boundary between the two strands.

Using this flag indicates that the input is a multiple sequence alignment

allows one to specify a consensus structure. Therefore, this is the only

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=number\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads as computation cores are available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
sequence at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many sequences in the input in parallel. RNAeval will create
as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input sequences
of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this increases memory
consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory until an empty
compute slot is available and each running job requires its own dynamic
programming matrices.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-unordered}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not try to keep output in order with input while parallel processing is in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When parallel input processing ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}}}} flag) is enabled, the order in which
input is processed depends on the host machines job scheduler. Therefore, any
output to stdout or files generated by this program will most likely not
follow the order of the corresponding input data set. The default of RNAeval
is to use a specialized data structure to still keep the results output in
order with the input data. However, this comes with a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off in terms of
memory consumption, since all output must be kept in memory for as long as no
chunks of consecutive, ordered output are available. By setting this flag,
RNAeval will not buffer individual results but print them as soon as they
have been computated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAeval is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAeval ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-shapeMethod}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select SHAPE reactivity data incorporation strategy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE reactivities into pseudo
energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Convert by using the linear equation according to Deigan et al 2009.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Derived pseudo energy terms will be applied for every nucleotide involved in
a stacked pair. This method is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in the provided
parameter, i.e.: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting. The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}}
and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if necessary,
otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6. To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7,
use a parameter string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also
provide only one of the two parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Db\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}: Convert SHAPE reactivities to pseudo energies according to Zarringhalam

\sphinxAtStartPar
et al 2012. SHAPE reactivities will be converted to pairing probabilities by
using linear mapping. Aberration from the observed pairing probabilities will
be penalized during the folding recursion. The magnitude of the penalties can
affected by adjusting the factor beta (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Zb0.8”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}}: Apply a given vector of perturbation energies to unpaired nucleotides

\sphinxAtStartPar
according to Washietl et al 2012.Perturbation vectors can be calculated by
using RNApvmin.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-shapeConversion}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select method for SHAPE reactivity conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”O”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter is useful when dealing with the SHAPE incorporation according
to Zarringhalam et al. The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE
reactivities into the probability for a certain nucleotide to be unpaired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}: Use linear mapping according to Zarringhalam et al.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}: Use a cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}approach to divide into paired and unpaired nucleotides
(e.g. “C0.25”)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}: Skip the normalizing step since the input data already represents
probabilities for being unpaired rather than raw reactivity values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}: Use a linear model to convert the reactivity into a probability for
being unpaired (e.g. “Ls0.68i0.2” to use a slope of 0.68 and an intercept
of 0.2)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{O}}: Use a linear model to convert the log of the reactivity into a
probability for being unpaired (e.g. “Os1.6i\sphinxhyphen{}2.29” to use a slope of 1.6
and an intercept of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.29)

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding.
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the
first character is a “\sphinxhyphen{}” then AB will imply that AB and BA are allowed
pairs, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-nsp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp=}}}}}”\sphinxhyphen{}GA”  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAfold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate minimum free energy secondary structures and partition function of
RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads RNA sequences, calculates their minimum free energy (mfe)
structure and prints the mfe structure in bracket notation and its free energy.
If not specified differently using commandline arguments, input is accepted
from stdin or read from an input file, and output printed to stdout. If the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}
option was given it also computes the partition function (pf) and base pairing
probability matrix, and prints the free energy of the thermodynamic ensemble,
the frequency of the mfe structure in the ensemble, and the ensemble diversity
to stdout.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It also produces PostScript files with plots of the resulting secondary
structure graph and a “dot plot” of the base pairing matrix.
The dot plot shows a matrix of squares with area proportional to the pairing
probability in the upper right half, and one square for each pair in the
minimum free energy structure in the lower left half. For each pair i\sphinxhyphen{}j with
probability p\textgreater{}10E\sphinxhyphen{}6 there is a line of the form

\sphinxAtStartPar
i  j  sqrt(p)  ubox

\sphinxAtStartPar
in the PostScript file, so that the pair probabilities can be easily extracted.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sequences may be provided in a simple text format where each sequence occupies
a single line. Output files are named “rna.ps” and “dot.ps”. Existing files
of the same name will be overwritten.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is also possible to provide sequence data in FASTA format. In this case, the
first word of the FASTA header will be used as prefix for output file names.
PostScript files “prefix\_ss.ps” and “prefix\_dp.ps” are produced for the
structure and dot plot, respectively. Note, however, that once FASTA input was
provided all following sequences must be in FASTA format too.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To avoid problems with certain operating systems and/or file systems the prefix
will ALWAYS be sanitized! This step substitutes any special character in the
prefix by a filename delimiter. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option to change the
delimiting character according to your requirements.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program will continue to read new sequences until a line consisting of the
single character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} or an end of file (EOF) condition is encountered.

\subsubsection{I/O Options:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:i-o-options}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options for input and output (pre\sphinxhyphen{})processing
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}i@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}i}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}i@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}i}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-i}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-infile}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}i}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile}}\DUrole{p}{=}filename}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read a file instead of reading from stdin.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default behavior of RNAfold is to read input from stdin or the file(s)
that follow(s) the RNAfold command. Using this parameter the user can specify
input file names where data is read from. Note, that any additional files
supplied to RNAfold are still processed as well.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}o@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}o}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}o@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}o}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}outfile@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}outfile}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}outfile@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}outfile}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-o}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-outfile}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}o}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}outfile}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=filename\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Print output to file instead of stdout.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option may be used to write all output to output files rather than
printing to stdout. The default filename is “RNAfold\_output.fold” if no
FASTA header precedes the input sequences and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} feature is
inactive. Otherwise, output files with the scheme “prefix.fold” are
generated, where the “prefix” is taken from the sequence id, e.g. the FASTA
header. The user may specify a single output file name for all data generated
from the input by supplying a filename as argument following immediately
after this parameter.
In case a file with the same filename already exists, any output of the
program will be appended to it. Note: Any special characters in the filename
will be replaced by the filename delimiter, hence there is no way to pass an
entire directory path through this option (yet). (See also the
“\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-j}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-jobs}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=number\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads as computation cores are available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
sequence at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many sequences in the input in parallel. RNAfold will create
as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input sequences
of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this increases memory
consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory until an empty
compute slot is available and each running job requires its own dynamic
programming matrices.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-unordered}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not try to keep output in order with input while parallel processing is in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When parallel input processing ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}}}} flag) is enabled, the order in which
input is processed depends on the host machines job scheduler. Therefore, any
output to stdout or files generated by this program will most likely not
follow the order of the corresponding input data set. The default of RNAfold
is to use a specialized data structure to still keep the results output in
order with the input data. However, this comes with a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off in terms of
memory consumption, since all output must be kept in memory for as long as no
chunks of consecutive, ordered output are available. By setting this flag,
RNAfold will not buffer individual results but print them as soon as they
have been computated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}}}

Do not automatically substitute nucleotide “T” with “U”.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-auto-id}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAfold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAfold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequence will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:
“prefix\_xxxx\_ss.ps” (secondary structure plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp.ps”
(dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp2.ps” (stack probabilities), etc. where xxxx is
the sequence number. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiter between prefix and increasing number for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\_”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the default delimiter “\_” between the
prefix string and the increasing number for automatically generated ID.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}. This option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start}}\DUrole{p}{=}LONG}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the first number in automatically generated IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When sequence IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, usually starting with 1. Using this parameter, the first number can
be specified to the users requirements. Note: negative numbers are not
allowed.
Note: Setting this parameter implies to ignore any IDs retrieved from the
input data, i.e. it activates the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} flag.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-filename-delim}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-filename-full}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001\_ss.ps” for secondary structure
plots. With this flag set, no truncation of the output filenames is done,
i.e. output filenames receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note,
however, that invalid characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by
a delimiting character or simply removed, (see also the parameter option
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\end{fulllineitems}



\subsubsection{Algorithms:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:algorithms}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select additional algorithms which should be included in the calculations.
The Minimum free energy (MFE) and a structure representative are calculated
in any case.
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-p}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-partfunc}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=INT\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the partition function and base pairing probability matrix.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the MFE structure we print a coarse representation of the pair
probabilities in form of a pseudo bracket notation followed by the ensemble
free energy. This notation makes use of the letters \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{,}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\}}},
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} denoting bases that are essentially unpaired, weakly paired,
strongly paired without preference, weakly upstream (downstream) paired, or
strongly up\sphinxhyphen{} (down\sphinxhyphen{})stream paired bases, respectively. On the next line the
centroid structure as derived from the pair probabilities together with its
free energy and distance to the ensemble is shown. Finally it prints the
frequency of the mfe structure, and the structural diversity (mean distance
between the structures in the ensemble).
See the description of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_pf()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mean\_bp\_dist()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_centroid()}}
in the RNAlib documentation for details.
Note that unless you also specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}}, the partition function and mfe
calculations will use a slightly different energy model. See the discussion
of dangling end options below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An additionally passed value to this option changes the behavior of partition
function calculation:
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p0}} Calculate the partition function but not the pair probabilities, saving
about 50\% in runtime. This prints the ensemble free energy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG=\sphinxhyphen{}kT ln(Z)}}.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p2}} Compute stack probabilities, i.e. the probability that a pair \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i,j)}} and
the immediately interior pair \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i+1,j\sphinxhyphen{}1)}} are formed simultaneously in
addition to pair probabilities. A second postscript dot plot named
“name\_dp2.ps”, or “dot2.ps” (if the sequence does not have a name), is
produced that contains pair probabilities in the upper right half and stack
probabilities in the lower left.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-betaScale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\DUrole{p}{=}DOUBLE}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the scaling of the Boltzmann factors. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument provided with this option is used to scale the thermodynamic
temperature in the Boltzmann factors independently from the temperature of
the individual loop energy contributions. The Boltzmann factors then become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(\sphinxhyphen{} dG/(kT*betaScale))}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} is the Boltzmann constant, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG}} the free
energy contribution of the state and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} the absolute temperature.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}S@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}S}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-S}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-pfScale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}S}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}pfScale}}\DUrole{p}{=}DOUBLE}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the calculation of the pf use scale*mfe as an estimate for the ensemble free energy (used to avoid overflows).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.07”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default is 1.07, useful values are 1.0 to 1.2. Occasionally needed for
long sequences.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-MEA}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=gamma\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute MEA (maximum expected accuracy) structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The expected accuracy is computed from the pair probabilities: each base pair
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(i,j)}} receives a score \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{2*gamma*p\_ij}} and the score of an unpaired base is
given by the probability of not forming a pair. The parameter gamma tunes the
importance of correctly predicted pairs versus unpaired bases. Thus, for
small values of gamma the MEA structure will contain only pairs with very
high probability. Using {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-MEA}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}MEA}}}}} implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} for computing the pair
probabilities.

\end{fulllineitems}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-C}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-constraint}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=filename\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate structures subject to constraints. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=””)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads first the sequence, then a string containing constraints on
the structure encoded with the symbols:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}} (no constraint for this base)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}} (the corresponding base has to be paired

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} (the base is unpaired)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textgreater{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textless{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
and matching brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} (base i pairs base j)

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the exception of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, constraints will disallow all pairs conflicting
with the constraint. This is usually sufficient to enforce the constraint,
but occasionally a base may stay unpaired in spite of constraints. PF folding
ignores constraints of type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use constraints for multiple sequences. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually, constraints provided from input file only apply to a single input
sequence. Therefore, RNAfold will stop its computation and quit after the
first input sequence was processed. Using this switch, RNAfold processes
multiple input sequences and applies the same provided constraints to each of
them.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select SHAPE reactivity data incorporation strategy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE reactivities into pseudo
energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Convert by using the linear equation according to Deigan et al 2009.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Derived pseudo energy terms will be applied for every nucleotide involved in
a stacked pair. This method is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in the provided
parameter, i.e.: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting. The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}}
and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if necessary,
otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6. To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7,
use a parameter string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also
provide only one of the two parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Db\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}: Convert SHAPE reactivities to pseudo energies according to Zarringhalam

\sphinxAtStartPar
et al 2012. SHAPE reactivities will be converted to pairing probabilities by
using linear mapping. Aberration from the observed pairing probabilities will
be penalized during the folding recursion. The magnitude of the penalties can
affected by adjusting the factor beta (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Zb0.8”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}}: Apply a given vector of perturbation energies to unpaired nucleotides

\sphinxAtStartPar
according to Washietl et al 2012. Perturbation vectors can be calculated by
using RNApvmin.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-shapeConversion}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select method for SHAPE reactivity conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”O”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter is useful when dealing with the SHAPE incorporation according
to Zarringhalam et al. The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE
reactivities into the probability for a certain nucleotide to be unpaired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}: Use linear mapping according to Zarringhalam et al.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}: Use a cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}approach to divide into paired and unpaired nucleotides
(e.g. “C0.25”)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}: Skip the normalizing step since the input data already represents
probabilities for being unpaired rather than raw reactivity values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}: Use a linear model to convert the reactivity into a probability for
being unpaired (e.g. “Ls0.68i0.2” to use a slope of 0.68 and an intercept
of 0.2)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{O}}: Use a linear model to convert the log of the reactivity into a
probability for being unpaired (e.g. “Os1.6i\sphinxhyphen{}2.29” to use a slope of 1.6
and an intercept of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.29)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}motif@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}motif}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}motif@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}motif}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify stabilizing energy of a ligand binding

\sphinxAtStartPar
to a particular sequence/structure motif.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Some ligands binding to RNAs require and/or induce particular sequence and
structure motifs. For instance they bind to an interior loop, or small
hairpin loop. If for such cases a binding free energy is known, the binding
and therefore stabilizing effect of the ligand can be included in the folding
recursions. Interior loop motifs are specified as concatenations of 5\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} and 3\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}
motif, separated by an \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} character.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Energy contributions must be specified in kcal/mol.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the manpage for an example usage of this option.

\end{fulllineitems}

available corrections are performed. Otherwise, the user may limit the
modifications to a particular subset of modifications, resp. one\sphinxhyphen{}letter
codes, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}mP6}} will only correct for pseudouridine and m6A bases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently supported one\sphinxhyphen{}letter codes and energy corrections are:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}: 7\sphinxhyphen{}deaza\sphinxhyphen{}adenonsine (7DA)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{I}}: Inosine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}}: N6\sphinxhyphen{}methyladenosine (m6A)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}: Pseudouridine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}}: Purine (a.k.a. nebularine)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Dihydrouridine

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures

Produce structures without lonely pairs (helices of length 1).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

given 0 stacking energy.

\subsection{EXAMPLES}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Single line sequence input and calculation of partition function and MEA structure

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}MEA \PYGZhy{}d2 \PYGZhy{}p
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program will then prompt for sequence input. Using the example sequence
“CGACGTAGATGCTAGCTGACTCGATGC” and pressing ENTER the output of the program will be
similar to

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{CGACGUAGAUGCUAGCUGACUCGAUGC}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}
\PYG{n}{minimum} \PYG{n}{free} \PYG{n}{energy} \PYG{o}{=}  \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.90} \PYG{n}{kcal}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mol}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}
\PYG{n}{free} \PYG{n}{energy} \PYG{n}{of} \PYG{n}{ensemble} \PYG{o}{=}  \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.86} \PYG{n}{kcal}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{mol}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}  \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.80} \PYG{n}{d}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.81}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.90} \PYG{n}{MEA}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{22.32}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{n}{frequency} \PYG{n}{of} \PYG{n}{mfe} \PYG{n}{structure} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{ensemble} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.20997}\PYG{p}{;} \PYG{n}{ensemble} \PYG{n}{diversity} \PYG{l+m+mf}{4.19}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, the first line just repeats the sequence input. The second line contains a
MFE structure in dot bracket notation followed by the minimum free energy. After
this, the pairing probabilities for each nucleotide are shown in a pseudo dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket
notation followed by the free energy of ensemble. The next two lines show the centroid
structure with its free energy and its distance to the ensemble as well as the MEA structure,
its free energy and the maximum expected accuracy, respectively. The last line finally
contains the frequency of the MFE representative in the complete ensemble of secondary
structures and the ensemble diversity. For further details about the calculation and
interpretation of the given output refer to the reference manual of RNAlib.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since version 2.0 it is also possible to provide FASTA file sequence input. Assume
you have a file containing two sequences in FASTA format, e.g

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} cat sequences.fa
\PYGZgt{}seq1
CGGCUCGCAACAGACCUAUUAGUUUUACGUAAUAUUUG
GAACGAUCUAUAACACGACUUCACUCUU
\PYGZgt{}seq2
GAAUGACCCGAUAACCCCGUAAUAUUUGGAACGAUCUA
UAACACGACUUCACUCUU
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to compute the MFE for the two sequences the user can use the following
command

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZlt{} sequences.fa
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
which would result in an output like this

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{n}{seq1}
\PYG{n}{CGGCUCGCAACAGACCUAUUAGUUUUACGUAAUAUUUGGAACGAUCUAUAACACGACUUCACUCUU}
