\subsection{CONSTRAINT EXAMPLES}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:constraint-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Secondary structure constraints may be given in addition to the sequence information, too.
Using the first sequence of the previous example and restricting the nucleotides of the
outermost helix to be unpaired, i.e. base pairs (2,47) and (3,46) the input file should
have the following form

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} cat sequence\PYGZus{}unpaired.fa
\PYGZgt{}seq1
CGGCUCGCAACAGACCUAUUAGUUUUACGUAAUAUUUG
GAACGAUCUAUAACACGACUUCACUCUU
.xx...................................
.......xx...................
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calling RNAfold with the structure constraint option \sphinxhyphen{}C it shows the following result

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}C \PYGZlt{} sequence\PYGZus{}unpaired.fa
\PYGZgt{}seq1
CGGCUCGCAACAGACCUAUUAGUUUUACGUAAUAUUUGGAACGAUCUAUAACACGACUUCACUCUU
....(((...((((..(((((........)))))))))...)))...................... ( \PYGZhy{}4.20)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This represents the minimum free energy and a structure representative of the RNA
sequence given that nucleotides 2,3,46 and 47 must not be involved in any base pair.
For further information about constrained folding refer to the details of the \sphinxhyphen{}C option
and the reference manual of RNAlib.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Since version 2.2 the ViennaRNA Package distinguishes hard and soft constraints.
As a consequence, structure predictions are easily amenable to a versatile set of constraints,
such as maximal base pair span, incorporation of SHAPE reactivity data, and RNA\sphinxhyphen{}ligand binding
to hairpin, or interior loop motifs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Restricting the maximal span of a base pair}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A convenience commandline option allows you to easily limit the distance (j \sphinxhyphen{} i + 1) between
two nucleotides i and j that form a basepair. For instance a limit of 600nt can be accomplished
using:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}maxBPspan 600
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Guide structure prediction with SHAPE reactivity data}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use SHAPE reactivity data to guide secondary structure prediction:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}shape=reactivities.dat \PYGZlt{} sequence.fa
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where the file reactivities.dat is a two column text file with sequence positions (1\sphinxhyphen{}based)
and normalized reactivity values (usually between 0 and 2. Missing values may be left out,
or assigned a negative score:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} cat reactivities.dat
9    \PYGZhy{}999       \PYGZsh{} No reactivity information
10   \PYGZhy{}999
11   0.042816   \PYGZsh{} normalized SHAPE reactivity
12   0          \PYGZsh{} also a valid SHAPE reactivity
15   0.15027    \PYGZsh{} Missing data for pos. 13\PYGZhy{}14
...
42   0.16201
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note, that RNAfold will only process the first sequence in the input file, when provided
with SHAPE reactivity data!

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Complex structure constraints and grammar extensions}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Structure constraints beyond those that can be expressed with a pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}dot bracket notation
may be provided in a so\sphinxhyphen{}called command file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}commands=constraints.txt \PYGZlt{} sequence.fa
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The command file syntax is a generalization of constraints as used in
UNAfold/mfold. Each line starts with a one or two letter command followed
by command parameters. For structure constraints, this amounts to a single
command character followed by three or four numbers. In addition, optional
auxiliary modifier characters may be used to limit the constraint to specific
loop types. For base pair specific constraints,
we currently distinguish pairs in exterior loops (E), closing pairs of hairpin
loops (H), closing (I) and enclosed (i) pairs of interior loops, and closing (M)
and enclosed (m) pairs of multibranch loops. Nucleotide\sphinxhyphen{}wise constraints may be
limited to their loop context using the corresponding uppercase characters. The
default is to apply a constraint to all (A) loop types. Furthermore, pairing
constraints for single nucleotides may be limited to upstream (U), or downstream (D)
orientation. The command file specification is as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{F} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k}   \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{ORIENTATION}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Force nucleotides i...i+k\PYGZhy{}1 to be paired}
\PYG{n}{F} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k}   \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Force helix of size k starting with (i,j) to be formed}
\PYG{n}{P} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k}   \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Prohibit nucleotides i...i+k\PYGZhy{}1 to be paired}
\PYG{n}{P} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k}   \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Prohibit pairs (i,j),...,(i+k\PYGZhy{}1,j\PYGZhy{}k+1)}
\PYG{n}{P} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{l} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Prohibit pairing between two ranges}
\PYG{n}{C} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k}   \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{TYPE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nucleotides i,...,i+k\PYGZhy{}1 must appear in context TYPE}
\PYG{n}{C} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k}          \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Remove pairs conflicting with (i,j),...,(i+k\PYGZhy{}1,j\PYGZhy{}k+1)}
\PYG{n}{E} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{n}{e}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add pseudo\PYGZhy{}energy e to nucleotides i...i+k\PYGZhy{}1}
\PYG{n}{E} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{n}{e}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add pseudo\PYGZhy{}energy e to pairs (i,j),...,(i+k\PYGZhy{}1,j\PYGZhy{}k+1)}
\PYG{n}{UD} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{n}{e}    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{LOOP}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add ligand binding to unstructured domains with motif}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} m and binding free energy e}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} [LOOP]        = \PYGZob{} E, H, I, M, A \PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} [TYPE]        = [LOOP] + \PYGZob{} i, m \PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} [ORIENTATION] = \PYGZob{} U, D \PYGZcb{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Again, RNAfold by default only processes the first sequence in the input sequence
when provided with constraints in a command file. To apply the exact same constraints
to each of the input sequences in a multi FASTA file, use the batch mode commandline
option:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}constraint=constraints.txt \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}batch \PYGZlt{} sequences.fa
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ligand binding contributions to specific hairpin/interior loop motifs}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A convenience function allows one to specify a hairping/interior loop motif where a ligand
is binding with a particular binding free energy dG.
Here is an example that adds a theophylline binding motif. Free energy contribution of
this motif of dG=\sphinxhyphen{}9.22kcal/mol is derived from k\_d=0.32umol/l, taken from Jenison et al.
1994. Although the structure motif consists of a symmetric interior loop of size 6,
followed by a small helix of 3 basepairs, and a bulge of 3 nucleotides, the entire
structure can still be represented by one interior loop.
See the below mofif description where the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} character splits the motif into a 5’ and
a 3’ part. The first line gives the sequences motif, the second line shows the actual
structure motif of the aptamer pocket, and the third line is the interior loop motif
that fully encapsulates the theophylline aptamer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{GAUACCAG}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{n}{CCCUUGGCAGC}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To use the above information in the folding recursions of RNAfold, one only needs to
provide the motif itself, and binding free energy:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}motif=\PYGZdq{}GAUACCAG\PYGZam{}CCCUUGGCAGC,(...((((\PYGZam{})...)))...),\PYGZhy{}9.22\PYGZdq{} \PYGZlt{} sequences.fa
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Adding the \textendash{}verbose option to the above call of RNAfold also prints the sequence
position of each motif found in the MFE structure. In case interior\sphinxhyphen{}loop like motifs
are provided, two intervals are printed denoting the 5\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} and 3\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} part, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Ligand binding contributions to unpaired segments of the RNA structure}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The extension of the RNA folding grammar with unstructured domains allows for an easy
incorporation of ligands that bind to unpaired stretches of an RNA structure. To
model such interactions only two parameters are required: (i) a sequence motif in
IUPAC notation that specifies where the ligand binds to, and (ii) a binding free
energy that can be derived from the association/dissociation constant of the ligand.
With these two parameters in hand, the modification of RNAfold to include the competition
of regular intramolecular base pairing and ligand interaction is as easy as writing
a simple command file of the form:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{UD} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{n}{e}    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{LOOP}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
where m is the motif string in upper\sphinxhyphen{}case IUPAC notation, and e the binding free energy
in kcal/mol and optional loop type restriction {[}LOOP{]}. See also the command file specification as defined above.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For instance, having a protein with a 4\sphinxhyphen{}nucleotide footprint binding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AAAA}}, a
binding free energy e = \sphinxhyphen{}5.0 kcal/mol, and a binding restriction to exterior\sphinxhyphen{} and
multibranch loops results in a command file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} cat commands.txt
UD AAAA \PYGZhy{}5.0  ME
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
and the corresponding call to RNAfold to compute MFE and equilibrium probabilities becomes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}commands=commands.txt \PYGZhy{}p \PYGZlt{} sequence.fa
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The resulting MFE plot will be annotated to display the binding site(s) of the ligand,
and the base pair probability dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot is extended to include the probability that
a particular nucleotide is bound by the ligand.


\subsection{POST\sphinxhyphen{}TRANSCRIPTIONAL MODIFICATION EXAMPLES}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAfold:post-transcriptional-modification-examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Many RNA molecules harbor (post\sphinxhyphen{}transcriptional) modifications. These modified base
often change the pairing behavior or energy contribution for the loops they are part of.
To accommodate for that effect (to a certain degree) one may use additional correcting
energy parameters for loops with the respective modified bases. In literature, a few
stacking\sphinxhyphen{} and some terminal mismatch energies can be found. Some of them are already provided
within the ViennaRNA Package. The \textendash{}modification and \textendash{}mod\sphinxhyphen{}file command line parameters can be
used to apply these parameters in the predictions. While the former allows one to select a
subset of implemented modified base corrections, the latter enables the prediction programs
to read energy parameters for modified bases from a user\sphinxhyphen{}provided JSON file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Consider, for instance, the following tRNA sequence with dihydrouridines and pseudouridines
annotated by their respective one\sphinxhyphen{}letter codes D and P:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} cat tRNAphe.fa
\PYGZgt{}tRNAphe
GCCGAAAUAGCUCAGDDGGGAGAGCGPPAGACUGAAGAPCUAAAGGDCCCUGGUPCGAUCCCGGGUUUCGGCACCA
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Now, a prediction that includes support for the destabilizing effect of D and the stabilizing
effects of P within base pair stacks can be done as follows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYGZdl{} RNAfold \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}modifications=DP \PYGZlt{} tRNAphe.fa
\PYGZgt{}tRNAphe
GCCGAAAUAGCUCAGDDGGGAGAGCGPPAGACUGAAGAPCUAAAGGDCCCUGGUPCGAUCCCGGGUUUCGGCACCA
(((((((..((((........)))).(((((.......)))))....(((.((......)).)))))))))).... (\PYGZhy{}23.37)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{Synopsis}

RNAheat\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZlt{}input0\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}\PYGZlt{}input1\PYGZgt{}\PYG{o}{]}...

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAheat 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate specific heat of RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads RNA sequences from stdin or input files and calculates their specific
heat in the temperature range t1 to t2, from the partition function by numeric
differentiation. The result is written to stdout as a list of pairs of
temperature in C and specific heat in kcal/(mol*K).
The program will continue to read new sequences until a line consisting of the
single character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} or an end of file condition is encountered.
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}h@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}h}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}h@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}h}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}help@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}help}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}help@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}help}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\subsubsection{I/O Options:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:i-o-options}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options for input and output (pre\sphinxhyphen{})processing
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}i@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}i}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}i@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}i}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:cmdoption-i}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:cmdoption-infile}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}i}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}infile}}\DUrole{p}{=}filename}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read a file instead of reading from stdin

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default behavior of RNAheat is to read input from stdin or the file(s)
that follow(s) the RNAheat command. Using this parameter the user can specify
input file names where data is read from. Note, that any additional files
supplied to RNAheat are still processed as well.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:cmdoption-j}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:cmdoption-jobs}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=number\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads as computation cores are available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
sequence at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many sequences in the input in parallel. RNAheat will create
as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input sequences
of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this increases memory
consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory until an empty
compute slot is available and each running job requires its own dynamic
programming matrices.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:cmdoption-unordered}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not try to keep output in order with input while parallel processing is in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When parallel input processing ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}}}} flag) is enabled, the order in which
input is processed depends on the host machines job scheduler. Therefore, any
output to stdout or files generated by this program will most likely not
follow the order of the corresponding input data set. The default of RNAheat
is to use a specialized data structure to still keep the results output in
order with the input data. However, this comes with a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off in terms of
memory consumption, since all output must be kept in memory for as long as no
chunks of consecutive, ordered output are available. By setting this flag,
RNAheat will not buffer individual results but print them as soon as they
have been computated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not automatically substitute nucleotide “T” with “U”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAheat:cmdoption-auto-id}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAheat is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAheat ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequences’ FASTA id will be prefixed with the
provided string. FASTA ids then take the form “\textgreater{}prefix\_xxxx” where xxxx is
the sequence number. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiter between prefix and increasing number for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\_”)}

prefix string and the increasing number for automatically generated ID.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}. This option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

number, usually starting with 1. Using this parameter, the first number can

allowed.
Note: Setting this parameter implies to ignore any IDs retrieved from the

Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the
first character is a “\sphinxhyphen{}” then AB will imply that AB and BA are allowed
pairs, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-nsp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp=}}}}}”\sphinxhyphen{}GA”  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAinverse:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAinverse 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Find RNA sequences with given secondary structure

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program searches for sequences folding into a predefined structure, thereby
inverting the folding algorithm. Target structures (in bracket notation) and
starting sequences for the search are read alternately from stdin.
Characters in the start sequence other than “AUGC” (or the alphabet specified
with {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-a}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}}}}) will be treated as wild cards and replaced by a random character. Any
lower case characters in the start sequence will be kept fixed during the
search. If necessary, the sequence will be elongated to the length of the
structure. Thus a string of “N”s as well as a blank line specify a random
start sequence.
For each search the best sequence found and its Hamming distance to the start
sequence are printed to stdout. If the the search was unsuccessful, a structure
distance to the target is appended.
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Fp}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-R}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}R}}}}} options can modify the output format, see commandline options
below.
The program will continue to read new structures and sequences until a line
consisting of the single character “@” or an end of file condition is
encountered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”m”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In partition function mode, the probability of the target structure
exp(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}E\textasciigrave{}(S)/kT)/Q is maximized. This probability is written in brackets after
the found sequence and Hamming distance. In most cases you\textquotesingle{}ll want to use the
:option:}}\sphinxhyphen{}f\textasciigrave{} option in conjunction with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Fp}}, see below.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAinverse:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAinverse:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the
first character is a “\sphinxhyphen{}” then AB will imply that AB and BA are allowed
pairs.
e.g. RNAfold \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}nsp}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}GA}}  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNALalifold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate locally stable secondary structures for a set of aligned RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
reads aligned RNA sequences from stdin or file.aln and calculates locally
stable RNA secondary structure with a maximal base pair span. For a sequence of
length n and a base pair span of L the algorithm uses only O(n+L*L) memory and
O(n*L*L) CPU time. Thus it is practical to “scan” very large genomes for
short RNA
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
structures.
\end{quote}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}input\sphinxhyphen{}format}}\DUrole{p}{=}C|S|F|M}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
File format of the input multiple sequence alignment (MSA).

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, the input is considered to be in a particular file
format. Otherwise, the program tries to determine the file format
automatically, if an input file was provided in the set of parameters. In
case the input MSA is provided in interactive mode, or from a terminal (TTY),
the programs default is to assume CLUSTALW format.
Currently, the following formats are available: ClustalW (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}), Stockholm 1.0
(\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}), FASTA/Pearson (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F}}), and MAF (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}).

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aln}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=prefix\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Produce output alignments and secondary structure plots for each hit found.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option tells the program to produce, for each hit, a colored and
structure annotated (sub)alignment and secondary structure plot in PostScript
format. It also adds the subalignment hit into a multi\sphinxhyphen{}Stockholm formatted
file “RNALalifold\_results.stk”. The postscript output file names are
“aln\_start\_end.eps” and “ss\_start\_end.eps”. All files will be created in
the current directory. The optional argument string can be used to set a
specific prefix that is used to name the output files. The file names then
become “prefix\_aln\_start\_end.eps”, “prefix\_ss\_start\_end.eps”, and
“prefix.stk”. Note: Any special characters in the prefix will be replaced
by the filename delimiter, hence there is no way to pass an entire directory
path through this option yet. (See also the “\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aln\sphinxhyphen{}stk@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aln\sphinxhyphen{}stk}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aln\sphinxhyphen{}stk@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}aln\sphinxhyphen{}stk}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add hits to a multi\sphinxhyphen{}Stockholm formatted output file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”RNALalifold\_results”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default file name used for the output is “RNALalifold\_results.stk”.
Users may change the filename to “prefix.stk” by specifying the prefix as
optional argument. The file will be create in the current directory if it
does not already exist. In case the file already exists, output will be
appended to it. Note: Any special characters in the prefix will be replaced
by the filename delimiter, hence there is no way to pass an entire directory
path through this option yet. (See also the “\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split the free energy contributions into separate parts

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, only the total energy contribution for each hit is returned.
Using this option, this contribution is split into individual parts, i.e. the
Nearest Neighbor model energy, the covariance pseudo energy, and if
applicable, a remaining pseudo energy derived from special constraints, such
as probing signals like SHAPE.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each alignment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNALalifold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input alignment if the input file format allows to do that. Alignment IDs
are, for instance, usually given in Stockholm 1.0 formatted input. If this
flag is active, RNALalifold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and
automatically generates an ID for each alignment.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each alignment will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:

the alignment number beginning with the second alignment in the input. Use
this setting in conjunction with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-n}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}continuous\sphinxhyphen{}ids}}}}} flag to assign IDs

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use SHAPE reactivity data to guide structure predictions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple shapefiles for the individual sequences in the alignment may be
specified  as a comma separated list. An optional association of particular
shape files to a specific  sequence in the alignment can be expressed by
prepending the sequence number to the filename,  e.g.
“5=seq5.shape,3=seq3.shape” will assign the reactivity values from file
seq5.shape to  the fifth sequence in the alignment, and the values from file
seq3.shape to sequence 3. If  no assignment is specified, the reactivity
values are assigned to corresponding sequences in  the order they are given.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the method how to convert SHAPE reactivity data to pseudo energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, the only data conversion method available is that of to Deigan et
al 2009.  This method is the default and is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in
the provided parameter, i.e.:  {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting.
The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}} and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a  non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if
necessary. Otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6 as stated in the paper mentionen
before.  To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7, use a  parameter
string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also provide only one
of the two  parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or

\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Produce colored and structure annotated subalignment for each hit.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default file name used for the output is “aln\_start\_end.eps” where
“start” and “end” denote the first and last column of the subalignment
relative to the input (1\sphinxhyphen{}based). Users may change the filename to
“prefix\_aln\_start\_end.eps” by specifying the prefix as optional argument.
Files will be create in the current directory. Note: Any special characters
in the prefix will be replaced by the filename delimiter, hence there is no
way to pass an entire directory path through this option yet. (See also the
“\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNALfold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate locally stable secondary structures of RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute locally stable RNA secondary structure with a maximal base pair span.
For a sequence of length n and a base pair span of L the algorithm uses only
O(n+L*L) memory and O(n*L*L) CPU time. Thus it is practical to “scan” very
large genomes for short RNA structures.
Output consists of a list of secondary structure components of size \textless{}= L, one
entry per line. Each output line contains the predicted local structure its
energy in kcal/mol and the starting position of the local structure.

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}o}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}outfile}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=filename\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Print output to file instead of stdout.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option may be used to write all output to output files rather than
printing to stdout. The number of output files created for batch input
(multiple sequences) depends on three conditions: (i) In case an optional
filename is given as parameter argument, a single file with the specified
filename will be written into. If the optional argument is omitted, (ii)
FASTA input or an active {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} switch will write to multiple files that
follow the naming scheme “prefix.lfold”. Here, “prefix” is taken from the
sequence id as specified in the FASTA header. Lastly, (iii) single\sphinxhyphen{}line
sequence input without FASTA header will be written to a single file
“RNALfold\_output.lfold”. In case an output file already exists, any output
of the program will be appended to it.
Since the filename argument is optional, it must immediately follow the short
option flag to not be mistaken as new parameter to the program. For instance
\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\sphinxhyphen{}ornafold.out\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} will write to a file “rnafold.out”.
Note: Any special characters in the filename will be replaced by the filename
delimiter, hence there is no way to pass an entire directory path through
this option yet. (See also the “\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNALfold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNALfold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequence will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:
“prefix\_xxxx.lfold” where xxxx is the sequence number. Note: Setting this
parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}. This option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001\_ss.ps” for secondary structure
plots. With this flag set, no truncation of the output filenames is done,
i.e. output filenames receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note,
however, that invalid characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by
a delimiting character or simply removed, (see also the parameter option
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}L@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}L}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}L@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}L}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}span@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}span}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}span@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}span}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the maximum distance between any two pairing nucleotides.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”150”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option specifies the window length L and therefore the upper limit for
the distance between the bases i and j of any pair (i, j), i.e. (j \sphinxhyphen{} i + 1)
\textless{}= L.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}z@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}z}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}z@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}z}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-z}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-zscore}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}z}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=DOUBLE\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Limit the output to predictions with a Z\sphinxhyphen{}score below a threshold.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\sphinxhyphen{}2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option activates z\sphinxhyphen{}score regression using a trained SVM. Any predicted
structure that exceeds the specified threshold will be ommited from the
output.
Since the Z\sphinxhyphen{}score threshold is given as a negative number, it must
immediately preceed the short option to not be mistaken as a separate
argument, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}z\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.9 sets the threshold to a value of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.9

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-zscore-pre-filter}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apply the z\sphinxhyphen{}score filtering in the forward recursions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of z\sphinxhyphen{}score filtering considers the entire structure space to
decide whether or not a locally optimal structure at any position i is
reported or not. When using this post\sphinxhyphen{}filtering step, however, alternative
locally optimal structures

\sphinxAtStartPar
starting at i with higher energy but lower z\sphinxhyphen{}score can be easily missed. The

\sphinxAtStartPar
pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter

\sphinxAtStartPar
option restricts the structure space already in the forward recursions, such

\sphinxAtStartPar
that

\sphinxAtStartPar
only optimal solution among those candidates that satisfy the z\sphinxhyphen{}score

\sphinxAtStartPar
threshold are considered. Therefore, good results according to the z\sphinxhyphen{}score
threshold criterion are less likely to be superseded by results with better
energy but worse z\sphinxhyphen{}score. Note, that activating this switch results in higher
computation time which scales linear in the window length.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}report\sphinxhyphen{}subsumed@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}report\sphinxhyphen{}subsumed}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}report\sphinxhyphen{}subsumed@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}report\sphinxhyphen{}subsumed}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}report\sphinxhyphen{}subsumed}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Report subsumed structures if their z\sphinxhyphen{}score is less than that of the enclosing structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In default mode, RNALfold only reports locally optimal structures if they are
no constituents of another, larger structure with less free energy. In
z\sphinxhyphen{}score mode, however, such a larger structure may have a higher z\sphinxhyphen{}score,
thus may be less informative than the smaller substructure. Using this switch
activates reporting both, the smaller and the larger structure if the z\sphinxhyphen{}score
of the smaller is lower than that of the larger.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}b@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}b}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}b@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}b}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}backtrack\sphinxhyphen{}global@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}backtrack\sphinxhyphen{}global}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}backtrack\sphinxhyphen{}global@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}backtrack\sphinxhyphen{}global}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-b}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-backtrack-global}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}b}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}backtrack\sphinxhyphen{}global}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Backtrack a global MFE structure. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of just reporting the locally stable secondary structure a global MFE
structure can be constructed that only consists of locally optimal
substructures. This switch activates a post\sphinxhyphen{}processing step that takes the
locally optimal structures to generate the global MFE structure which
constitutes the MFE value reported in the last line. The respective global
MFE structure is printed just after the inut sequence part on the last line,
preceding the global MFE score.
Note, that this option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-o}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}o}}}}}/\textendash{}outfile since the locally optimal
structures must be read after the regular prediction step! Also note, that
using this option in combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-z}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}z}}}}}/\textendash{}zscore implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-zscore-pre-filter}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}zscore\sphinxhyphen{}pre\sphinxhyphen{}filter}}}}}
to ensure proper construction of the global MFE structure!

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select SHAPE reactivity data incorporation strategy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE reactivities into pseudo
energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Convert by using the linear equation according to Deigan et al 2009.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Derived pseudo energy terms will be applied for every nucleotide involved in
a stacked pair. This method is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in the provided
parameter, i.e.: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting. The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}}
and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if necessary,
otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6. To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7,
use a parameter string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also
provide only one of the two parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Db\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}: Convert SHAPE reactivities to pseudo energies according to Zarringhalam

\sphinxAtStartPar
et al 2012. SHAPE reactivities will be converted to pairing probabilities by
using linear mapping. Aberration from the observed pairing probabilities will
be penalized during the folding recursion. The magnitude of the penalties can
affected by adjusting the factor beta (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Zb0.8”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}}: Apply a given vector of perturbation energies to unpaired nucleotides

\sphinxAtStartPar
according to Washietl et al 2012. Perturbation vectors can be calculated by
using RNApvmin.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-shapeConversion}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select method for SHAPE reactivity conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”O”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter is useful when dealing with the SHAPE incorporation according
to Zarringhalam et al. The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE
reactivities into the probability for a certain nucleotide to be unpaired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}: Use linear mapping according to Zarringhalam et al.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}: Use a cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}approach to divide into paired and unpaired nucleotides
(e.g. “C0.25”)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}: Skip the normalizing step since the input data already represents
probabilities for being unpaired rather than raw reactivity values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}: Use a linear model to convert the reactivity into a probability for
being unpaired (e.g. “Ls0.68i0.2” to use a slope of 0.68 and an intercept
of 0.2)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{O}}: Use a linear model to convert the log of the reactivity into a
probability for being unpaired (e.g. “Os1.6i\sphinxhyphen{}2.29” to use a slope of 1.6
and an intercept of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.29)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}m@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}m}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}m@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}m}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-m}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-modifications}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}m}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=STRING\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow for modified bases within the RNA sequence string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”7I6P9D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat modified bases within the RNA sequence differently, i.e. use
corresponding energy corrections and/or pairing partner rules if available.
For that, the modified bases in the input sequence must be marked by their
corresponding one\sphinxhyphen{}letter code. If no additional arguments are supplied, all
available corrections are performed. Otherwise, the user may limit the
modifications to a particular subset of modifications, resp. one\sphinxhyphen{}letter
codes, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}mP6}} will only correct for pseudouridine and m6A bases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently supported one\sphinxhyphen{}letter codes and energy corrections are:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}: 7\sphinxhyphen{}deaza\sphinxhyphen{}adenonsine (7DA)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{I}}: Inosine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}}: N6\sphinxhyphen{}methyladenosine (m6A)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}: Pseudouridine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}}: Purine (a.k.a. nebularine)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Dihydrouridine

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}e@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}e}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}e@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}e}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}energyModel@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}energyModel}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}energyModel@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}energyModel}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNALfold:cmdoption-helical-rise}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}helical\sphinxhyphen{}rise}}\DUrole{p}{=}FLOAT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the helical rise of the helix in units of Angstrom.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2.8”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use with caution! This value will be re\sphinxhyphen{}set automatically to 3.4 in case DNA
parameters are loaded via {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-P}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}P}}}}} DNA and no further value is provided.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAmultifold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute secondary structures of multiple interacting RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program works much like RNAfold, but allows one to specify multiple RNA
sequences which are then allowed to form conncected components. RNA sequences
are read from stdin in the usual format, i.e. each line of input corresponds to
one sequence, except for lines starting with “\textgreater{}” which contain the name of
the next sequence(s).
Multiple strands must be concatenated using the \textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}\&\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{} character as separator.
RNAmultifold can compute MFE, partition function, corresponding ensemble free
energy and base pairing probabilities. These properties are either computed for
a particular arrangement (concatenation) of sequences, for the full ensemble of
the complex of input RNAs, or all complexes formed by the input sequences up to
a specified number of interacting sequences.
Output consists of a PostScript “dot plot” file containing the pair
probabilities, see the RNAfold man page for details.
The program will continue to read new sequences until a line consisting of the
single character \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{@}} or an end of file condition is encountered.

\subsubsection{I/O Options:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:i-o-options}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options for input and output (pre\sphinxhyphen{})processing
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}j@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}j}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-j}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-jobs}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}j}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=number\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads as computation cores are available.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
sequence pair at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many sequence pairs in the input in parallel. RNAmultifold
will create as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input
sequences of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this
increases memory consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory
until an empty compute slot is available and each running job requires its
own dynamic programming matrices.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-unordered}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}unordered}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Do not try to keep output in order with input while parallel processing is in place.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When parallel input processing ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAalifold:cmdoption-j}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}jobs}}}}} flag) is enabled, the order in which
input is processed depends on the host machines job scheduler. Therefore, any
output to stdout or files generated by this program will most likely not
follow the order of the corresponding input data set. The default of
RNAmultifold is to use a specialized data structure to still keep the results
output in order with the input data. However, this comes with a trade\sphinxhyphen{}off in
terms of memory consumption, since all output must be kept in memory for as
long as no chunks of consecutive, ordered output are available. By setting
this flag, RNAmultifold will not buffer individual results but print them as
soon as they have been computated.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noconv}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures

Do not automatically substitute nucleotide “T” with “U”.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-auto-id}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAmultifold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAmultifold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and
automatically generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix
and an increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to
the output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-id-prefix}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequence will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:
“prefix\_xxxx\_ss.ps” (secondary structure plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp.ps”
(dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp2.ps” (stack probabilities), etc. where xxxx is
the sequence number. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiter between prefix and increasing number for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\_”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the default delimiter “\_” between the
prefix string and the increasing number for automatically generated ID.

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-id-digits}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}digits}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}. This option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}start}}\DUrole{p}{=}LONG}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the first number in automatically generated IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When sequence IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, usually starting with 1. Using this parameter, the first number can
be specified to the users requirements. Note: negative numbers are not
allowed.
Note: Setting this parameter implies to ignore any IDs retrieved from the
input data, i.e. it activates the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} flag.
