\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-filename-full}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001\_ss.ps” for secondary structure
plots. With this flag set, no truncation of the output filenames is done,
i.e. output filenames receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note,
however, that invalid characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by
a delimiting character or simply removed, (see also the parameter option
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\end{fulllineitems}



\subsubsection{Algorithms:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:algorithms}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select additional algorithms which should be included in the calculations.
The Minimum free energy (MFE) and a structure representative are calculated
in any case.
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-p}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-partfunc}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}partfunc}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=INT\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the partition function and base pairing probability matrix in addition to the MFE structure. Default is calculation of mfe structure only.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In addition to the MFE structure we print a coarse representation of the pair
probabilities in form of a pseudo bracket notation, followed by the ensemble
free energy.
Note that unless you also specify \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}}, the partition function and mfe
calculations will use a slightly different energy model. See the discussion
of dangling end options below.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An additionally passed value to this option changes the behavior of partition
function calculation:

\sphinxAtStartPar
In order to calculate the partition function but not the pair probabilities

\sphinxAtStartPar
use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p0}} option and save about

\sphinxAtStartPar
50\% in runtime. This prints the ensemble free energy \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG=\sphinxhyphen{}kT ln(Z)}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}a@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}a@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}a}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}all\_pf}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the partition function and free energies not only for the complex formed by the input sequences (the “ABC… mutimer”), but also of all complexes formed by the input sequences up to the number of input sequences, e.g. AAA, AAB, ABB, BBB, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output will contain the free energies for each of these species. Using {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAcofold:cmdoption-a}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}a}}}}}
automatically switches on the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} option.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Start concentrations are read from stdin (unless the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}} option is used) in
{[}mol/l{]}, equilibrium concentrations are given realtive to the sum of the
inputs. An arbitrary number of initial concentrations can be specified (one

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the scaling of the Boltzmann factors. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument provided with this option is used to scale the thermodynamic
temperature in the Boltzmann factors independently from the temperature of
the individual loop energy contributions. The Boltzmann factors then become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(\sphinxhyphen{} dG/(kT*betaScale))}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} is the Boltzmann constant, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG}} the free
energy contribution of the state and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} the absolute temperature.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the calculation of the pf use scale*mfe as an estimate for the ensemble free energy (used to avoid overflows).

\sphinxAtStartPar

The default is 1.07, useful values are 1.0 to 1.2. Occasionally needed for
long sequences.

Set the threshold/cutoff for base pair probabilities included in the postscript output.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1e\sphinxhyphen{}5”)}

By setting the threshold the base pair probabilities that are included in the
output can be varied. By default only those exceeding \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1e\sphinxhyphen{}5}} in probability
will be shown as squares in the dot plot. Changing the threshold to any other

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAmultifold:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the
first character is a “\sphinxhyphen{}” then AB will imply that AB and BA are allowed
pairs, e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-nsp}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}nsp=}}}}}”\sphinxhyphen{}GA”  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApaln:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNApaln 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA alignment based on sequence base pairing propensities

\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses string\sphinxhyphen{}alignment techniques to perform fast pairwise structural alignments
of RNAs. Similar to RNApdist secondary structure is incorporated in an
approximate manner by computing base pair probabilities, which are then reduced
to a vector holding the probability that a base is paired upstream, downstream,
or remains unpaired. Such pair propsensity vectors can then be compared using
standard alignment algorithms. In contrast to RNApdist, RNApaln performs
similarity (instead of distance) alignments, considers both sequence and
structure information, and uses affine (rather than linear) gap costs. RNApaln
can perform semi\sphinxhyphen{}local alignments by using free end gaps, a true local
alignment mode is planned.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The same approach has since been used in the StraL program from Gerhard
Steeger’s group. Since StraL has optimized parameters and a multiple alignment
mode, it be be currently the better option.

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApaln:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNApaln:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNApaln:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

Allow other pairs in addition to the usual AU,GC,and GU pairs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Its argument is a comma separated list of additionally allowed pairs. If the
first character is a “\sphinxhyphen{}” then AB will imply that AB and BA are allowed
pairs.
e.g. RNAfold \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}nsp}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}GA}}  will allow GA and AG pairs. Nonstandard pairs are
given 0 stacking energy.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAparconv:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAparconv 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert energy parameter files from ViennaRNA 1.8.4 to 2.0 format

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts energy parameter files from “old” ViennaRNAPackage 1.8.4 format to
the new format used since ViennaRNAPackage 2.0.
The Program reads a valid energy parameter file or valid energy parameters from
stdin and prints the converted energy parameters to stdout or a specified
output file. Per default, the converted output file contains the whole set of
energy parameters used throughout ViennaRNAPackage 1.8.4. The user can specify
sets of energy parameters that should not be included in the output.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApdist:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNApdist 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate distances between thermodynamic RNA secondary structures ensembles

\sphinxAtStartPar
This program reads RNA sequences from stdin and calculates structure distances
between the thermodynamic ensembles of their secondary structures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To do this the partition function and matrix of base pairing probabilities is
computed for each sequence. The probability matrix is then condensed into a
vector holding for each base the probabilities of being unpaired, paired
upstream, or paired downstream, respectively. These profiles are compared
by a standard alignment algorithm.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The base pair probabilities are also saved as postscript “dot plots” (as in
RNAfold) in the files  “name\_dp.ps”, where name is the name of the sequence,
or a number if unnamed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the comparison directive. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”p”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Possible arguments for this option are: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xp}} compare the structures pairwise
(p), i.e. first with 2nd, third with 4th etc.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xm}} calculate the distance matrix between all structures. The output is
formatted as a lower triangle matrix.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xf}} compare each structure to the first one.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}Xc}} compare continuously, that is i\sphinxhyphen{}th with (i+1)th structure.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAPKplex:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAPKplex 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
predicts RNA secondary structures including pseudoknots

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes RNA secondary structures by first making two sequence intervals
accessible and unpaired using the algorithm of RNAplfold and then calculating
the energy of the interaction of those two intervals. The algorithm uses
O(n\textasciicircum{}2*w\textasciicircum{}4) CPU time and O(n*w\textasciicircum{}2) memory space.
The algorithm furthermore always considers dangle=2 model.

\sphinxAtStartPar
It  also  produces a PostScript file with a plot of the pseudoknot\sphinxhyphen{}free
secondary structure graph, in which the bases  forming  the  pseuodknot
are marked red.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sequences are read in a simple text format where each sequence occupies
a single line. Each sequence may be preceded by a line of the form
.. code:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{name}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
to assign a name to the sequence. If a name is given in the input, the
PostScript file “name.ps” is produced for the structure graph.  Other\sphinxhyphen{}
wise  the  file  name defaults to PKplex.ps. Existing files of the same
name will be overwritten.
The input format is similar to fasta except that  even  long  sequences
may  not  be  interrupted  by  line  breaks,  and  the header lines are
optional.  The program will continue to read new sequences until a line
consisting  of  the  single  character @ or an end of file condition is
encountered.

\sphinxAtStartPar
print suboptimal structures whose energy difference of the pseudoknot to the optimum pseudoknot is smaller than the given value.

\sphinxAtStartPar

pseudoknot interaction energy, the penalty for initiating a  pseudoknot and
the energy of the pseudoknot\sphinxhyphen{}free part of the structure. The {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAPKplex:cmdoption-s}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}s}}}}} option only
takes the pseudoknot interaction energy into account, so the final energy
differences may be bigger than the specified value \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=0.)}.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAplex:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAplex 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Find targets of a query RNA

\sphinxAtStartPar
reads two RNA sequences from stdin or \textless{}filename\textgreater{} and computes optimal and
suboptimal secondary structures for their hybridization. The calculation is
simplified by allowing only inter\sphinxhyphen{}molecular base pairs. Accessibility effects
can be estimated by RNAplex if a RNAplfold accessibility profile is provided.
The computed optimal and suboptimal structure are written to stdout, one
structure per line. Each line consist of: The structure in dot bracket format
with a “\&” separating the two strands. The range of the structure in the two
sequences in the format  “from,to : from,to”; the energy of duplex structure
in kcal/mol.
The format is especially useful for computing the hybrid structure between a
small probe sequence and a long target sequence.

Speedup of the target search \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option allows one to decide if the backtracking has to be done ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}} 0, {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}}
2) or not ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}} 1). For {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}} 0 the structure is computed based on the standard
energy model. This is the slowest and most precise mode of RNAplex. With {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}}
2, the structure is computed based on the approximated plex model. If a lot
of targets are returned this is can greatly improve the runtime of RNAplex.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}f}}}}} 1 is the fastest mode, as no structure are recomputed

\end{fulllineitems}

structure figure a la RNAfold with color\sphinxhyphen{}coded annotation of the
accessibilities is returned

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAplfold:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAplfold 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate locally stable secondary structure \sphinxhyphen{} pair probabilities

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes local pair probabilities for base pairs with a maximal span of L. The
probabilities are averaged over all windows of size L that contain the base
pair. For a sequence of length n and a window size of L the algorithm uses only
O(n+L*L) memory and O(n*L*L) CPU time. Thus it is practical to “scan” very
large genomes for short stable RNA structures.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Output consists of a dot plot in postscript file, where the averaged pair probabilities
can easily be parsed and visually inspected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxhyphen{}u option makes i possible to compute the probability that a stretch of x consequtive
nucleotides is unpaired, which is useful for predicting possible binding sites. Again
this probability is averaged over all windows containing the region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
.B WARNING! Output format changed!!

\sphinxAtStartPar
The output is a plain text matrix containing on each line a position i followed by the
probability that i is unpaired, {[}i\sphinxhyphen{}1..i{]} is unpaired {[}i\sphinxhyphen{}2..i{]} is unpaired and so on to
the probability that {[}i\sphinxhyphen{}x+1..i{]} is unpaired.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAplfold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAplfold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures

Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequences’ FASTA id will be prefixed with the
provided string. FASTA ids then take the form “\textgreater{}prefix\_xxxx” where xxxx is
the sequence number. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming
scheme: “prefix\_xxxx\_dp.ps” (dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_lunp” (unpaired
probabilities), etc. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001\_ss.ps” for secondary structure
plots. With this flag set, no truncation of the output filenames is done,
i.e. output filenames receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note,
however, that invalid characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by
a delimiting character or simply removed, (see also the parameter option
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the scaling of the Boltzmann factors. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument provided with this option is used to scale the thermodynamic
temperature in the Boltzmann factors independently from the temperature of
the individual loop energy contributions. The Boltzmann factors then become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(\sphinxhyphen{} dG/(kT*betaScale))}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} is the Boltzmann constant, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG}} the free
energy contribution of the state and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} the absolute temperature.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use SHAPE reactivity data to guide structure predictions.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAplfold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select SHAPE reactivity data incorporation strategy.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE reactivities into pseudo
energy contributions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Convert by using the linear equation according to Deigan et al 2009.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Derived pseudo energy terms will be applied for every nucleotide involved in
a stacked pair. This method is recognized by a capital \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} in the provided
parameter, i.e.: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”D” is the default setting. The slope \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}}
and the intercept \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{b}} can be set to a non\sphinxhyphen{}default value if necessary,
otherwise m=1.8 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.6. To alter these parameters, e.g. m=1.9 and b=\sphinxhyphen{}0.7,
use a parameter string like this: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9b\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”. You may also
provide only one of the two parameters like: {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Dm1.9” or
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Db\sphinxhyphen{}0.7”.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Z}}: Convert SHAPE reactivities to pseudo energies according to Zarringhalam

\sphinxAtStartPar
et al 2012. SHAPE reactivities will be converted to pairing probabilities by
using linear mapping. Aberration from the observed pairing probabilities will
be penalized during the folding recursion. The magnitude of the penalties can
affected by adjusting the factor beta (e.g. {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-shapeMethod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeMethod=}}}}}”Zb0.8”).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}}: Apply a given vector of perturbation energies to unpaired nucleotides

\sphinxAtStartPar
according to Washietl et al 2012. Perturbation vectors can be calculated by
using RNApvmin.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAplfold:cmdoption-shapeConversion}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\DUrole{p}{=}method}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select method for SHAPE reactivity conversion.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”O”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter is useful when dealing with the SHAPE incorporation according
to Zarringhalam et al. The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE
reactivities into the probability for a certain nucleotide to be unpaired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}: Use linear mapping according to Zarringhalam et al.
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}: Use a cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}approach to divide into paired and unpaired nucleotides
(e.g. “C0.25”)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}: Skip the normalizing step since the input data already represents
probabilities for being unpaired rather than raw reactivity values
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}: Use a linear model to convert the reactivity into a probability for
being unpaired (e.g. “Ls0.68i0.2” to use a slope of 0.68 and an intercept
of 0.2)
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{O}}: Use a linear model to convert the log of the reactivity into a
probability for being unpaired (e.g. “Os1.6i\sphinxhyphen{}2.29” to use a slope of 1.6
and an intercept of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.29)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}commands@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}commands}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}commands@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}commands}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}commands}}\DUrole{p}{=}filename}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Read additional commands from file

\sphinxAtStartPar
Commands include hard and soft constraints, but also structure motifs in
hairpin and interior loops that need to be treeted differently. Furthermore,
commands can be set for unstructured and structured domains.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}m}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}modifications}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=STRING\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Allow for modified bases within the RNA sequence string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”7I6P9D”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Treat modified bases within the RNA sequence differently, i.e. use
corresponding energy corrections and/or pairing partner rules if available.
For that, the modified bases in the input sequence must be marked by their
corresponding one\sphinxhyphen{}letter code. If no additional arguments are supplied, all
available corrections are performed. Otherwise, the user may limit the
modifications to a particular subset of modifications, resp. one\sphinxhyphen{}letter
codes, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}mP6}} will only correct for pseudouridine and m6A bases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently supported one\sphinxhyphen{}letter codes and energy corrections are:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{7}}: 7\sphinxhyphen{}deaza\sphinxhyphen{}adenonsine (7DA)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{I}}: Inosine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{6}}: N6\sphinxhyphen{}methyladenosine (m6A)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}}: Pseudouridine

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{9}}: Purine (a.k.a. nebularine)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}}: Dihydrouridine

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAplot:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAplot 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Draw RNA Secondary Structures

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads (aligned) RNA sequences and structures in the format as
produced by RNAfold or Stockholm 1.0 and produces drawings of the secondary
structure graph.
Coordinates for the structure graphs are produced using either E. Bruccoleri’s
naview routines, or a simple radial layout method.
For aligned sequences and consensus structures ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAeval:cmdoption-a}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}msa}}}}} option) the graph may be
annotated by covariance information. Additionally, a color\sphinxhyphen{}annotated EPS
alignment figure can be produced, similar to that obtained by RNAalifold and
RNALalifold.
If the sequence was preceded by a FASTA header, or if the multiple sequence
alignment contains an ID field, these IDs will be taken as names for the output
file(s): “name\_ss.ps” and “name\_aln.ps”. Otherwise “rna.ps” and
“aln.ps” will be used. This behavior may be over\sphinxhyphen{}ruled by explicitly setting

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Split batch input into jobs and start processing in parallel using multiple threads. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default processing of input data is performed in a serial fashion, i.e. one
sequence at a time. Using this switch, a user can instead start the
computation for many sequences in the input in parallel. RNAplot will create
as many parallel computation slots as specified and assigns input sequences
of the input file(s) to the available slots. Note, that this increases memory
consumption since input alignments have to be kept in memory until an empty
compute slot is available and each running job requires its own dynamic
programming matrices. A value of 0 indicates to use as many parallel threads
as computation cores are available.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Available formats are: PostScript (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{ps}}), Graph Meta Language (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{gml}}),
Scalable Vector Graphics (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{svg}}), and XRNA save file (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{xrna}}). Output
filenames will end in “.ps” “.gml” “.svg” “.ss”, respectively.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAfold is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAfold ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}prefix}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequence will be prefixed with the provided
string. Hence, the output files will obey the following naming scheme:
“prefix\_xxxx\_ss.ps” (secondary structure plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp.ps”
(dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot), “prefix\_xxxx\_dp2.ps” (stack probabilities), etc. where xxxx is
the sequence number. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

This parameter can be used to change the default delimiter “\_” between the
prefix string and the increasing number for automatically generated ID.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading
zeros, such that the number takes up a certain width. Using this parameter,
the width can be specified to the users need. We allow numbers in the range
{[}1:18{]}. This option implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

When sequence IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, usually starting with 1. Using this parameter, the first number can
be specified to the users requirements. Note: negative numbers are not
allowed.
Note: Setting this parameter implies to ignore any IDs retrieved from the
input data, i.e. it activates the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} flag.

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001\_ss.ps” for secondary structure
plots. With this flag set, no truncation of the output filenames is done,
i.e. output filenames receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note,
however, that invalid characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by
a delimiting character or simply removed, (see also the parameter option
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNApvmin 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate a perturbation vector that minimizes discripancies between predicted
and observed pairing probabilities

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads a RNA sequence from stdin and uses an iterative minimization
process to calculate a perturbation vector that minimizes the discripancies
between predicted pairing probabilites and observed pairing probabilities
(deduced from given shape reactivities). Experimental data is read from a given
SHAPE file and normalized to pairing probabilities. The experimental data has
to be provided in a multiline plain text file where each line has the format
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}position{]} {[}nucleotide{]} {[}absolute shape reactivity{]}}} (e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{3 A 0.7}}). The
objective function used for the minimization may be weighted by choosing
appropriate values for sigma and tau.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The minimization progress will be written to stderr. Once the minimization has
terminated, the obtained perturbation vector is written to stdout.

\subsubsection{Algorithms:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:algorithms}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Select additional algorithms which should be included in the calculations.
The Minimum free energy (MFE) and a structure representative are calculated
in any case.
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:cmdoption-shapeConversion}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}shapeConversion}}\DUrole{p}{=}STRING}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the method used to convert SHAPE reactivities to pairing probabilities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”O”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following methods can be used to convert SHAPE reactivities into the
probability for a certain nucleotide to be unpaired.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}}: Use linear mapping according to Zarringhalam et al. 2012

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}}: Use a cutoff\sphinxhyphen{}approach to divide into paired and unpaired nucleotides
(e.g. “C0.25”)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{S}}: Skip the normalizing step since the input data already represents
probabilities for being unpaired rather than raw reactivity values

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}: Use a linear model to convert the reactivity into a probability for
being unpaired (e.g. “Ls0.68i0.2” to use a slope of 0.68 and an intercept
of 0.2)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{O}}: Use a linear model to convert the log of the reactivity into a
probability for being unpaired (e.g. “Os1.6i\sphinxhyphen{}2.29” to use a slope of 1.6
and an intercept of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}2}}.29)

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tauSigmaRatio@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tauSigmaRatio}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tauSigmaRatio@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}tauSigmaRatio}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ratio of the weighting factors tau and sigma. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A high ratio will lead to a solution as close as possible to the experimental
data, while a low ratio will lead to results close to the thermodynamic
prediction without guiding pseudo energies.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}objectiveFunction@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}objectiveFunction}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}objectiveFunction@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}objectiveFunction}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}objectiveFunction}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
The energies of the perturbation vector and the discripancies between predicted and observed pairing probabilities contribute to the objective function. This parameter defines, which function is used to process the contributions before summing them up. 0 square 1 absolute.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sampleSize@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sampleSize}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sampleSize@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sampleSize}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sampleSize}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
The iterative minimization process requires to evaluate the gradient of the objective function.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1000”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A sample size of 0 leads to an analytical evaluation which scales as O(N\textasciicircum{}4).
Choosing a sample size \textgreater{}0 estimates the gradient by sampling the given number
of sequences from the ensemble, which is much faster.

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Specify the vector of initial pertubations. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”0”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Defines the initial perturbation vector which will be used as starting vector
for the minimization process. The value 0 results in a null vector. Every
other value x will be used to populate the initial vector with random numbers

“conjugate\_pr”, “vector\_bfgs”, “vector\_bfgs2”, “steepest\_descent”, “default” default=”default”)

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default option uses a custom implementation of the gradient descent
algorithms while all other options represent various algorithms implemented
in the GNU Scientific Library. When the GNU Scientific Library can not be
found, only the default minimizer is available.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Model Details:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:model-details}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Tweak the energy model and pairing rules additionally using the following
parameters
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}d@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}d}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:cmdoption-d}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:cmdoption-dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}dangles}}\DUrole{p}{=}INT}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
How to treat “dangling end” energies for bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”2”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} only unpaired bases can participate in at most one dangling end.
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} this check is ignored, dangling energies will be added for the bases
adjacent to a helix on both sides in any case; this is the default for mfe
and partition function folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}}).
The option \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d0}} ignores dangling ends altogether (mostly for debugging).
With \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} mfe folding will allow coaxial stacking of adjacent helices in
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops. At the moment the implementation will not allow coaxial stacking
of the two interior pairs in a loop of degree 3 and works only for mfe
folding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Note that with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}} only the MFE computations will be using this
setting while partition function uses \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d2}} setting, i.e. dangling ends will be
treated differently.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}noLP}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\subsection{EXAMPLES}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNApvmin:examples}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNApvmin acceptes a SHAPE file and a corresponding nucleotide sequence, which is read form stdin.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{RNApvmin} \PYG{n}{sequence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shape} \PYG{o}{\PYGZlt{}} \PYG{n}{sequence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{fasta} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{sequence}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{pv}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The normalized SHAPE reactivity data has to be stored in a text file, where each line contains the position
and the reactivity for a certain nucleotide ({[}position{]} {[}nucleotide{]} {[}SHAPE reactivity{]}).

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{l+m+mi}{1} \PYG{n}{A} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.286}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{2} \PYG{n}{U} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.383}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{3} \PYG{n}{C} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.033}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{4} \PYG{n}{C} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.017}
\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}
\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{o}{.}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{98} \PYG{n}{U} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.234}
\PYG{l+m+mi}{99} \PYG{n}{G} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.885}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The nucleotide information in the SHAPE file is optional and will be used to cross check the given input sequence if present.
If SHAPE reactivities could not be determined for every nucleotide, missing values can simply be omited.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The progress of the minimization will be printed to stderr. Once a solution was found, the calculated perturbation vector
will be print to stdout and can then further be used to constrain RNAfold’s MFE/partition function calculation by applying
the perturbation energies as soft constraints.

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsnoop:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAsnoop 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
Find targets of a query H/ACA snoRNA

\sphinxAtStartPar
reads a target RNA sequence and a H/ACA snoRNA sequence
from a target and query file, respectively and computes optimal
and suboptimal secondary structures for their hybridization. The
calculation can be done roughly in O(nm), where is n the length
of the target sequence and m is the length of the snoRNA stem, as it
is specially tailored to the special case of H/ACA snoRNA. For general
purpose target predictions, please have a look at RNAduplex, RNAup,
RNAcofold and RNAplex. Accessibility effects can be estimated by
RNAsnoop if a RNAplfold accessibility profile is provided.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The computed optimal and suboptimal structure are written to
stdout, one structure per line. Each line consist
of: The structure in dot bracket format with a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} separating the
two strands. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}\textgreater{}}} brackets represent snoRNA intramolecular
interactions, while the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{()}} brackets represent intermolecular
interactions between the snoRNA and its target.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The range of the structure in the two sequences in the format
“from,to : from,to”; the energy of duplex structure in
kcal/mol. If available the opening energy are also returned.

0 is the fastest mode, as no structure are recomputed and only the

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the stem structure subject to constraints.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads first the stem sequence, then a string containing
constraints on the structure encoded with the symbols:

\sphinxAtStartPar
. (no constraint for this base)

\begin{DUlineblock}{0em}
\item[] (the corresponding base has to be paired
\end{DUlineblock}

\sphinxAtStartPar
x (the base is unpaired)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\textless{} (base i is paired with a base j\textgreater{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{} (base i is paired with a base j\textless{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
and matching brackets ( ) (base i pairs base j)

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the exception of “|”, constraints will disallow all pairs conflicting
with the constraint. This is usually sufficient to enforce the constraint,
but occasionally a base may stay unpaired in spite of constraints. PF folding
ignores constraints of type “|”.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{DESCRIPTION}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:description}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAsubopt 2.6.4

\sphinxAtStartPar
calculate suboptimal secondary structures of RNAs

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads RNA sequences from stdin and (in the default {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}}}}} mode) calculates all
suboptimal secondary structures within a user defined energy range above the
minimum free energy (mfe). It prints the suboptimal structures in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket
notation followed by the energy in kcal/mol to stdout. Be careful, the number
of structures returned grows exponentially with both sequence length and energy
range.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, when used with the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} option, RNAsubopt produces Boltzmann
weighted samples of secondary structures.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Print output to file instead of stdout.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This option may be used to write all output to output files rather than
printing to stdout. The default filename is “RNAsubopt\_output.sub” if no
FASTA header precedes the input sequences and the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}} feature is
inactive. Otherwise, output files with the scheme “prefix.sub” are
generated, where the “prefix” is taken from the sequence id. The user may
specify a single output file name for all data generated from the input by
supplying an optional string as argument to this parameter. In case a file
with the same filename already exists, any output of the program will be
appended to it. Note: Any special characters in the filename will be replaced
by the filename delimiter, hence there is no way to pass an entire directory
path through this option yet. (See also the “\textendash{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim” parameter)

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically generate an ID for each sequence. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The default mode of RNAsubopt is to automatically determine an ID from the
input sequence data if the input file format allows to do that. Sequence IDs
are usually given in the FASTA header of input sequences. If this flag is
active, RNAsubopt ignores any IDs retrieved from the input and automatically
generates an ID for each sequence. This ID consists of a prefix and an
increasing number. This flag can also be used to add a FASTA header to the
output even if the input has none.

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Prefix for automatically generated IDs (as used in output file names).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”sequence”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If this parameter is set, each sequences’ FASTA id will be prefixed with the
provided string. FASTA ids then take the form “\textgreater{}prefix\_xxxx” where xxxx is
the sequence number. Note: Setting this parameter implies {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-auto-id}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}auto\sphinxhyphen{}id}}}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

Specify the number of digits of the counter in automatically generated alignment IDs.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”4”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When alignments IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing
number, starting with 1. This number will always be left\sphinxhyphen{}padded by leading

When sequence IDs are automatically generated, they receive an increasing

Note: Setting this parameter implies to ignore any IDs retrieved from the

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}\DUrole{p}{=}CHAR}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Change the delimiting character used in sanitized filenames.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”ID\sphinxhyphen{}delimiter”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to change the delimiting character used while
sanitizing filenames, i.e. replacing invalid characters. Note, that the
default delimiter ALWAYS is the first character of the “ID delimiter” as
supplied through the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-id-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}id\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}} option. If the delimiter is a whitespace
character or empty, invalid characters will be simply removed rather than
substituted. Currently, we regard the following characters as illegal for use
in filenames: backslash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textbackslash{}}}, slash \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{/}}, question mark \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{?}}, percent sign \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%}},
asterisk \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{*}}, colon \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{:}}, pipe symbol \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, double quote \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{"}}, triangular
brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-filename-full}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}full}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use full FASTA header to create filenames. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This parameter can be used to deactivate the default behavior of limiting
output filenames to the first word of the sequence ID. Consider the following
example: An input with FASTA header \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}NM\_0001 Homo Sapiens some gene}} usually
produces output files with the prefix “NM\_0001” without the additional data
available in the FASTA header, e.g. “NM\_0001.sub”. With this flag set, no
truncation of the output filenames is performed, i.e. output filenames
receive the full FASTA header data as prefixes. Note, however, that invalid
characters (such as whitespace) will be substituted by a delimiting character
or simply removed, (see also the parameter option {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-filename-delim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}filename\sphinxhyphen{}delim}}}}}).

\end{fulllineitems}



\subsubsection{Algorithms:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:algorithms}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute suboptimal structures with energy in a certain range of the optimum (kcal/mol).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default is calculation of mfe structure only.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deltaEnergyPost@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deltaEnergyPost}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deltaEnergyPost@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}deltaEnergyPost}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only print structures with energy within range of the mfe after post reevaluation of energies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Useful in conjunction with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}logML}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d1}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}d3}}: while the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}}}}} option specifies
the range before energies are re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluated, this option specifies the maximum
energy after re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluation.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}s@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}s}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}s@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}s}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sorted@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sorted}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sorted@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sorted}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-s}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-sorted}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}s}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sorted}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sort the suboptimal structures by energy and lexicographical order.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Structures are first sorted by energy in ascending order. Within groups of
the same energy, structures are then sorted in ascending in lexicographical
order of their dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-en-only}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}en\sphinxhyphen{}only}}}}} flag to deactivate
this second step. Note that sorting is done in memory, thus it can easily
lead to exhaution of RAM! This is especially true if the number of structures
produced becomes large or the RNA sequence is rather long. In such cases
better use an external sort method, such as UNIX “sort”.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}en\sphinxhyphen{}only@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}en\sphinxhyphen{}only}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}en\sphinxhyphen{}only@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}en\sphinxhyphen{}only}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-en-only}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}en\sphinxhyphen{}only}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only sort structures by free energy. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In combination with {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNAaliduplex:cmdoption-s}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}sorted}}}}}, this flag deactivates the second sorting
criteria and sorts structures solely by their free energy instead of
additionally sorting by lexicographic order in each energy band. This might
save some time during the sorting process in situations where lexicographic
order is not required.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}p@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}p}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomly draw structures according to their probability in the Boltzmann ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead of producing all suboptimals in an energy range, produce a random
sample of suboptimal structures, drawn with probabilities equal to their
Boltzmann weights via stochastic backtracking in the partition function. The
{\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNALalifold:cmdoption-e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{man/RNA2Dfold:cmdoption-p}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}p}}}}} options are mutually exclusive.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT\_en@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT\_en}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT\_en@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT\_en}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}stochBT\_en}}\DUrole{p}{=}number}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same as “\textendash{}stochBT” but also print free energies and probabilities of the backtraced structures.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}betaScale}}\DUrole{p}{=}DOUBLE}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the scaling of the Boltzmann factors. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”1.”)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The argument provided with this option is used to scale the thermodynamic
temperature in the Boltzmann factors independently from the temperature of
the individual loop energy contributions. The Boltzmann factors then become
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp(\sphinxhyphen{} dG/(kT*betaScale))}} where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k}} is the Boltzmann constant, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dG}} the free
energy contribution of the state and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{T}} the absolute temperature.

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Structure Constraints:}
\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:structure-constraints}}\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Command line options to interact with the structure constraints feature of
this program
\end{quote}
\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}maxBPspan}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Set the maximum base pair span.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=”\sphinxhyphen{}1”)}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}C@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}C@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}C}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-C}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-constraint}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}C}}\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}constraint}}\DUrole{p}{{[}}=filename\DUrole{p}{{]}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate structures subject to constraints. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=””)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The program reads first the sequence, then a string containing constraints on
the structure encoded with the symbols:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.}} (no constraint for this base)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}} (the corresponding base has to be paired

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{x}} (the base is unpaired)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textgreater{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}} (base i is paired with a base j\textless{}i)

\sphinxAtStartPar
and matching brackets \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(}} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{)}} (base i pairs base j)

\sphinxAtStartPar
With the exception of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}, constraints will disallow all pairs conflicting
with the constraint. This is usually sufficient to enforce the constraint,
but occasionally a base may stay unpaired in spite of constraints. PF folding
ignores constraints of type \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{|}}.

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{command line option@\spxentry{command line option}!\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}\index{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch@\spxentry{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}!command line option@\spxentry{command line option}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{man/RNAsubopt:cmdoption-batch}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}batch}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use constraints for multiple sequences. \sphinxstyleemphasis{(default=off)}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Usually, constraints provided from input file only apply to a single input
sequence. Therefore, RNAsubopt will stop its computation and quit after the
first input sequence was processed. Using this switch, RNAsubopt processes
multiple input sequences and applies the same provided constraints to each of
them.

\end{fulllineitems}
