\section{Command Files}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:command-files}}\label{\detokenize{io/commands::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The RNAlib and many programs of the ViennaRNA Package can parse and apply data from
so\sphinxhyphen{}called \sphinxstyleemphasis{command files}. These commands may refer to structure constraints or even
extensions of the RNA folding grammar (such as {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar:unstructured-domains}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Unstructured Domains}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Commands are given as a line of whitespace delimited data fields. The syntax we use
extends the constraint definitions used in the \sphinxhref{http://mfold.rna.albany.edu/?q=mfold}{mfold}
or \sphinxhref{http://mfold.rna.albany.edu/?q=DINAMelt/software}{UNAfold} software, where
each line begins with a command character followed by a set of positions.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, we introduce several new commands, and allow for an optional loop type context
specifier in form of a sequence of characters, and an orientation flag that enables one
to force a nucleotide to pair upstream, or downstream.


\subsection{Constraint commands}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:constraint-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The following set of commands is recognized:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F}} … Force

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{P}} … Prohibit

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} … Conflicts/Context dependency

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} … Allow (for non\sphinxhyphen{}canonical pairs)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{E}} … Soft constraints for unpaired position(s), or base pair(s)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{RNA folding grammar exensions}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:rna-folding-grammar-exensions}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{UD}} … Add ligand binding using the {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar:unstructured-domains}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Unstructured Domains}}}} feature

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Specification of the loop type context}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:specification-of-the-loop-type-context}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional loop type context specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}LOOP{]}}} may be a combination of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{E}} … Exterior loop

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{H}} … Hairpin loop

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{I}} … Internal/Interior loop

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}} … Multibranch loop

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} … All loops

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For structure constraints, we additionally allow one to address base pairs enclosed
by a particular kind of loop, which results in the specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} which consists
of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}LOOP{]}}} plus the following character:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i}} … enclosed pair of an Interior loop

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{m}} … enclosed pair of a Multibranch loop

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}LOOP{]}}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} flags are set, all contexts are considered
(equivalent to \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} ).


\subsection{Controlling the orientation of base pairing}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:controlling-the-orientation-of-base-pairing}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For particular nucleotides that are forced to pair, the following \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}ORIENTATION{]}}} flags
may be used:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{U}} … Upstream

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{D}} … Downstream

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If no \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}ORIENTATION{]}}} flag is set, both directions are considered.


\subsection{Sequence coordinates}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:sequence-coordinates}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sequence positions of nucleotides/base pairs are 1\sphinxhyphen{}based and consist of three
positions \(i\), \(j\), and \(k\). Alternativly, four positions may
be provided as a pair of two position ranges \([i:j]\), and \([k:l]\)
using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} sign as delimiter within each range, i.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{i\sphinxhyphen{}j}}, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{k\sphinxhyphen{}l}}.


\subsection{Valid constraint commands}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:valid-constraint-commands}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Below are resulting general cases that are considered \sphinxstyleemphasis{valid} constraints:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Forcing a range of nucleotide positions to be paired”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{F} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{ORIENTATION}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enforces the set of \(k\) consecutive nucleotides starting at
position \(i\) to be paired. The optional loop type specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}}
allows to force them to appear as closing/enclosed pairs of certain types of
loops.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Forcing a set of consecutive base pairs to form”}::

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{F} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enforces the base pairs \((i,j), \ldots, (i+(k-1), j-(k-1))\) to form.
The optional loop type specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} allows to specify in which loop
context the base pair must appear.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Prohibiting a range of nucleotide positions to be paired”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{P} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prohibit a set of \(k\) consecutive nucleotides to participate
in base pairing, i.e. make these positions unpaired. The optional loop type
specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} allows to force the nucleotides to appear within the
loop of specific types.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Probibiting a set of consecutive base pairs to form”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{P} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Probibit the base pairs \((i,j), \ldots, (i+(k-1), j-(k-1))\) to form.
The optional loop type specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} allows to specify the type of
loop they are disallowed to be the closing or an enclosed pair of.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Prohibiting two ranges of nucleotides to pair with each other”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{P} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{l} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Prohibit any nucleotide \(p \in [i:j]\) to pair with any other nucleotide
\(q \in [k:l]\). The optional loop type specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} allows to
specify the type of loop they are disallowed to be the closing or an enclosed pair of.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Enforce a loop context for a range of nucleotide positions”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{C} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enforces nucleotides to be unpaired similar to \sphinxstyleemphasis{prohibiting} nucleotides to be paired,
as described above. It too marks the corresponding nucleotides to be unpaired, however,
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} flag can be used to enforce specfic loop types the nucleotides must appear in.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Remove pairs that conflict with a set of consecutive base pairs”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{C} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove all base pairs that conflict with a set of consecutive base pairs
\((i,j), \ldots, (i+(k-1), j-(k-1))\). Two base pairs \((i,j)\) and
\((p,q)\) conflict with each other if \(i < p < j < q\), or
\(p < i < q < j\).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Allow a set of consecutive (non\sphinxhyphen{}canonical) base pairs to form”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{A} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{WHERE}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
This command enables the formation of the consecutive base pairs
\((i,j), \ldots, (i+(k-1), j-(k-1))\), no matter if they are \sphinxstyleemphasis{canonical},
or \sphinxstyleemphasis{non\sphinxhyphen{}canonical}. In contrast to the above \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{W}} commands, which remove
conflicting base pairs, the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{A}} command does not. Therefore, it may be used to
allow \sphinxstyleemphasis{non\sphinxhyphen{}canoncial} base pair interactions. Since the RNAlib does not contain
free energy contributions \(E_{ij}\) for non\sphinxhyphen{}canonical base pairs \((i,j)\),
they are scored as the \sphinxstyleemphasis{maximum} of similar, known contributions. In terms of a
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Nussinov} like scoring function the free energy of non\sphinxhyphen{}canonical base pairs is
therefore estimated as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}E_{ij} = \min \left[  \max_{(i,k) \in \{GC, CG, AU, UA, GU, UG\}} E_{ik}, \max_{(k,j) \in \{GC, CG, AU, UA, GU, UG\}} E_{kj} \right].\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The optional loop type specifier \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}WHERE{]}}} allows to specify in which loop
context the base pair may appear.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Apply pseudo free energy to a range of unpaired nucleotide positions”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{E} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{n}{e}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this command to apply a pseudo free energy of \(e\) to the set of \(k\)
consecutive nucleotides, starting at position \(i\). The pseudo free energy is
applied only if these nucleotides are considered unpaired in the recursions, or
evaluations, and is expected to be given in units of \(\text{kcal} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}\).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Apply pseudo free energy to a set of consecutive base pairs”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{E} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{n}{j} \PYG{n}{k} \PYG{n}{e}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this command to apply a pseudo free energy of \(e\) to the set of base pairs
\((i,j), \ldots, (i+(k-1), j-(k-1))\). Energies are expected to be given in
units of \(\text{kcal} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}\).

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Valid domain extensions commands}
\label{\detokenize{io/commands:valid-domain-extensions-commands}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{“Add ligand binding to unpaired motif (a.k.a. unstructured domains)”}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{UD} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{n}{e} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{LOOP}\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Description:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Add ligand binding to unpaired sequence motif \(m\) (given in IUPAC format,
capital letters) with binding energy \(e\) in particular loop type(s).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{UD}  \PYG{n}{AAA}   \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.0}    \PYG{n}{A}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The above example applies a binding free energy of \(-5\,\text{kcal} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}\)
for a motif \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AAA}} that may be present in all loop types.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Energy Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{io/parameters:energy-parameters}}\label{\detokenize{io/parameters::doc}}

\subsection{Modified Bases}
\label{\detokenize{io/parameters:modified-bases}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The functions {\hyperref[\detokenize{modified_bases:c.vrna_sc_mod}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_sc\_mod()}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{modified_bases:c.vrna_sc_mod_json}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_sc\_mod\_json()}}}}} and alike
implement an energy correction framework to account for modified bases in the
secondary structure predictions. To supply these functions with the energy
parameters and general specifications of the base modification, the following
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JSON}} data format may be used:

\sphinxAtStartPar
JSON data must consist of a header section \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{modified\_bases}} This header
is an object with the mandatory keys:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{name}} specifying a name of the modified base

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unmodified}} that consists of a single upper\sphinxhyphen{}case letter of the unmodified
version of this base,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{one\_letter\_code}} key to specify which letter is used for the modified
bases in the subsequent energy parameters, and

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
an array of \sphinxtitleref{pairing\_partners\textasciigrave{}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter must be uppercase characters. An optional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sources}} key may contain
an array of related publications, e.g. those the parameters have been derived from.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Next to the header may follow additional keys to specify the actual energy
contributions of the modified base in various loop contexts. All energy
contributions must be specified in free energies \(\Delta G\) in units of
\(\text{kcal} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}\). To allow for rescaling of the free
energies at temperatures that differ from the default (\(37^\circ C\)),
enthalpy parameters \(\Delta H\) may be specified as well. Those, however
are optional. The keys for free energy (at \(37^\circ C\)) and enthalpy
parameters have the suffixes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_energies}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_enthalpies}}, respectively.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parser and underlying framework currently supports the following
loop contexts:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{base pair stacks} (via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{stacking}} key prefix).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This key must point to an object with one key value pair for each
stacking interaction data is provided for. Here, the key consists
of four upper\sphinxhyphen{}case characters denoting the interacting bases, where
the the first two represent one strand in 5’ to 3’ direction and the
last two the opposite strand in 3’ to 5’ direction. The values
are energies in \(kcal \cdot mol^{-1}\).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{terminal mismatches} (via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mismatch}} key prefix).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This key points to an object with key value pairs for each mismatch
energy parameter that is available. Keys are 4 characters long
nucleotide one\sphinxhyphen{}letter codes as used in base pair stacks above.
The second and fourth character denote the two unpaired mismatching
bases, while the other two represent the closing base pair.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dangling ends} (via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dangle5}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{dangle3}} key prefixes).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The object behind these keys, again, consists of key value pairs
for each dangling end energy parameter. Keys are 3 characters long
where the first two represent the two nucleotides that form the
base pair, and the third is the unpaired base that either stacks
on the 3’ or 5’ end of the enclosed part of the base pair.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{terminal pairs} (via the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{terminal}} key prefix).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Terminal base pairs, such as AU or GU, sometimes receive an
additional energy penalty. The object behind this key may
list energy parameters to apply whenever particular base
pairs occur at the end of a helix. Each of those parameters
is specified as key value pair, where the key consists of
two upper\sphinxhyphen{}case characters denoting the terminal base pair.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Below is a JSON template specifying most of the possible input
parameters. Actual energy parameter files can be found in the
source code tarball within the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{misc/}} subdirectory.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}modified\PYGZus{}base\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}name\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}My modification (M)\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}sources\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}authors\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Author 1, Author 2\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}title\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}UV\PYGZhy{}melting of modified oligos\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}journal\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Some journal\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}year\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m+mi}{2022}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}doi\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}10.0000/000000\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{],}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}unmodified\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}G\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}pairing\PYGZus{}partners\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{[}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}U\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}A\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{],}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}one\PYGZus{}letter\PYGZus{}code\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}M\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}fallback\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}G\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}stacking\PYGZus{}energies\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}MAUU\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m+mf}{\PYGZhy{}1.2}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}AGMC\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{l+m+mf}{\PYGZhy{}2.73}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{},}
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n+nt}{\PYGZdq{}stacking\PYGZus{}enthalpies\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}

\sphinxstepscope


\chapter{Concepts and Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{api:concepts-and-algorithms}}\label{\detokenize{api::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Our library is grouped into several modules, each addressing different
aspects of RNA secondary structure related problems. This is an overview
of the concepts and algorithms for which implementations can be found
in this library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Almost all of them rely on the physics based Nearest Neighbor Model
for RNA secondary structure prediction.

\sphinxstepscope


\section{Free Energy Evaluation}
\label{\detokenize{eval:free-energy-evaluation}}\label{\detokenize{eval::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Secondary structures are decomposed into individual loops to eventually
evaluate their stability in terms of free energy. Here, we demonstrate
how this is done and which parts of the \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib} API are dedicated to
free energy evaluation.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsection{Energy Evaluation for Individual Loops}
\label{\detokenize{eval/eval_loops:energy-evaluation-for-individual-loops}}\label{\detokenize{eval/eval_loops::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To assess the free energy contribution of a particular loop \(L\) within a
secondary structure, two variants are provided
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{bare} free energy \(E_L\) (usually in units of deka\sphinxhyphen{}calories, i.e.
multiples of \(10 \text{cal} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}\), and

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{Boltzmann weight} \(q = exp(-\beta E_L)\) of the free energy \(E_L\)
(with \(\beta = \frac{1}{RT}\), gas constant \(R\) and temperature \(T\))

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The latter is usually required for partition function computations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluate the free energy of a base pair in the exterior loop. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evalue the free energy of a base pair connecting two nucleotides in the exterior loop and take hard constraints into account.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Typically, this is simply dangling end contributions of the adjacent nucleotides, potentially a terminal A\sphinxhyphen{}U mismatch penalty, and maybe some generic soft constraint contribution for that decomposition.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For dangles == 1 || 3 this function also evaluates the three additional pairs (i + 1, j), (i, j \sphinxhyphen{} 1), and (i + 1, j \sphinxhyphen{} 1) and returns the minimum for all four possibilities in total.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{j}} \textendash{} 3’ position of the base pair 

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the Energy of a hairpin\sphinxhyphen{}loop. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
To evaluate the free energy of a hairpin\sphinxhyphen{}loop, several parameters have to be known. A general hairpin\sphinxhyphen{}loop has this structure: where X\sphinxhyphen{}Y marks the closing pair {[}e.g. a \sphinxstylestrong{(G,C)} pair{]}. The length of this loop is 6 as there are six unpaired nucleotides (a1\sphinxhyphen{}a6) enclosed by (X,Y). The 5’ mismatching nucleotide is a1 while the 3’ mismatch is a6. The nucleotide sequence of this loop is “a1.a2.a3.a4.a5.a6” 

\sphinxAtStartPar


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1ga5fe3524fd6d2a297099238f117254c13}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{scale\_parameters()}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1ga8a69ca7d787e4fd6079914f5343a1f35}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_param\_t}}}}


\end{sphinxseealso}



\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter sequence should contain the sequence of the loop in capital letters of the nucleic acid alphabet if the loop size is below 7. This is useful for unusually stable tri\sphinxhyphen{}, tetra\sphinxhyphen{} and hexa\sphinxhyphen{}loops which are treated differently (based on experimental data) if they are tabulated.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\subsection{Energy Evaluation for Atomic Moves}
\label{\detokenize{eval/eval_move:energy-evaluation-for-atomic-moves}}\label{\detokenize{eval/eval_move::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions to evaluate the free energy change of a structure after application of
(a set of) atomic moves

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, atomic moves are not to be confused with moves of actual physical atoms. Instead,
an atomic move is considered the smallest conformational change a secondary structure
can undergo to form another, distinguishable structure. We currently support the
following moves
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Opening (dissociation) of a single base pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Closing (formation) of a single base pair

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Shifting one pairing partner of an existing pair to a different location

\end{itemize}

Calculate energy of a move (closing or opening of a base pair) 

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the parameters m1 and m2 are negative, it is deletion (opening) of a base pair, otherwise it is insertion (opening).

\subsection{Evaluation of Structures}
\label{\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:evaluation-of-structures}}\label{\detokenize{eval/eval_structures::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Several different functions to evaluate the free energy of a full secondary structure
under a particular set of parameters and the Nearest Neighbor Energy model are available
in \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For most of them, two different forms of representations for the secondary structure may
be used:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Dot\sphinxhyphen{}Bracket string

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A pair table representation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Furthermore, the evaluation functions are divided into \sphinxstylestrong{basic} and \sphinxstylestrong{simplified} variants,
where \sphinxstylestrong{basic} functions require the use of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:c.vrna_fold_compound_t}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}}} data structure
holding the sequence string, and model configuration (settings and parameters).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{simplified} functions, on the other hand, provide often used default model settings
that may be called directly with only sequence and structure data.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Finally, \sphinxstylestrong{verbose} variants exist for some functions that allow one to print the
(individual) free energy contributions to some \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FILE}} stream.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the pseudo energy derived by the covariance scores of a set of aligned sequences. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Consensus structure prediction is driven by covariance scores of base pairs in rows of the provided alignment. This function allows one to retrieve the total amount of this covariance pseudo energy scores. The {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:group__fold__compound_1ga1b0cef17fd40466cef5968eaeeff6166}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}} does not need to contain any DP matrices, but requires all most basic init values as one would get from a call like this:

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for detailed energy evaluation of a given sequence/structure pair. In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga06985672a4c73f0e56e1c5722e0aa88e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_structure()}}}} this function prints detailed energy contributions based on individual loops to a file handle. If NULL is passed as file handle, this function defaults to print to stdout. Any positive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verbosity\_level}} activates potential warning message of the energy evaluting functions, while values \( \ge 1 \) allow for detailed control of what data is printed. A negative parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verbosity\_level}} turns off printing all together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Model details, energy parameters, and possibly soft constraints are used as provided via the parameter ‘fc’. The fold\_compound does not need to contain any DP matrices, but all the most basic init values as one would get from a call like this: 
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures\sphinxstyleemphasis{\#include \textless{}ViennaRNA/eval.h\textgreater{}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the free energy of an already folded RNA and print contributions per loop. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for detailed energy evaluation of a given sequence/structure pair. In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga06985672a4c73f0e56e1c5722e0aa88e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_structure()}}}} this function prints detailed energy contributions based on individual loops to a file handle. If NULL is passed as file handle, this function defaults to print to stdout. Any positive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verbosity\_level}} activates potential warning message of the energy evaluting functions, while values \( \ge 1 \) allow for detailed control of what data is printed. A negative parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verbosity\_level}} turns off printing all together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga4078d8889e54c1f2e832f6c558399498}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_structure\_verbose()}}}} this function assumes default model details and default energy parameters in order to evaluate the free energy of the secondary structure. Threefore, it serves as a simple interface function for energy evaluation for situations where no changes on the energy model are required.

\sphinxAtStartPar

Calculate the free energy of an already folded RNA sequence alignment. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for energy evaluation for a given multiple sequence alignment and consensus structure pair. In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga06985672a4c73f0e56e1c5722e0aa88e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_structure()}}}} this function assumes default model details and default energy parameters in order to evaluate the free energy of the secondary structure. Therefore, it serves as a simple interface function for energy evaluation for situations where no changes on the energy model are required.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluate the free energy of a consensus structure for an RNA sequence alignment and print contributions per loop. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for detailed energy evaluation of a given sequence alignment/consensus structure pair. In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga7762c3a7bdcbc3a14ef93259d322c7d6}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_consensus\_structure\_simple()}}}} this function prints detailed energy contributions based on individual loops to a file handle. If NULL is passed as file handle, this function defaults to print to stdout. Any positive \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verbosity\_level}} activates potential warning message of the energy evaluting functions, while values \( \ge 1 \) allow for detailed control of what data is printed. A negative parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{verbosity\_level}} turns off printing all together.

\sphinxAtStartPar

Simply pass a sequence alignment as list of strings (including gaps) as first, and the consensus structure as second argument. The last two arguments are optional and default to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1gaf4afe19780b61b4962c613bde324128b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_VERBOSITY\_QUIET}}}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}}, respectively. \sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the free energy of an already folded RNA. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for energy evaluation of a given sequence/structure pair where the structure is provided in pair\_table format as obtained from {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/struct/pairtable:group__struct__utils__pair__table_1gab124ba58014a97d2fb8c21831e19f107}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_ptable()}}}}. Model details, energy parameters, and possibly soft constraints are used as provided via the parameter ‘fc’. The fold\_compound does not need to contain any DP matrices, but all the most basic init values as one would get from a call like this: 
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{fc}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{vrna\PYGZus{}fold\PYGZus{}compound}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{sequence}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{NULL}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{VRNA\PYGZus{}OPTION\PYGZus{}EVAL\PYGZus{}ONLY}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
 In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga9e8775770750783304d24fe0c4b15293}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_structure\_pt\_verbose()}}}} this function assumes default model details and default energy parameters in order to evaluate the free energy of the secondary structure. Threefore, it serves as a simple interface function for energy evaluation for situations where no changes on the energy model are required.

\subsection{Energy Parameters}
\label{\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:energy-parameters}}\label{\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For secondary structure free energy evaluation we usually utilize the set of
thermodynamic \sphinxstylestrong{Nearest Neighbor} energy parameters also used in other software,
such as \sphinxstyleemphasis{UNAfold} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAstructure}.

\sphinxstepscope


\subsubsection{Salt Corrections}
\label{\detokenize{eval/params/salt:salt-corrections}}\label{\detokenize{eval/params/salt::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
All relevant functions to compute salt correction at a given salt concentration and temperature.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The corrections for loop and stack are taken from Einert and Netz {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id51}{2011}{]}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
All corrections returned are in units of \(\text{dcal} \cdot \text{mol}^{-1}\).

\subsubsection{Converting Energy Parameter Files}
\label{\detokenize{eval/params/convert:converting-energy-parameter-files}}\label{\detokenize{eval/params/convert::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Converting energy parameter files into the latest format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To preserve some backward compatibility the RNAlib also provides
functions to convert energy parameter files from the format used
in version 1.4\sphinxhyphen{}1.8 into the new format used since version 2.0

\subsubsection{Available Parameter Sets}
\label{\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:available-parameter-sets}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
While the \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib} already contains a compiled\sphinxhyphen{}in set of the latest
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Turner 2004 Free Energy Parameters}, we defined a file format that allows to
change these parameters at runtime. The ViennaRNA Package already comes with
a set of parameter files containing
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Turner 1999 RNA parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mathews 1999 DNA parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Andronescu 2007 RNA parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mathews 2004 DNA parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Get a data structure containing prescaled free energy parameters already transformed to Boltzmann factors. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function returns a data structure that contains all necessary precomputed energy contributions for each type of loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1ga51839957423a01c8613f5a978b37a514}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_params()}}}}, the free energies within this data structure are stored as their Boltzmann factors, i.e.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\( exp(-E / kT) \)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where \( E \) is the free energy.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigstartmultiline
\pysiglinewithargsret{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1gac377cdd18c3a6da4e04683742fda3b7a}}\DUrole{kt}{void}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{vrna\_exp\_params\_rescale}}}}{{\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:c.vrna_fold_compound_t}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{n}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{*}\DUrole{n}{fc}\sphinxparamcomma \DUrole{kt}{double}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{*}\DUrole{n}{mfe}}{}
\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures\sphinxstyleemphasis{\#include \textless{}ViennaRNA/params/basic.h\textgreater{}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rescale Boltzmann factors for partition function computations. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function may be used to (automatically) rescale the Boltzmann factors used in partition function computations. Since partition functions over subsequences can easily become extremely large, the RNAlib internally rescales them to avoid numerical over\sphinxhyphen{} and/or underflow. Therefore, a proper scaling factor \(s\) needs to be chosen that in turn is then used to normalize the corresponding partition functions \(\hat{q}[i,j] = q[i,j] / s^{(j-i+1)}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function provides two ways to automatically adjust the scaling factor.\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\alph}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic guess

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic adjustment according to MFE

\end{enumerate}


\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} as second parameter activates the \sphinxstyleemphasis{automatic guess mode}. Here, the scaling factor is recomputed according to a mean free energy of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{184.3*length}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
cal for random sequences.

\sphinxAtStartPar
On the other hand, if the MFE for a sequence is known, it can be used to recompute a more robust scaling factor, since it represents the lowest free energy of the entire ensemble of structures, i.e. the highest Boltzmann factor. To activate this second mode of
\sphinxstyleemphasis{automatic adjustment according to MFE}, a pointer to the MFE value needs to be passed as second argument. This value is then taken to compute the scaling factor as \( s = exp((sfact * MFE) / kT / length )\), where sfact is an additional scaling weight located in the vrna\_md\_t data structure of \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp\_params}} in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fc}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The computed scaling factor \(s\) will be stored as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pf\_scale}} attribute of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp\_params}} data structure in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fc}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar


\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{{\hyperref[\detokenize{wrappers:wrappers_1_wrappers000132}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{SWIG Wrapper Notes:}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached to {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:structvrna__fc__s}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_fc\_s}}}} objects as overloaded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp\_params\_rescale()}} method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When no parameter is passed to this method, the resulting action is the same as passing \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{NULL}} as second parameter to {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1gac377cdd18c3a6da4e04683742fda3b7a}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_exp\_params\_rescale()}}}}, i.e. default scaling of the partition function. Passing an energy in kcal/mol, e.g. as retrieved by a previous call to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mfe()}} method, instructs all subsequent calls to scale the partition function accordingly. See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.exp_params_rescale}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.exp\_params\_rescale()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}. 


\end{fulllineitems}



\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1ga4abbca93defd54fa0dc797ceca36d2f0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_exp\_params\_subst()}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/model_details:group__model__details_1ga1f8a10e12a0a1915f2a4eff0b28ea17c}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_md\_t}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/energy_parameters:group__energy__parameters_1ga01d8b92fe734df8d79a6169482c7d8d8}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_exp\_param\_t}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:group__fold__compound_1ga1b0cef17fd40466cef5968eaeeff6166}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This recomputation only takes place if the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pf\_scale}} attribute of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{exp\_params}} data structure contained in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fc}} has a value below \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{1.0}}.

\pysigstopsignatures\sphinxstyleemphasis{\#include \textless{}ViennaRNA/loops/external.h\textgreater{}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the energy contribution of a stem branching off a loop\sphinxhyphen{}region. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function computes the energy contribution of a stem that branches off a loop region. This can be the case in multiloops, when a stem branching off increases the degree of the loop but also \sphinxstyleemphasis{immediately interior base pairs} of an exterior loop contribute free energy. To switch the behavior of the function according to the evaluation of a multiloop\sphinxhyphen{} or exterior\sphinxhyphen{}loop\sphinxhyphen{}stem, you pass the flag ‘extLoop’. The returned energy contribution consists of a TerminalAU penalty if the pair type is greater than 2, dangling end contributions of mismatching nucleotides adjacent to the stem if only one of the si1, sj1 parameters is greater than 0 and mismatch energies if both mismatching nucleotides are positive values. Thus, to avoid incorporating dangling end or mismatch energies just pass a negative number, e.g. \sphinxhyphen{}1 to the mismatch argument.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is an illustration of how the energy contribution is assembled: 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, (X,Y) is the base pair that closes the stem that branches off a loop region. The nucleotides si1 and sj1 are the 5’\sphinxhyphen{} and 3’\sphinxhyphen{} mismatches, respectively. If the base pair type of (X,Y) is greater than 2 (i.e. an A\sphinxhyphen{}U or G\sphinxhyphen{}U pair, the TerminalAU penalty will be included in the energy contribution returned. If si1 and sj1 are both nonnegative numbers, mismatch energies will also be included. If one of si1 or sj1 is a negative value, only 5’ or 3’ dangling end contributions are taken into account. To prohibit any of these mismatch contributions to be incorporated, just pass a negative number to both, si1 and sj1. In case the argument extLoop is 0, the returned energy contribution also includes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{internal\sphinxhyphen{}loop\sphinxhyphen{}penalty} of a multiloop stem with closing pair type.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Compute the Energy of an interior\sphinxhyphen{}loop}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function computes the free energy \(\Delta G\) of an interior\sphinxhyphen{}loop with the following structure:  This general structure depicts an interior\sphinxhyphen{}loop that is closed by the base pair (X,Y). The enclosed base pair is (V,U) which leaves the unpaired bases a\_1\sphinxhyphen{}a\_n and b\_1\sphinxhyphen{}b\_n that constitute the loop. In this example, the length of the interior\sphinxhyphen{}loop is \((n+m)\)
\sphinxAtStartPar
where n or m may be 0 resulting in a bulge\sphinxhyphen{}loop or base pair stack. The mismatching nucleotides for the closing pair (X,Y) are:

\sphinxAtStartPar
5’\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch: a\_1

\sphinxAtStartPar
3’\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch: b\_m

\sphinxAtStartPar
and for the enclosed base pair (V,U):

\sphinxAtStartPar
5’\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch: b\_1

\sphinxAtStartPar
3’\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch: a\_n


\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsection{Loop Decomposition}
\label{\detokenize{eval:loop-decomposition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each base pair in a secondary structure closes a loop, thereby directly
enclosing unpaired nucleotides, and/or further base pairs. Our implementation
distinguishes four basic types of loops:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
hairpin loops

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
interior loops

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
multibranch loops

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
exterior loop

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
While the exterior loop is a special case without a closing pair, the other
loops are determined by the number of base pairs involved in the loop formation,
i.e. hairpin loops are 1\sphinxhyphen{}loops, since only a single base pair delimits the loop.
interior loops are 2\sphinxhyphen{}loops due to their enclosing, and enclosed base pair. All
loops where more than two base pairs are involved, are termed multibranch loops.

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{loop_types}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Any secondary structure can be decomposed into its loops. Each of the loops then
can be scored in terms of free energy, and the free energy of an entire secondary
structure is simply the sum of free energies of its loops.

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{loop_decomposition}.png}

Reset the global default model details to a specific set of parameters, or their initial values. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function resets the global default model details to their initial values, i.e. as specified by the ViennaRNA Package release, upon passing NULL as argument. Alternatively it resets them according to a set of provided parameters.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{sphinxseealso}



\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The global default parameters affect all function calls of RNAlib where model details are not explicitly provided. Hence, any change of them is not considered threadsafe
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function first resets the global default settings to factory defaults, and only then applies user provided settings (if any). User settings that do not meet specifications are skipped.

\index{pf\_scale (C var)@\spxentry{pf\_scale}\spxextra{C var}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/model_details:c.pf_scale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigstartmultiline
\pysigline{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/model_details:group__model__details_1gad3b22044065acc6dee0af68931b52cfd}}\DUrole{kt}{double}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{pf\_scale}}}}
\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
A scaling factor used by {\hyperref[\detokenize{partfunc/global_deprecated:group__part__func__global__deprecated_1gadc3db3d98742427e7001a7fd36ef28c2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{pf\_fold()}}}} to avoid overflows. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Should be set to approximately \(exp{((-F/kT)/length)}\), where \(F\) is an estimate for the ensemble free energy, for example the minimum free energy. You must call {\hyperref[\detokenize{partfunc/global_deprecated:group__part__func__global__deprecated_1ga384e927890f9c034ff09fa66da102d28}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{update\_pf\_params()}}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
after changing this parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If pf\_scale is \sphinxhyphen{}1 (the default) , an estimate will be provided automatically when computing partition functions, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{partfunc/global_deprecated:group__part__func__global__deprecated_1gadc3db3d98742427e7001a7fd36ef28c2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{pf\_fold()}}}} The automatic estimate is usually insufficient for sequences more than a few hundred bases long. 

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{dangles (C var)@\spxentry{dangles}\spxextra{C var}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/model_details:c.dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigstartmultiline
\pysigline{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/model_details:group__model__details_1ga72b511ed1201f7e23ec437e468790d74}}\DUrole{kt}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{dangles}}}}
\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Switch the energy model for dangling end contributions (0, 1, 2, 3) 

\sphinxAtStartPar
If set to 0 no stabilizing energies are assigned to bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multiloops (so called dangling ends). Normally (dangles = 1) dangling end energies are assigned only to unpaired bases and a base cannot participate simultaneously in two dangling ends. In the partition function algorithm {\hyperref[\detokenize{partfunc/global_deprecated:group__part__func__global__deprecated_1gadc3db3d98742427e7001a7fd36ef28c2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{pf\_fold()}}}} these checks are neglected. If {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/model_details:group__model__details_1ga72b511ed1201f7e23ec437e468790d74}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{dangles}}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
is set to 2, all folding routines will follow this convention. This treatment of dangling ends gives more favorable energies to helices directly adjacent to one another, which can be beneficial since such helices often do engage in stabilizing interactions through co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If dangles = 3 co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking is explicitly included for adjacent helices in multiloops. The option affects only mfe folding and energy evaluation (
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mfe/global_deprecated:group__mfe__global__deprecated_1gaadafcb0f140795ae62e5ca027e335a9b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{fold()}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_deprecated:group__eval__deprecated_1gaf93986cb3cb29770ec9cca69c9fab8cf}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{energy\_of\_structure()}}}}), as well as suboptimal folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{subopt/wuchty:group__subopt__wuchty_1ga9913b3a58b8d315be3f4f7f4dbe3c481}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{subopt()}}}}) via re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluation of energies. Co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking with one intervening mismatch is not considered so far.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Default is 2 in most algorithms, partition function algorithms can only handle 0 and 2 

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{vrna\_md\_s.dangles (C var)@\spxentry{vrna\_md\_s.dangles}\spxextra{C var}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/model_details:c.vrna_md_s.dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigstartmultiline
\pysigline{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/model_details:structvrna__md__s_1adcda4ff2ea77748ae0e8700288282efc}}\DUrole{kt}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{dangles}}}}
\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifies the dangle model used in any energy evaluation (0,1,2 or 3) 

\sphinxAtStartPar
If set to 0 no stabilizing energies are assigned to bases adjacent to helices in free ends and multiloops (so called dangling ends). Normally (dangles = 1) dangling end energies are assigned only to unpaired bases and a base cannot participate simultaneously in two dangling ends. In the partition function algorithm {\hyperref[\detokenize{partfunc/global:group__part__func__global_1gaff6fe7a499a62d62d10cb850d5222f00}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_pf()}}}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
these checks are neglected. To provide comparability between free energy minimization and partition function algorithms, the default setting is 2. This treatment of dangling ends gives more favorable energies to helices directly adjacent to one another, which can be beneficial since such helices often do engage in stabilizing interactions through co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If set to 3 co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking is explicitly included for adjacent helices in multiloops. The option affects only mfe folding and energy evaluation (
{\hyperref[\detokenize{mfe/global:group__mfe__global_1ga5577af664e5b9056b44fa5df29e9befb}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_mfe()}}}} and {\hyperref[\detokenize{eval/eval_structures:group__eval_1ga06985672a4c73f0e56e1c5722e0aa88e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_eval\_structure()}}}}), as well as suboptimal folding ({\hyperref[\detokenize{subopt/wuchty:group__subopt__wuchty_1gad0cce16455fda0737873d8e1c5846480}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_subopt()}}}}) via re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluation of energies. Co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking with one intervening mismatch is not considered so far. Note, that some function do not implement all dangle model but only a subset of (0,1,2,3). In particular, partition function algorithms can only handle 0 and 2. Read the documentation of the particular recurrences or energy evaluation function for information about the provided dangle model. 

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsection{Unstructured Domains}
\label{\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:unstructured-domains}}\label{\detokenize{grammar/domains_up::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add and modify unstructured domains to the RNA folding grammar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides the tools to add and modify unstructured domains to the production rules of the RNA folding grammar.
Usually this functionality is utilized for incorporating ligand binding to unpaired stretches of an RNA.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Although the additional production rule(s) for unstructured domains as descibed in {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar:unstructured-domains}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Unstructured Domains}}}}
are always treated as \sphinxstyleemphasis{segments possibly bound to one or more ligands}, the current implementation requires
that at least one ligand is bound. The default implementation already takes care of the required changes,
however, upon using callback functions other than the default ones, one has to take care of this fact.
Please also note, that this behavior might change in one of the next releases, such that the decomposition
schemes as shown above comply with the actual implementation.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A default implementation allows one to readily use this feature by simply adding sequence motifs and corresponding
binding free energies with the function {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:c.vrna_ud_add_motif}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_ud\_add\_motif()}}}}} (see also {\hyperref[\detokenize{ligands/unstructured_domains::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Ligands Binding to Unstructured Domains}}}}).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The grammar extension is realized using a callback function that
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
evaluates the binding free energy of a ligand to its target sequence segment (white boxes in the figures above), or

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
returns the free energy of an unpaired stretch possibly bound by a ligand, stored in the additional \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{U}} DP matrix.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback is passed the segment positions, the loop context, and which of the two above mentioned
evaluations are required. A second callback implements the pre\sphinxhyphen{}processing step that
prepares the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{U}} DP matrix by evaluating all possible cases of the additional production rule.
Both callbacks have a default implementation in \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib}, but may be over\sphinxhyphen{}written by a
user\sphinxhyphen{}implementation, making it fully user\sphinxhyphen{}customizable.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For equilibrium probability computations, two additional callbacks exist. One to store/add and one to retrieve the
probability of unstructured domains at particular positions. Our implementation already takes care of computing
the probabilities, but users of the unstructured domain feature are required to provide a mechanism to efficiently
store/add the corresponding values into some external data structure.

Detect unstructured domains in centroid structure. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Given a centroid structure and a set of unstructured domains compute the list of unstructured domain motifs present in the centroid. Since we do not explicitly annotate unstructured domain motifs in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket strings, this function can be used to check for the presence and location of unstructured domain motifs under the assumption that the dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket string is the centroid structure of the equiibrium ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function adds a ligand binding motif and the associated binding free energy to the {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:group__domains__up_1ga0009117b14d29143e8b18ab891f48c2d}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_ud\_t}}}} attribute of a {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:group__fold__compound_1ga1b0cef17fd40466cef5968eaeeff6166}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}}. \pysigstopsignatures\sphinxstyleemphasis{\#include \textless{}ViennaRNA/unstructured\_domains.h\textgreater{}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Attach production rule callbacks for free energies computations. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this function to bind a user\sphinxhyphen{}implemented grammar extension for unstructured domains.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{e\_cb}} needs to evaluate the free energy contribution \(f(i,j)\) of the unpaired segment \([i,j]\). It will be executed in each of the regular secondary structure production rules. Whenever the callback is passed the {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:group__domains__up_1gaab12b58d59be76446a9f76fad2fe624c}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_MOTIF}}}} flag via its \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{loop\_type}} parameter the contribution of any ligand that consecutively binds from position \(i\) to \(j\) (the white box) is requested. Otherwise, the callback usually performs a lookup in the precomputed \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}} matrices. Which \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{B}} matrix is addressed will be indicated by the flags {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:group__domains__up_1gaac911374e86236a51bfd42e1f098eaba}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_EXT\_LOOP}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:group__domains__up_1ga23b610ea9564346c45cc1e2bbb62adf7}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_HP\_LOOP}}}} {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:group__domains__up_1gac4a0feccd9654c149203200248c2716b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_INT\_LOOP}}}}, and {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:group__domains__up_1ga67b80796655e5227a4ed662bfbe398b0}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_MB\_LOOP}}}}. As their names already imply, they specify exterior loops (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{F}} production rule), hairpin loops and interior loops (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{C}} production rule), and multibranch loops (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{M1}} production rule).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxincludegraphics{{ligands_up_callback}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pre\_cb}} callback will be executed as a pre\sphinxhyphen{}processing step right before the regular secondary structure rules. Usually one would use this callback to fill the dynamic programming matrices \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{U}} and preparations of the auxiliary data structure {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/domains_up:structvrna__unstructured__domain__s_1a8802b1b0512999a9f35202031811ce17}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_unstructured\_domain\_s.data}}}}

\label{\detokenize{grammar/domains_struc:structured-domains}}\label{\detokenize{grammar/domains_struc::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add and modify structured domains to the RNA folding grammar.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides the tools to add and modify structured domains to
the production rules of the RNA folding grammar.

\sphinxAtStartPar

structural modules that exhibit a more or less complex base pairing pattern.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback to evaluate whether or not a particular decomposition step is contributing to the solution space. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the prototype for callback functions used by the folding recursions to evaluate generic hard constraints. The first four parameters passed indicate the delimiting nucleotide positions of the decomposition, and the parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{denotes}} the decomposition step. The last parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{data}} is the auxiliary data structure associated to the hard constraints via vrna\_hc\_add\_data(), or NULL if no auxiliary data was added.

\pysigstartmultiline
\pysiglinewithargsret{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga74dd0cf2be4b70680a48488923d4cdec}}\DUrole{kt}{void}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{vrna\_constraints\_add}}}}{{\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:c.vrna_fold_compound_t}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{n}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{*}\DUrole{n}{fc}\sphinxparamcomma \DUrole{k}{const}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{kt}{char}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{*}\DUrole{n}{constraint}\sphinxparamcomma \DUrole{kt}{unsigned}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{kt}{int}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{options}}{}
\pysigstopmultiline
\pysigstopsignatures\sphinxstyleemphasis{\#include \textless{}ViennaRNA/constraints/basic.h\textgreater{}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add constraints to a {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:group__fold__compound_1ga1b0cef17fd40466cef5968eaeeff6166}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}} data structure. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this function to add/update the hard/soft constraints The function allows for passing a string ‘constraint’ that can either be a filename that points to a constraints definition file or it may be a pseudo dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation indicating hard constraints. For the latter, the user has to pass the {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga4bfc2f15c4f261c62a11af9d2aa80c90}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_DB}}}} option. Also, the user has to specify, which characters are allowed to be interpreted as constraints by passing the corresponding options via the third parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following is an example for adding hard constraints given in pseudo dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation. Here, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{fc}} is the {\hyperref[\detokenize{utils/datastructures/fold_compound:group__fold__compound_1ga1b0cef17fd40466cef5968eaeeff6166}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_fold\_compound\_t}}}} object, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{structure}} is a char array with the hard constraint in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation, and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{enforceConstraints}} is a flag indicating whether or not constraints for base pairs should be enforced instead of just doing a removal of base pair that conflict with the constraint.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{k+kt}{unsigned}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{int}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constraint\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{VRNA\PYGZus{}CONSTRAINT\PYGZus{}DB\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{enforceConstraints}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{constraint\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{VRNA\PYGZus{}CONSTRAINT\PYGZus{}DB\PYGZus{}ENFORCE\PYGZus{}BP}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{k}{if}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{canonicalBPonly}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{n}{constraint\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{|}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{VRNA\PYGZus{}CONSTRAINT\PYGZus{}DB\PYGZus{}CANONICAL\PYGZus{}BP}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{+w}{      }\PYG{n}{vrna\PYGZus{}constraints\PYGZus{}add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{fc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{const}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kt}{char}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{n}{cstruc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constraint\PYGZus{}options}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In constrat to the above, constraints may also be read from file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{vrna\PYGZus{}constraints\PYGZus{}add}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{fc}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{constraints\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{VRNA\PYGZus{}OPTION\PYGZus{}DEFAULT}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize/Reset hard constraints to default values. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function resets the hard constraints to their default values, i.e. all positions may be unpaired in all contexts, and base pairs are allowed in all contexts, if they resemble canonical pairs. Previously set hard constraints will be removed before initialization.

\pysigstartmultiline
\pysigline{\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:structvrna__hc__s}}\DUrole{k}{struct}\DUrole{w}{ }\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{\DUrole{n}{vrna\_hc\_s}}}}

\pysigstopsignatures\sphinxstyleemphasis{\#include \textless{}ViennaRNA/constraints/hard.h\textgreater{}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The hard constraints data structure. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
The content of this data structure determines the decomposition pattern used in the folding recursions. Attribute ‘matrix’ is used as source for the branching pattern of the decompositions during all folding recursions. Any entry in matrix{[}i,j{]} consists of the 6 LSB that allows one to distinguish the following types of base pairs:\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
in the exterior loop ({\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga9418eda62a5dec070896702c279d2548}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_EXT\_LOOP}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosing a hairpin ({\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga79203702b197b6b9d3b78eed40663eb1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_HP\_LOOP}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosing an interior loop ({\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga21feeab3a9e5fa5a9e3d9ac0fcf5994f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosed by an exterior loop ({\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga0536288e04ff6332ecdc23ca4705402b}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP\_ENC}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosing a multi branch loop ({\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga456ecd2ff00056bb64da8dd4f61bbfc5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosed by a multi branch loop ({\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga02a3d703ddbcfce393e4bbfcb9db7077}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP\_ENC}}}})

\end{itemize}


\sphinxAtStartPar
The four linear arrays ‘up\_xxx’ provide the number of available unpaired nucleotides (including position i) 3’ of each position in the sequence.

\sphinxAtStartPar


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga4fdb1e98f0d1a2d5728dd3a3aae4a357}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_hc\_init()}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga696dcf77887d856c6f21ea266d8b9ca2}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_hc\_free()}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga9418eda62a5dec070896702c279d2548}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_EXT\_LOOP}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga79203702b197b6b9d3b78eed40663eb1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_HP\_LOOP}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga21feeab3a9e5fa5a9e3d9ac0fcf5994f}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga456ecd2ff00056bb64da8dd4f61bbfc5}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:group__hard__constraints_1ga02a3d703ddbcfce393e4bbfcb9db7077}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP\_ENC}}}}

\subsubsection{Soft Constraints}
\label{\detokenize{grammar/constraints/soft:soft-constraints}}\label{\detokenize{grammar/constraints/soft::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Functions and data structures for secondary structure soft constraints.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Soft\sphinxhyphen{}constraints are used to change position specific contributions
in the recursions by adding bonuses/penalties in form of pseudo free energies
to certain loop configurations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Callback to retrieve pseudo energy contribution for soft constraint feature. 

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the prototype for callback functions used by the folding recursions to evaluate generic soft constraints. The first four parameters passed indicate the delimiting nucleotide positions of the decomposition, and the parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{denotes}} the decomposition step. The last parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{data}} is the auxiliary data structure associated to the hard constraints via {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/soft:group__soft__constraints_1ga0bab36ee5f9934b729778ec6f53cec3e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_sc\_add\_data()}}}}, or NULL if no auxiliary data was added.

\sphinxAtStartPar

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{fulllineitems}

This is the prototype for callback functions used by the partition function recursions to evaluate generic soft constraints. The first four parameters passed indicate the delimiting nucleotide positions of the decomposition, and the parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{denotes}} the decomposition step. The last parameter \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{data}} is the auxiliary data structure associated to the hard constraints via {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/soft:group__soft__constraints_1ga0bab36ee5f9934b729778ec6f53cec3e}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{vrna\_sc\_add\_data()}}}}, or NULL if no auxiliary data was added.

\sphinxAtStartPar


\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{{\hyperref[\detokenize{callbacks:callbacks_1_callbacks000016}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Notes on Callback Functions:}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
This callback enables one to add (pseudo\sphinxhyphen{})energy contributions to individual decompositions of the secondary structure (Partition function variant, i.e. contributions must be returned as Boltzmann factors). 

\end{fulllineitems}

\subsubsection{Introduction}
\label{\detokenize{grammar/constraints:introduction}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Secondary Structure constraints can be subdivided into two groups:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Hard Constraints}}}}, and

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Soft Constraints}}}}.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
While \sphinxstyleemphasis{hard constraints} directly influence the production rules used in the folding
recursions by allowing, disallowing, or enforcing certain decomposition steps,
\sphinxstyleemphasis{soft constraints} are used to change position specific contributions
in the recursions by adding bonuses/penalties in form of pseudo free energies
to certain loop configurations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Secondary structure constraints are always applied at decomposition level, i.e.
in each step of the recursive structure decomposition, for instance during MFE
prediction. Below is a visualization of the decomposition scheme

\noindent\sphinxincludegraphics{{recursions}.png}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Hard Constraints}}}} the following option flags may be used to constrain
the pairing behavior of single, or pairs of nucleotides:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_EXT_LOOP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_EXT\_LOOP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_HP_LOOP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_HP\_LOOP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_INT_LOOP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_INT_LOOP_ENC}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP\_ENC}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_MB_LOOP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_MB_LOOP_ENC}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP\_ENC}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_ENFORCE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_NO\_REMOVE}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/hard:c.VRNA_CONSTRAINT_CONTEXT_ALL_LOOPS}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_ALL\_LOOPS}}}}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, for {\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints/soft::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Soft Constraints}}}} we do not allow for simple loop type
dependent constraining. But soft constraints are equipped with generic constraint
support. This enables the user to pass arbitrary callback functions that
return auxiliary energy contributions for evaluation the evaluation of any
decomposition.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback will then always be notified about the type of decomposition
that is happening, and the corresponding delimiting sequence positions. The
following decomposition steps are distinguished, and should be captured by
the user’s implementation of the callback:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_PAIR_HP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_PAIR\_HP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_PAIR_IL}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_PAIR\_IL}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_PAIR_ML}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_PAIR\_ML}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_ML_ML_ML}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_ML\_ML\_ML}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_ML_STEM}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_ML\_STEM}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_ML_ML}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_ML\_ML}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_ML_UP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_ML\_UP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_ML_ML_STEM}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_ML\_ML\_STEM}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_ML_COAXIAL}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_ML\_COAXIAL}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_EXT}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_EXT}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_UP}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_UP}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_STEM}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_STEM}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_EXT_EXT}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_EXT\_EXT}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_STEM_EXT}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_STEM\_EXT}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_STEM_OUTSIDE}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_STEM\_OUTSIDE}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_EXT_STEM}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_EXT\_STEM}}}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{grammar/constraints:c.VRNA_DECOMP_EXT_EXT_STEM1}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_DECOMP\_EXT\_EXT\_STEM1}}}}}

\end{itemize}
