\index{E\_Stem() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{E\_Stem()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.E_Stem}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{E\_Stem}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{type}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{si1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{sj1}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{extLoop}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{P}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the energy contribution of a stem branching off a loop\sphinxhyphen{}region.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function computes the energy contribution of a stem that branches off a loop region. This can
be the case in multiloops, when a stem branching off increases the degree of the loop but also
\sphinxstyleemphasis{immediately interior base pairs} of an exterior loop contribute free energy. To switch the behavior
of the function according to the evaluation of a multiloop\sphinxhyphen{} or exterior\sphinxhyphen{}loop\sphinxhyphen{}stem, you pass the flag
‘extLoop’. The returned energy contribution consists of a TerminalAU penalty if the pair type is
greater than 2, dangling end contributions of mismatching nucleotides adjacent to the stem if only
one of the si1, sj1 parameters is greater than 0 and mismatch energies if both mismatching
nucleotides are positive values. Thus, to avoid incorporating dangling end or mismatch energies just
pass a negative number, e.g. \sphinxhyphen{}1 to the mismatch argument.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{This is an illustration of how the energy contribution is assembled:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
3’  5’
|   |
X \sphinxhyphen{} Y

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
5’\sphinxhyphen{}si1     sj1\sphinxhyphen{}3’

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here, (X,Y) is the base pair that closes the stem that branches off a loop region. The nucleotides
si1 and sj1 are the 5’\sphinxhyphen{} and 3’\sphinxhyphen{} mismatches, respectively. If the base pair type of (X,Y) is greater
than 2 (i.e. an A\sphinxhyphen{}U or G\sphinxhyphen{}U pair, the TerminalAU penalty will be included in the energy contribution
returned. If si1 and sj1 are both nonnegative numbers, mismatch energies will also be included. If
one of si1 or sj1 is a negative value, only 5’ or 3’ dangling end contributions are taken into
account. To prohibit any of these mismatch contributions to be incorporated, just pass a negative
number to both, si1 and sj1. In case the argument extLoop is 0, the returned energy contribution
also includes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{internal\sphinxhyphen{}loop\sphinxhyphen{}penalty} of a multiloop stem with closing pair type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\DUrole{versionmodified,deprecated}{Deprecated since version 2.6.4: }Please use one of the functions RNA.E\_ext\_stem() and E\_MLstem() instead! Use the former for
cases where \sphinxtitleref{extLoop} != 0 and the latter otherwise.


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.E_MLstem}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{E\_MLstem}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_ExtLoop}}


\end{sphinxseealso}


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}

\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The pair type of the first base pair un the stem

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{si1}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The 5’\sphinxhyphen{}mismatching nucleotide

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sj1}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The 3’\sphinxhyphen{}mismatching nucleotide

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{extLoop}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} A flag that indicates whether the contribution reflects the one of an exterior loop or not

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{P}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.param() *}}) \textendash{} The data structure containing scaled energy parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Free energy of the branch off the loop in dcal/mol

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluate a stem branching off the exterior loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Given a base pair \((i,j)\) encoded by \sphinxstyleemphasis{type}, compute the energy contribution including
dangling\sphinxhyphen{}end/terminal\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch contributions. Instead of returning the energy contribution per\sphinxhyphen{}se,
this function returns the corresponding Boltzmann factor. If either of the adjacent nucleotides
\((i - 1)\) and \((j+1)\) must not contribute stacking energy, the corresponding encoding
must be \(-1\).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The base pair encoding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n5d}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The encoded nucleotide directly adjacent at the 5’ side of the base pair (may be \sphinxhyphen{}1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n3d}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The encoded nucleotide directly adjacent at the 3’ side of the base pair (may be \sphinxhyphen{}1)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.param() *}}) \textendash{} The pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed energy parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local MFE prediction using a sliding window approach (simplified interface)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This simplified interface to RNA.fold\_compound.mfe\_window() computes the MFE and locally optimal secondary
structure using default options. Structures are predicted using a sliding window approach, where
base pairs may not span outside the window. Memory required for dynamic programming (DP) matrices
will be allocated and free’d on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly. Hence, after return of this function, the recursively
filled matrices are not available any more for any post\sphinxhyphen{}processing.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as overloaded function \sphinxtitleref{Lfold()} in the global namespace. The
parameter \sphinxtitleref{file} defaults to \sphinxtitleref{NULL} and may be omitted. See e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.Lfold}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.Lfold()}}}}} in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\index{Lfoldz() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{Lfoldz()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.Lfoldz}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{Lfoldz}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{sequence}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{window\_size}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{min\_z}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{nullfile}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local MFE prediction using a sliding window approach with z\sphinxhyphen{}score cut\sphinxhyphen{}off (simplified interface)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This simplified interface to RNA.fold\_compound.mfe\_window\_zscore() computes the MFE and locally optimal secondary
structure using default options. Structures are predicted using a sliding window approach, where
base pairs may not span outside the window. Memory required for dynamic programming (DP) matrices
will be allocated and free’d on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly. Hence, after return of this function, the recursively
filled matrices are not available any more for any post\sphinxhyphen{}processing. This function is the z\sphinxhyphen{}score
version of RNA.Lfold(), i.e. only predictions above a certain z\sphinxhyphen{}score cut\sphinxhyphen{}off value are printed.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{string}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The nucleic acid sequence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{window\_size}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The window size for locally optimal structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{min\_z}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) \textendash{} The minimal z\sphinxhyphen{}score for a predicted structure to appear in the output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{file}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FILE *}}) \textendash{} The output file handle where predictions are written to (if NULL, output is written to stdout)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{MEA\_from\_plist() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{MEA\_from\_plist()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.MEA_from_plist}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{MEA\_from\_plist}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}\DUrole{n}{args}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute a MEA (maximum expected accuracy) structure from a list of probabilities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The algorithm maximizes the expected accuracy
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}A(S) = \sum_{(i,j) \in S} 2 \gamma p_{ij} + \sum_{i \notin S} p^u_{i}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher values of \(\gamma\) result in more base pairs of lower probability and thus higher
sensitivity. Low values of \(\gamma\) result in structures containing only highly likely pairs
(high specificity). The code of the MEA function also demonstrates the use of sparse dynamic
programming scheme to reduce the time and memory complexity of folding.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as overloaded function \sphinxtitleref{MEA\_from\_plist\textasciigrave{}(gamma = 1., md = NULL). Note,
that it returns the MEA structure and MEA value as a tuple (MEA\_structure, MEA). See, e.g.
:py:func:\textasciigrave{}RNA.MEA\_from\_plist()} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{plist}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.ep() *}}) \textendash{} A list of base pair probabilities the MEA structure is computed from

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sequence}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The RNA sequence that corresponds to the list of probability values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) \textendash{} The weighting factor for base pairs vs. unpaired nucleotides

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{md}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.md() *}}) \textendash{} A model details data structure (maybe NULL)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mea}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(double)}}) \textendash{} A pointer to a variable where the MEA value will be written to

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An MEA structure (or NULL on any error)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The unpaired probabilities \(p^u_{i} = 1 - \sum_{j \neq i} p_{ij}\) are usually computed from
the supplied pairing probabilities \(p_{ij}\) as stored in \sphinxtitleref{plist} entries of type
RNA.PLIST\_TYPE\_BASEPAIR. To overwrite individual \(p^u_{o}\) values simply add entries with
type RNA.PLIST\_TYPE\_UNPAIRED
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To include G\sphinxhyphen{}Quadruplex support, the corresponding field in \sphinxtitleref{md} must be set.
\end{quote}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{PS\_dot\_plot\_list() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{PS\_dot\_plot\_list()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.PS_dot_plot_list}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{PS\_dot\_plot\_list}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{seq}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{filename}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{pl}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{mf}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{comment}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Produce a postscript dot\sphinxhyphen{}plot from two pair lists.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function reads two plist structures (e.g. base pair probabilities and a secondary structure) as
produced by assign\_plist\_from\_pr() and assign\_plist\_from\_db() and produces a postscript “dot plot”
that is written to ‘filename’.
Using base pair probabilities in the first and mfe structure in the second plist, the resulting
“dot plot” represents each base pairing probability by a square of corresponding area in a upper
triangle matrix. The lower part of the matrix contains the minimum free energy structure.

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{filename}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} A filename for the postscript output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{pl}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.ep() *}}) \textendash{} The base pair probability pairlist

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mf}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.ep() *}}) \textendash{} The mfe secondary structure pairlist

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{comment}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} A comment

\end{itemize}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Minimum Free Energy (MFE), and a corresponding consensus secondary structure for an RNA
sequence alignment using a comparative method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This simplified interface to RNA.fold\_compound.mfe() computes the MFE and, if required, a consensus secondary
structure for an RNA sequence alignment using default options. Memory required for dynamic
programming (DP) matrices will be allocated and free’d on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly. Hence, after return of this
function, the recursively filled matrices are not available any more for any post\sphinxhyphen{}processing, e.g.
suboptimal backtracking, etc.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as function \sphinxtitleref{alifold()} in the global namespace. The parameter
\sphinxtitleref{structure} is returned along with the MFE und must not be provided. See e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.alifold}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.alifold()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sequences}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const char **}}) \textendash{} RNA sequence alignment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{structure}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} A pointer to the character array where the secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation will be
written to

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
the minimum free energy (MFE) in kcal/mol

\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{boustrophedon() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{boustrophedon()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.boustrophedon}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{boustrophedon}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}\DUrole{n}{args}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate a sequence of Boustrophedon distributed numbers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function generates a sequence of positive natural numbers within the interval \([start,
end]\) in a Boustrophedon fashion. That is, the numbers \(start, \ldots, end\) in the resulting
list are alternating between left and right ends of the interval while progressing to the inside,
i.e. the list consists of a sequence of natural numbers of the form:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}start, end, start + 1, end - 1, start + 2, end - 2, \ldots\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The resulting list is 1\sphinxhyphen{}based and contains the length of the sequence of numbers at it’s 0\sphinxhyphen{}th
position.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Upon failure, the function returns \sphinxstylestrong{NULL}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as overloaded global function \sphinxtitleref{boustrophedon()}. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.boustrophedon}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.boustrophedon()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}) \textendash{} The first number of the list (left side of the interval)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{end}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{size()}}) \textendash{} The last number of the list (right side of the interval)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of alternating numbers from the interval \([start, end]\) (or \sphinxstylestrong{NULL} on error)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(unsigned int)}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

Compute Minimum Free Energy (MFE), and a corresponding secondary structure for a circular RNA
sequence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This simplified interface to RNA.fold\_compound.mfe() computes the MFE and, if required, a secondary structure for
a circular RNA sequence using default options. Memory required for dynamic programming (DP) matrices
will be allocated and free’d on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly. Hence, after return of this function, the recursively
filled matrices are not available any more for any post\sphinxhyphen{}processing, e.g. suboptimal backtracking,
etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Folding of circular RNA sequences is handled as a post\sphinxhyphen{}processing step of the forward recursions.
See   Hofacker and Stadler {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id21}{2006}{]}  for further details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}knots from an input structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function removes pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}knots from an input structure by determining the minimum number of base
pairs that need to be removed to make the structure pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}knot free.

\sphinxAtStartPar
To accomplish that, we use a dynamic programming algorithm similar to the Nussinov maxmimum matching
approach.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The input structure must be in a dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket string like form where crossing base pairs are denoted
by the use of additional types of matching brackets, e.g. \sphinxtitleref{\textless{}\textgreater{}}, \sphinxtitleref{\{\}}, {\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}\textasciigrave{}}{[}{]}, \sphinxtitleref{\{\}}. Furthermore,
crossing pairs may be annotated by matching uppercase/lowercase letters from the alphabet \sphinxtitleref{A\sphinxhyphen{}Z}. For
the latter, the uppercase letter must be the 5’ and the lowercase letter the 3’ nucleotide of the
base pair. The actual type of brackets to be recognized by this function must be specifed through
the \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as an overloaded function \sphinxtitleref{db\_pk\_remove()} where the optional second
parameter \sphinxtitleref{options} defaults to RNA.BRACKETS\_ANY. See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.db_pk_remove}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.db\_pk\_remove()}}}}} in
the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\index{db\_to\_tree\_string() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{db\_to\_tree\_string()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.db_to_tree_string}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{db\_to\_tree\_string}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{std::string structure}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{unsigned int type}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ std::string}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert a Dot\sphinxhyphen{}Bracket structure string into tree string representation.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows one to convert a secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation into one of the
various tree representations for secondary structures. The resulting tree is then represented as a
string of parenthesis and node symbols, similar to to the Newick format.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently we support conversion into the following formats, denoted by the value of parameter
\sphinxtitleref{type:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_HIT \sphinxhyphen{}  Homeomorphically Irreducible Tree (HIT) representation of a secondary
structure.   (See also   Fontana \sphinxstyleemphasis{et al.} {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id25}{1993}{]} )

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_SHAPIRO\_SHORT \sphinxhyphen{}  (short) Coarse Grained representation of a secondary
structure   (same as   Shapiro {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id27}{1988}{]} , but with root node \sphinxtitleref{R} and without \sphinxtitleref{S} nodes for
the stems)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_SHAPIRO \sphinxhyphen{}  (full) Coarse Grained representation of a secondary structure
(See also   Shapiro {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id27}{1988}{]} )

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_SHAPIRO\_EXT \sphinxhyphen{}  (extended) Coarse Grained representation of a secondary
structure   (same as   Shapiro {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id27}{1988}{]} , but external nodes denoted as \sphinxtitleref{E} )

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_SHAPIRO\_WEIGHT \sphinxhyphen{}  (weighted) Coarse Grained representation of a secondary
structure   (same as RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_SHAPIRO\_EXT but with additional weights for number of
unpaired nucleotides in loop, and number of pairs in stems)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.STRUCTURE\_TREE\_EXPANDED \sphinxhyphen{}  Expanded Tree representation of a secondary structure.

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{structure}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The null\sphinxhyphen{}terminated dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket structure string

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} A switch to determine the type of tree string representation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A tree representation of the input \sphinxtitleref{structure}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Enumerate all necklaces with fixed content.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function implements \sphinxstyleemphasis{A fast algorithm to generate necklaces with fixed content} as published by
Sawada {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id36}{2003}{]} .

\sphinxAtStartPar
The function receives a list of counts (the elements on the necklace) for each type of object within
a necklace. The list starts at index 0 and ends with an entry that has a count of 0. The algorithm
then enumerates all non\sphinxhyphen{}cyclic permutations of the content, returned as a list of necklaces. This
list, again, is zero\sphinxhyphen{}terminated, i.e. the last entry of the list is a \sphinxtitleref{NULL} pointer.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as global function \sphinxtitleref{enumerate\_necklaces()} which accepts lists input,
an produces list of lists output. See, e.g.   {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.enumerate_necklaces}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.enumerate\_necklaces()}}}}} in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Evaluate free energy of a sequence/structure pair, assume sequence to be circular, allow for
G\sphinxhyphen{}Quadruplexes in the structure, and print contributions per loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is the same as RNA.eval\_structure\_simple\_v() but assumes the input sequence to be
circular and allows for annotated G\sphinxhyphen{}Quadruplexes in the dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket structure input.

\sphinxAtStartPar
G\sphinxhyphen{}Quadruplexes are annotated as plus signs (‘+’) for each G involved in the motif. Linker sequences
must be denoted by dots (‘.’) as they are considered unpaired. Below is an example of a 2\sphinxhyphen{}layer
G\sphinxhyphen{}quadruplex:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available through an overloaded version of RNA.eval\_circ\_gquad\_structure().
The last two arguments for this function are optional and default to RNA.VERBOSITY\_QUIET and
\sphinxtitleref{NULL}, respectively. See, e.g.   {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.eval_circ_gquad_structure}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.eval\_circ\_gquad\_structure()}}}}} in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the free energy of an already folded RNA.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for energy evaluation of a given sequence/structure pair where the structure is
provided in pair\_table format as obtained from RNA.ptable(). Model details, energy parameters, and
possibly soft constraints are used as provided via the parameter ‘fc’. The fold\_compound does not
need to contain any DP matrices, but all the most basic init values as one would get from a call
like this:  In contrast to RNA.fold\_compound.eval\_structure\_pt\_verbose() this function assumes default model
details and default energy parameters in order to evaluate the free energy of the secondary
structure. Threefore, it serves as a simple interface function for energy evaluation for situations
where no changes on the energy model are required.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate the free energy of an already folded RNA and print contributions per loop.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows for detailed energy evaluation of a given sequence/structure pair. In contrast
to RNA.fold\_compound.eval\_structure() this function prints detailed energy contributions based on individual
loops to a file handle. If NULL is passed as file handle, this function defaults to print to stdout.
Any positive \sphinxtitleref{verbosity\_level} activates potential warning message of the energy evaluting
functions, while values \(\ge 1\) allow for detailed control of what data is printed. A
negative parameter \sphinxtitleref{verbosity\_level} turns off printing all together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In contrast to RNA.fold\_compound.eval\_structure\_verbose() this function assumes default model details and default
energy parameters in order to evaluate the free energy of the secondary structure. Threefore, it
serves as a simple interface function for energy evaluation for situations where no changes on the
energy model are required.

\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{file\_fasta\_read}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{FILE * file}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{unsigned int options=0}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ int}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get a (fasta) data set from a file or stdin.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function may be used to obtain complete datasets from a filehandle or stdin. A dataset is
always defined to contain at least a sequence. If data starts with a fasta header, i.e. a line like
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\textgreater{}some header info  then RNA.file\_fasta\_read\_record() will assume that the sequence that follows
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
the header may span over several lines. To disable this behavior and to assign a single line to the
argument ‘sequence’ one can pass RNA.INPUT\_NO\_SPAN in the ‘options’ argument. If no fasta header is
read in the beginning of a data block, a sequence must not span over multiple lines!

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unless the options RNA.INPUT\_NOSKIP\_COMMENTS or RNA.INPUT\_NOSKIP\_BLANK\_LINES are passed, a
sequence may be interrupted by lines starting with a comment character or empty lines.
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A sequence is regarded as completely read if it was either assumed to not span over multiple lines,
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
a secondary structure or structure constraint follows the sequence on the next line, or a new header
marks the beginning of a new sequence…

\sphinxAtStartPar
All lines following the sequence (this includes comments) that do not initiate a new dataset
according to the above definition are available through the line\sphinxhyphen{}array ‘rest’. Here one can usually
find the structure constraint or other information belonging to the current dataset. Filling of
‘rest’ may be prevented by passing RNA.INPUT\_NO\_REST to the options argument.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The main purpose of this function is to be able to easily parse blocks of data in the header of a
loop where all calculations for the appropriate data is done inside the loop. The loop may be then
left on certain return values, e.g.:

\sphinxAtStartPar
In the example above, the while loop will be terminated when RNA.file\_fasta\_read\_record() returns
either an error, EOF, or a user initiated quit request.

\sphinxAtStartPar
As long as data is read from stdin (we are passing NULL as the file pointer), the id is printed if
it is available for the current block of data. The sequence will be printed in any case and if some
more lines belong to the current block of data each line will be printed as well.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{header}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char **}}) \textendash{} A pointer which will be set such that it points to the header of the record

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sequence}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char **}}) \textendash{} A pointer which will be set such that it points to the sequence of the record

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{rest}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{char ***}}) \textendash{} A pointer which will be set such that it points to an array of lines which also belong to the
record

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{file}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{FILE *}}) \textendash{} A file handle to read from (if NULL, this function reads from stdin)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{options}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} Some options which may be passed to alter the behavior of the function, use 0 for no options

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A flag with information about what the function actually did read

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{This function will exit any program with an error message if no sequence could be read!}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is NOT threadsafe! It uses a global variable to store information about the next data

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
block. Do not forget to free the memory occupied by header, sequence and rest!

\index{file\_msa\_detect\_format() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{file\_msa\_detect\_format()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect the format of a multiple sequence alignment file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function attempts to determine the format of a file that supposedly contains a multiple
sequence alignment (MSA). This is useful in cases where a MSA file contains more than a single
record and therefore RNA.file\_msa\_read() can not be applied, since it only retrieves the first.
Here, one can try to guess the correct file format using this function and then loop over the file,
record by record using one of the low\sphinxhyphen{}level record retrieval functions for the corresponding MSA
file format.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function exists as an overloaded version where the \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter may be omitted! In
that case, the \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter defaults to RNA.FILE\_FORMAT\_MSA\_DEFAULT. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.file_msa_detect_format}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.file\_msa\_detect\_format()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{filename}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The name of input file that contains the alignment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{options}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} Options to manipulate the behavior of this function

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The MSA file format, or RNA.FILE\_FORMAT\_MSA\_UNKNOWN

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function parses the entire first record within the specified file. As a result, it returns
RNA.FILE\_FORMAT\_MSA\_UNKNOWN not only if it can’t detect the file’s format, but also in cases where
the file doesn’t contain sequences!

Read a multiple sequence alignment from file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function reads the (first) multiple sequence alignment from an input file. The read alignment
is split into the sequence id/name part and the actual sequence information and stored in memory as
arrays of ids/names and sequences. If the alignment file format allows for additional information,
such as an ID of the entire alignment or consensus structure information, this data is retrieved as
well and made available. The \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter allows to specify the set of alignment file formats
that should be used to retrieve the data. If 0 is passed as option, the list of alignment file
formats defaults to RNA.FILE\_FORMAT\_MSA\_DEFAULT.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, the list of parsable multiple sequence alignment file formats consists of:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
msa\sphinxhyphen{}formats\sphinxhyphen{}clustal

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
msa\sphinxhyphen{}formats\sphinxhyphen{}stockholm

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
msa\sphinxhyphen{}formats\sphinxhyphen{}fasta

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
msa\sphinxhyphen{}formats\sphinxhyphen{}maf

\index{filename\_sanitize() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{filename\_sanitize()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.filename_sanitize}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{filename\_sanitize}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}\DUrole{n}{args}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sanitize a file name.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a new file name where all invalid characters are substituted by a replacement character. If
no replacement character is supplied, invalid characters are simply removed from the filename. File
names may also never exceed a length of 255 characters. Longer file names will undergo a ‘smart’
truncation process, where the filenames suffix, i.e. everything after the last dot .’, is attempted
to be kept intact. Hence, only the filename part before the suffix is reduced in such a way that the
total filename complies to the length restriction of 255 characters. If no suffix is present or the
suffix itself already exceeds the maximum length, the filename is simply truncated from the back of
the string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
For now we consider the following characters invalid:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
backslash ‘\textquotesingle{}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
slash ‘/’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
question mark ‘?’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
percent sign ‘’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
asterisk ‘*’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
colon ‘:’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pipe symbol ‘|’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
double quote ‘”’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
triangular brackets ‘\textless{}’ and ‘\textgreater{}’

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Furthermore, the (resulting) file name must not be a reserved file name, such as:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘.’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘..’

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{name}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The input file name

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{replacement}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The replacement character, or NULL

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The sanitized file name, or NULL

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allocates a new block of memory for the sanitized string. It also may return (a) NULL
if the input is pointing to NULL, or (b) an empty string if the input only consists of invalid
characters which are simply removed!
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{fold}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{string) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} (structure}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{mfe)fold(string) \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} (structure}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{mfe}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute Minimum Free Energy (MFE), and a corresponding secondary structure for an RNA sequence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This simplified interface to RNA.fold\_compound.mfe() computes the MFE and, if required, a secondary structure for
an RNA sequence using default options. Memory required for dynamic programming (DP) matrices will be
allocated and free’d on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly. Hence, after return of this function, the recursively filled
matrices are not available any more for any post\sphinxhyphen{}processing, e.g. suboptimal backtracking, etc.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{itemize}

separated by an ampersand character \sphinxtitleref{\&} (for cofolding)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound(aln)} \sphinxhyphen{} Initialize with a sequence alignment \sphinxstyleemphasis{aln} stored as a list of
sequences (with gap characters).

\end{itemize}

functions that mainly operate on the corresponding \sphinxtitleref{C} data structure:

\index{MEA() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{MEA()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.MEA}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{MEA}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{fold\_compound self}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ char}}
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{MEA}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{fold\_compound self}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{double gamma}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ char *}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute a MEA (maximum expected accuracy) structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The algorithm maximizes the expected accuracy
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}A(S) = \sum_{(i,j) \in S} 2 \gamma p_{ij} + \sum_{i \notin S} p^u_{i}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Higher values of \(\gamma\) result in more base pairs of lower probability and thus higher
sensitivity. Low values of \(\gamma\) result in structures containing only highly likely pairs
(high specificity). The code of the MEA function also demonstrates the use of sparse dynamic
programming scheme to reduce the time and memory complexity of folding.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Precondition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.fold\_compound.pf() must be executed on input parameter \sphinxtitleref{fc}

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as overloaded method \sphinxtitleref{MEA\textasciigrave{}(gamma = 1.) to objects of type
\textasciigrave{}fold\_compound}. Note, that it returns the MEA structure and MEA value as a tuple
(MEA\_structure, MEA). See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.MEA}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.MEA()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) \textendash{} The weighting factor for base pairs vs. unpaired nucleotides

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mea}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(double)}}) \textendash{} A pointer to a variable where the MEA value will be written to

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
An MEA structure (or NULL on any error)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get the centroid structure of the ensemble.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The centroid is the structure with the minimal average distance to all other structures
\(<d(S)> = \sum_{(i,j) \in S} (1-p_{ij}) + \sum_{(i,j) \notin S} p_{ij}\)
Thus, the centroid is simply the structure containing all pairs with \(p_{i}j>0.5\) The distance
of the centroid to the ensemble is written to the memory adressed by \sphinxstyleemphasis{dist}.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{dist}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(double)}}) \textendash{} A pointer to the distance variable where the centroid distance will be written to

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The centroid structure of the ensemble in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation (\sphinxtitleref{NULL} on error)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{ensemble\_defect() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{ensemble\_defect()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.ensemble_defect}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{ensemble\_defect}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}\DUrole{n}{args}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the Ensemble Defect for a given target structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a wrapper around \sphinxstylestrong{RNA.ensemble\_defect\_pt()}. Given a target structure \(s\), compute
the average dissimilarity of a randomly drawn structure from the ensemble, i.e.:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}ED(s) = 1 - \frac{1}{n} \sum_{ij, (i,j) \in s} p_{ij} - \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i}(1 - s_{i})q_{i}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with sequence length \(n\), the probability \(p_{ij}\) of a base pair \((i,j)\), the
probability \(q_{i} = 1 - \sum_{j} p_{ij}\) of nucleotide \(i\) being unpaired, and the
indicator variable \(s_{i} = 1\) if \(\exists (i,j) \in s\), and \(s_{i} = 0\)
otherwise.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Precondition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

terminal A\sphinxhyphen{}U mismatch penalty, and maybe some generic soft constraint contribution for that
decomposition.

\sphinxAtStartPar

dangling\sphinxhyphen{}end/terminal\sphinxhyphen{}mismatch contributions. Instead of returning the energy contribution per\sphinxhyphen{}se,
this function returns the corresponding Boltzmann factor. If either of the adjacent nucleotides
\((i - 1)\) and \((j+1)\) must not contribute stacking energy, the corresponding encoding
must be \(-1\).

\index{exp\_params\_rescale() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{exp\_params\_rescale()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.exp_params_rescale}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{exp\_params\_rescale}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}\DUrole{n}{args}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rescale Boltzmann factors for partition function computations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function may be used to (automatically) rescale the Boltzmann factors used in partition
function computations. Since partition functions over subsequences can easily become extremely
large, the RNAlib internally rescales them to avoid numerical over\sphinxhyphen{} and/or underflow. Therefore, a
proper scaling factor \(s\) needs to be chosen that in turn is then used to normalize the
corresponding partition functions \(\hat{q}[i,j] = q[i,j] / s^{(j-i+1)}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function provides two ways to automatically adjust the scaling factor.
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic guess

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic adjustment according to MFE

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing \sphinxtitleref{NULL} as second parameter activates the \sphinxstyleemphasis{automatic guess mode}. Here, the scaling factor is
recomputed according to a mean free energy of \sphinxtitleref{184.3*length} cal for random sequences.
On the other hand, if the MFE for a sequence is known, it can be used to recompute a more robust
scaling factor, since it represents the lowest free energy of the entire ensemble of structures,
i.e. the highest Boltzmann factor. To activate this second mode of \sphinxstyleemphasis{automatic adjustment according
to MFE}, a pointer to the MFE value needs to be passed as second argument. This value is then taken
to compute the scaling factor as \(s = exp((sfact * MFE) / kT / length )\), where sfact is an
additional scaling weight located in the RNA.md() data structure of \sphinxtitleref{exp\_params} in \sphinxtitleref{fc}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This recomputation only takes place if the \sphinxtitleref{pf\_scale} attribute of the \sphinxtitleref{exp\_params} data structure
contained in \sphinxtitleref{fc} has a value below \sphinxtitleref{1.0}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The computed scaling factor \(s\) will be stored as \sphinxtitleref{pf\_scale} attribute of the \sphinxtitleref{exp\_params}
data structure in \sphinxtitleref{fc}.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached to RNA.fc() objects as overloaded \sphinxtitleref{exp\_params\_rescale()} method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When no parameter is passed to this method, the resulting action is the same as passing \sphinxtitleref{NULL}
as second parameter to RNA.fold\_compound.exp\_params\_rescale(), i.e. default scaling of the
partition
function. Passing an energy in kcal/mol, e.g. as retrieved by a previous call to the \sphinxtitleref{mfe()}
method, instructs all subsequent calls to scale the partition function accordingly. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.exp_params_rescale}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.exp\_params\_rescale()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mfe}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(double)}}) \textendash{} A pointer to the MFE (in kcal/mol) or NULL

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.exp_params_subst}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.exp\_params\_subst}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.md}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.md}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.exp_param}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.exp\_param}}}}}, {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound}}}}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Reset Boltzmann factors for partition function computations within a RNA.fold\_compound() according
to provided, or default model details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows one to rescale Boltzmann factors for subsequent partition function computations
according to a set of model details, e.g. temperature values. To do so, the caller provides either a
pointer to a set of model details to be used for rescaling, or NULL if global default setting should
be used.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached to RNA.fc() objects as overloaded \sphinxtitleref{exp\_params\_reset()} method.

\sphinxAtStartPar
When no parameter is passed to this method, the resulting action is the same as passing \sphinxtitleref{NULL}
as second parameter to RNA.fold\_compound.exp\_params\_reset(), i.e. global default model settings
are used.
Passing an object of type RNA.md() resets the fold compound according to the specifications
stored within the RNA.md() object. See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.exp_params_reset}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.exp\_params\_reset()}}}}}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the specific heat for an RNA.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function computes an RNAs specific heat in a given temperature range from the partition
function by numeric differentiation. The result is returned as a list of pairs of temperature in C
and specific heat in Kcal/(Mol*K).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Users can specify the temperature range for the computation from \sphinxtitleref{T\_min} to \sphinxtitleref{T\_max}, as well as the
increment step size \sphinxtitleref{T\_increment}. The latter also determines how many times the partition function
is computed. Finally, the parameter \sphinxtitleref{mpoints} determines how smooth the curve should be. The
algorithm itself fits a parabola to \(2 \cdot mpoints + 1\) data points to calculate 2nd
derivatives. Increasing this parameter produces a smoother curve.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as overloaded method \sphinxtitleref{heat\_capacity()} to objects of type
\sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}. If the optional function arguments \sphinxtitleref{T\_min}, \sphinxtitleref{T\_max}, \sphinxtitleref{T\_increment}, and
\sphinxtitleref{mpoints} are omitted, they default to 0.0, 100.0, 1.0 and 2, respectively. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.heat_capacity}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.heat\_capacity()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{T\_max}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Highest temperature in C

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{T\_increment}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Stepsize for temperature incrementation in C (a reasonable choice might be 1C)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mpoints}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The number of interpolation points to calculate 2nd derivative (a reasonable choice might be 2,
min: 1, max: 100)

A list of pairs of temperatures and corresponding heat capacity or \sphinxstyleemphasis{NULL} upon any failure. The

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to RNA.fold\_compound.heat\_capacity(), this function computes an RNAs specific heat in a given temperature
range from the partition function by numeric differentiation. Instead of returning a list of
temperature/specific heat pairs, however, this function returns the individual results through a
callback mechanism. The provided function will be called for each result and passed the
corresponding temperature and specific heat values along with the arbitrary data as provided through
the \sphinxtitleref{data} pointer argument.

Users can specify the temperature range for the computation from \sphinxtitleref{T\_min} to \sphinxtitleref{T\_max}, as well as the
increment step size \sphinxtitleref{T\_increment}. The latter also determines how many times the partition function
is computed. Finally, the parameter \sphinxtitleref{mpoints} determines how smooth the curve should be. The
algorithm itself fits a parabola to \(2 \cdot mpoints + 1\) data points to calculate 2nd
derivatives. Increasing this parameter produces a smoother curve.

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get the mean base pair distance in the thermodynamic ensemble.
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}<d> = \sum_{a,b} p_{a} p_{b} d(S_{a},S_{b})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
this can be computed from the pair probs \(p_{ij}\) as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}<d> = \sum_{ij} p_{ij}(1-p_{ij})\end{split}
\end{equation*}\begin{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{mean\_bp\_distance()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}.

\end{description}

\index{mfe() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{mfe()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute minimum free energy and an appropriate secondary structure of an RNA sequence, or RNA
sequence alignment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Depending on the type of the provided RNA.fold\_compound(), this function predicts the MFE for a
single sequence (or connected component of multiple sequences), or an averaged MFE for a sequence
alignment. If backtracking is activated, it also constructs the corresponding secondary structure,
or consensus structure. Therefore, the second parameter, \sphinxstyleemphasis{structure}, has to point to an allocated
block of memory with a size of at least \(\mathrm{strlen}(\mathrm{sequence})+1\) to store the
backtracked MFE structure. (For consensus structures, this is the length of the alignment + 1. If
\sphinxtitleref{NULL} is passed, no backtracking will be performed.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{mfe()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}. The parameter
\sphinxtitleref{structure} is returned along with the MFE und must not be provided. See e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.mfe}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.mfe()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\index{mfe\_window() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{mfe\_window()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.mfe_window}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{mfe\_window}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{nullfile}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{None}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Local MFE prediction using a sliding window approach.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes minimum free energy structures using a sliding window approach, where base pairs may not
span outside the window. In contrast to RNA.fold\_compound.mfe(), where a maximum base pair span may be set using
the RNA.md().max\_bp\_span attribute and one globally optimal structure is predicted, this function
uses a sliding window to retrieve all locally optimal structures within each window. The size of the
sliding window is set in the RNA.md().window\_size attribute, prior to the retrieval of the
RNA.fold\_compound() using RNA.fold\_compound() with option RNA.OPTION\_WINDOW

\sphinxAtStartPar
The predicted structures are written on\sphinxhyphen{}the\sphinxhyphen{}fly, either to stdout, if a NULL pointer is passed as
file parameter, or to the corresponding filehandle.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as overloaded method \sphinxtitleref{mfe\_window()} to objects of type
\sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}. The parameter \sphinxtitleref{FILE} has default value of \sphinxtitleref{NULL} and can be omitted. See e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.mfe_window}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.mfe\_window()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

Apply a move to a secondary structure and indicate which neighbors have changed consequentially.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to RNA.move\_neighbor\_diff\_cb(), this function applies a move to a secondary structure and
reports back the neighbors of the current structure become affected by this move. Instead of
executing a callback for each of the affected neighbors, this function compiles two lists of
neighbor moves, one that is returned and consists of all moves that are novel or may have changed in
energy, and a second, \sphinxtitleref{invalid\_moves}, that consists of all the neighbor moves that become invalid,
respectively.

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{invalid\_moves}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.move() **}}) \textendash{} The address of a move list where the function stores those moves that become invalid

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

application of the move

Reset free energy parameters within a RNA.fold\_compound() according to provided, or default model
details.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function allows one to rescale free energy parameters for subsequent structure prediction or
evaluation according to a set of model details, e.g. temperature values. To do so, the caller
provides either a pointer to a set of model details to be used for rescaling, or NULL if global
default setting should be used.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When no parameter is passed to this method, the resulting action is the same as passing \sphinxtitleref{NULL}
as second parameter to RNA.fold\_compound.params\_reset(), i.e. global default model settings are
used. Passing
an object of type RNA.md() resets the fold compound according to the specifications stored
within the RNA.md() object. See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.params_reset}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.params\_reset()}}}}} in the

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute a path, store the final structure, and return a list of transition moves from the start to
the final structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function computes, given a start structure in pair table format, a transition path, updates the
pair table to the final structure of the path. Finally, if not requested otherwise by using the
RNA.PATH\_NO\_TRANSITION\_OUTPUT flag in the \sphinxtitleref{options} field, this function returns a list of
individual transitions that lead from the start to the final structure if requested.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The currently available transition paths are
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Steepest Descent / Gradient walk (flag: RNA.PATH\_STEEPEST\_DESCENT)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk (flag: RNA.PATH\_RANDOM)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The type of transitions must be set through the \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as an overloaded method \sphinxtitleref{path()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}.
The optional parameter \sphinxtitleref{options} defaults to RNA.PATH\_DEFAULT if it is omitted. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.path}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.path()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

execution of this function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

Determine an optimal direct (re\sphinxhyphen{})folding path between two secondary structures.

This function is similar to RNA.path\_direct(), but allows to specify an \sphinxstyleemphasis{upper\sphinxhyphen{}bound} for the
saddle point energy. The underlying algorithms will stop determining an (optimal) (re\sphinxhyphen{})folding path,
if none can be found that has a saddle point below the specified upper\sphinxhyphen{}bound threshold \sphinxtitleref{maxE}.

the optional parameter \sphinxtitleref{options} defaults to \sphinxtitleref{NULL}. In case the function did not find a path
with \(E_{saddle} < E_{max}\) it returns an empty list. See, e.g.

Sample a secondary structure from the Boltzmann ensemble according its probability.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a probabilistic (stochastic) backtracing in the partition function DP arrays to obtain a
secondary structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The structure \(s\) with free energy \(E(s)\) is picked from the Boltzmann distributed
ensemble according to its probability
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p(s) = \frac{exp(-E(s) / kT)}{Z}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with partition function \(Z = \sum_{s} exp(-E(s) / kT)\), Boltzmann constant \(k\) and
thermodynamic temperature \(T\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Sample a secondary structure of a subsequence from the Boltzmann ensemble according its probability.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Perform a probabilistic (stochastic) backtracing in the partition function DP arrays to obtain a
secondary structure. The parameters \sphinxtitleref{start} and \sphinxtitleref{end} specify the interval \([start:end]\) of
the subsequence with \(1 \leq start < end \leq n\) for sequence length \(n\), the
structure \(s_{start,end}\) should be drawn from.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The resulting substructure \(s_{start,end}\) with free energy \(E(s_{start, end})\) is
picked from the Boltzmann distributed sub ensemble of all structures within the interval
\([start:end]\) according to its probability
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p(s_{start,end}) = \frac{exp(-E(s_{start,end}) / kT)}{Z_{start,end}}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with partition function \(Z_{start,end} = \sum_{s_{start,end}} exp(-E(s_{start,end}) / kT)\),
Boltzmann constant \(k\) and thermodynamic temperature \(T\).
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Precondition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unique multiloop decomposition has to be active upon creation of \sphinxtitleref{fc} with RNA.fold\_compound()
or similar. This can be done easily by passing RNA.fold\_compound() a model details parameter
with RNA.md().uniq\_ML = 1.  RNA.fold\_compound.pf() has to be called first to fill the partition

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the partition function \(Q\) for a given RNA sequence, or sequence alignment.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If \sphinxstyleemphasis{structure} is not a NULL pointer on input, it contains on return a string consisting of the
letters “ . , | \{ \} ( ) “ denoting bases that are essentially unpaired, weakly paired, strongly
paired without preference, weakly upstream (downstream) paired, or strongly up\sphinxhyphen{} (down\sphinxhyphen{})stream paired
bases, respectively. If the model’s compute\_bpp is set to 0 base pairing probabilities will not be
computed (saving CPU time), otherwise after calculations took place pr will contain the probability
that bases \sphinxstyleemphasis{i} and \sphinxstyleemphasis{j} pair.

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.positional_entropy}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{positional\_entropy}}}{}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute a vector of positional entropies.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function computes the positional entropies from base pair probabilities as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}S(i) = - \sum_{j} p_{ij} \log(p_{ij}) - q_{i} \log(q_{i})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
with unpaired probabilities \(q_{i} = 1 - \sum_{j} p_{ij}\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Low entropy regions have little structural flexibility and the reliability of the predicted
structure is high. High entropy implies many structural alternatives. While these alternatives may
be functionally important, they make structure prediction more difficult and thus less reliable.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Precondition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function requires pre\sphinxhyphen{}computed base pair probabilities! Thus, RNA.fold\_compound.pf() must

\sphinxlineitem{be called}
\sphinxAtStartPar
beforehand.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{positional\_entropy()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}.
See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.positional_entropy}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.positional\_entropy()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\index{pr\_structure() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{pr\_structure()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.pr_structure}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{pr\_structure}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{structure}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the equilibrium probability of a particular secondary structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The probability \(p(s)\) of a particular secondary structure \(s\) can be computed as
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}p(s) = \frac{exp(-\beta E(s)}{Z}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
from the structures free energy \(E(s)\) and the partition function
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Z = \sum_{s} exp(-\beta E(s)),\quad\mathrm{with}\quad\beta = \frac{1}{RT}\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(R\) is the gas constant and \(T\) the thermodynamic temperature.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{Precondition}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The fold compound \sphinxtitleref{fc} must have went through a call to RNA.fold\_compound.pf() to fill the

\sphinxlineitem{dynamic}
\sphinxAtStartPar
programming matrices with the corresponding partition function.

\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{pr\_structure()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}. See,
e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.pr_structure}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.pr\_structure()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{rotational\_symmetry\_db() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{rotational\_symmetry\_db()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.rotational_symmetry_db}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{rotational\_symmetry\_db}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{structure}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Determine the order of rotational symmetry for a dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Given a (permutation of multiple) RNA strand(s) and a particular secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket
notation, compute the degree of rotational symmetry. In case there is only a single linear RNA
strand, the structure always has degree 1, as there are no rotational symmetries due to the
direction of the nucleic acid sequence and the fixed positions of 5’ and 3’ ends. However, for
circular RNAs, rotational symmetries might arise if the sequence consists of a concatenation of
\(k\) identical subsequences.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the argument \sphinxtitleref{positions} is not \sphinxtitleref{NULL}, the function stores an array of string start positions
for rotational shifts that map the string back onto itself. This array has length of order of
rotational symmetry, i.e. the number returned by this function. The first element \sphinxtitleref{positions\textasciigrave{}{[}0{]}
always contains a shift value of \textasciigrave{}0} representing the trivial rotation.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{rotational\_symmetry\_db()} to objects of type
\sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound} (i.e. RNA.fold\_compound()). Thus, the first argument must be omitted. In
contrast to our C\sphinxhyphen{}implementation, this function doesn’t simply return the order of rotational
symmetry of the secondary structure, but returns the list \sphinxtitleref{position} of cyclic permutation
shifts that result in a rotationally symmetric structure. The length of the list then determines
the order of rotational symmetry. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.rotational_symmetry_db}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.rotational\_symmetry\_db()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{structure}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket structure the degree of rotational symmetry is checked for

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{positions}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(list\sphinxhyphen{}like(unsigned int))}}) \textendash{} A pointer to an (undefined) list of alternative string start positions that lead to an identity
mapping (may be NULL)

\end{itemize}

\index{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_deigan() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_deigan()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_deigan}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{fold\_compound self}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{DoubleVector reactivities}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{double m}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{double b}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{unsigned int options=}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ int}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add SHAPE reactivity data as soft constraints (Deigan et al. method)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This approach of SHAPE directed RNA folding uses the simple linear ansatz
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Delta G_{\text{SHAPE}}(i) = m \ln(\text{SHAPE reactivity}(i)+1)+ b\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
to convert SHAPE reactivity values to pseudo energies whenever a nucleotide \(i\) contributes to
a stacked pair. A positive slope \(m\) penalizes high reactivities in paired regions, while a
negative intercept \(b\) results in a confirmatory {\color{red}\bfseries{}\textasciigrave{}}bonus’ free energy for correctly predicted
base pairs. Since the energy evaluation of a base pair stack involves two pairs, the pseudo energies
are added for all four contributing nucleotides. Consequently, the energy term is applied twice for
pairs inside a helix and only once for pairs adjacent to other structures. For all other loop types
the energy model remains unchanged even when the experimental data highly disagrees with a certain
motif.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_deigan()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}.
See, e.g.   {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.sc_add_SHAPE_deigan}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.sc\_add\_SHAPE\_deigan()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\end{description}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{reactivities}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const double *}}) \textendash{} A vector of normalized SHAPE reactivities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{m}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) \textendash{} The slope of the conversion function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{b}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) \textendash{} The intercept of the conversion function

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{options}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The options flag indicating how/where to store the soft constraints

\index{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_zarringhalam() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_zarringhalam()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.sc_add_SHAPE_zarringhalam}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_zarringhalam}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{fold\_compound self}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{DoubleVector reactivities}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{double b}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{double default\_value}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{char const * shape\_conversion}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{unsigned int options=}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ int}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add SHAPE reactivity data as soft constraints (Zarringhalam et al. method)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method first converts the observed SHAPE reactivity of nucleotide \(i\) into a probability
\(q_{i}\) that position \(i\) is unpaired by means of a non\sphinxhyphen{}linear map. Then pseudo\sphinxhyphen{}energies
of the form
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}\Delta G_{\text{SHAPE}}(x,i) = \beta\ |x_{i} - q_{i}|\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
are computed, where \(x_{i}=0\) if position \(i\) is unpaired and \(x_{i}=1\) if
\(i\) is paired in a given secondary structure. The parameter \(\beta\) serves as scaling
factor. The magnitude of discrepancy between prediction and experimental observation is represented
by \(|x_{i} - q_{i}|\).
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{sc\_add\_SHAPE\_zarringhalam()} to objects of type
\sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}. See, e.g.   {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.sc_add_SHAPE_zarringhalam}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.sc\_add\_SHAPE\_zarringhalam()}}}}} in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

Generate suboptimal structures within an energy band arround the MFE.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the most generic implementation of the suboptimal structure generator according to
Wuchty \sphinxstyleemphasis{et al.} {[}\hyperlink{cite.bibliography:id33}{1999}{]} . Identical to RNA.fold\_compound.subopt(), it computes all secondary structures within an
energy band \sphinxtitleref{delta} arround the MFE. However, this function does not print the resulting structures
and their corresponding free energies to a file pointer, or returns them as a list. Instead, it
calls a user\sphinxhyphen{}provided callback function which it passes the structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket format, the
corresponding free energy in kcal/mol, and a user\sphinxhyphen{}provided data structure each time a structure was
backtracked successfully. This function indicates the final output, i.e. the end of the backtracking
procedure by passing NULL instead of an actual dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket string to the callback.

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add an unstructured domain motif, e.g. for ligand binding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function adds a ligand binding motif and the associated binding free energy to the RNA.ud()
attribute of a RNA.fold\_compound(). The motif data will then be used in subsequent secondary
structure predictions. Multiple calls to this function with different motifs append all additional
data to a list of ligands, which all will be evaluated. Ligand motif data can be removed from the
RNA.fold\_compound() again using the RNA.fold\_compound.ud\_remove() function. The loop type parameter allows one
to limit the ligand binding to particular loop type, such as the exterior loop, hairpin loops,
interior loops, or multibranch loops.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{motif}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The sequence motif the ligand binds to

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{motif\_en}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{double}}) \textendash{} The binding free energy of the ligand in kcal/mol

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{motif\_name}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The name/id of the motif (may be \sphinxtitleref{NULL})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{loop\_type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The loop type the ligand binds to

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}
