\index{ud\_set\_prod\_rule\_cb() (RNA.fold\_compound method)@\spxentry{ud\_set\_prod\_rule\_cb()}\spxextra{RNA.fold\_compound method}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.ud_set_prod_rule_cb}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{ud\_set\_prod\_rule\_cb}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{fold\_compound self}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{PyObject * prod\_cb}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{PyObject * eval\_cb}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ PyObject *}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Attach production rule callbacks for free energies computations.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this function to bind a user\sphinxhyphen{}implemented grammar extension for unstructured domains.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The callback \sphinxtitleref{e\_cb} needs to evaluate the free energy contribution \(f(i,j)\) of the unpaired
segment \([i,j]\). It will be executed in each of the regular secondary structure production
rules. Whenever the callback is passed the RNA.UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_MOTIF flag via its \sphinxtitleref{loop\_type}
parameter the contribution of any ligand that consecutively binds from position \(i\) to
\(j\) (the white box) is requested. Otherwise, the callback usually performs a lookup in the
precomputed \sphinxtitleref{B} matrices. Which \sphinxtitleref{B} matrix is addressed will be indicated by the flags
RNA.UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_EXT\_LOOP,
RNA.UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_HP\_LOOPRNA.UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_INT\_LOOP, and
RNA.UNSTRUCTURED\_DOMAIN\_MB\_LOOP. As their names already imply, they specify exterior loops (\sphinxtitleref{F}
production rule), hairpin loops and interior loops (\sphinxtitleref{C} production rule), and multibranch loops (\sphinxtitleref{M}
and \sphinxtitleref{M1} production rule).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxtitleref{pre\_cb} callback will be executed as a pre\sphinxhyphen{}processing step right before the regular secondary
structure rules. Usually one would use this callback to fill the dynamic programming matrices \sphinxtitleref{U}
and preparations of the auxiliary data structure RNA.unstructured\_domain().data
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is attached as method \sphinxtitleref{ud\_set\_prod\_rule\_cb()} to objects of type \sphinxtitleref{fold\_compound}.
See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.ud_set_prod_rule_cb}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.ud\_set\_prod\_rule\_cb()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{pre\_cb}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.ud\_production}}) \textendash{} A pointer to a callback function for the \sphinxtitleref{B} production rule

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{e\_cb}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.ud}}) \textendash{} A pointer to a callback function for free energy evaluation

\end{itemize}

\index{get\_xy\_coordinates() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{get\_xy\_coordinates()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.get_xy_coordinates}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{get\_xy\_coordinates}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{char const * structure}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.COORDINATE}]{\sphinxcrossref{COORDINATE}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute nucleotide coordinates for secondary structure plot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function takes a secondary structure and computes X\sphinxhyphen{}Y coordinates for each nucleotide that then
can be used to create a structure plot. The parameter \sphinxtitleref{plot\_type} is used to select the underlying
layout algorithm. Currently, the following selections are provided:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.PLOT\_TYPE\_SIMPLE

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.PLOT\_TYPE\_NAVIEW

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.PLOT\_TYPE\_CIRCULAR

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.PLOT\_TYPE\_TURTLE

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNA.PLOT\_TYPE\_PUZZLER

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Passing an unsupported selection leads to the default algorithm RNA.PLOT\_TYPE\_NAVIEW

\sphinxAtStartPar
Here is a simple example how to use this function, assuming variable \sphinxtitleref{structure} contains a valid
dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket string:
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{structure}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{x}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float **}}) \textendash{} The address of a pointer of X coordinates (pointer will point to memory, or NULL on failure)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{y}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float **}}) \textendash{} The address of a pointer of Y coordinates (pointer will point to memory, or NULL on failure)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{plot\_type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The layout algorithm to be used

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The length of the structure on success, 0 otherwise

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}

\end{description}\end{quote}


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_coords\_pt}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_coords\_simple}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_coords\_naview}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_coords\_circular}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_coords\_turtle}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_coords\_puzzler}}


\end{sphinxseealso}


\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
On success, this function allocates memory for X and Y coordinates and assigns the pointers at
addressess \sphinxtitleref{x} and \sphinxtitleref{y} to the corresponding memory locations. It’s the users responsibility to
cleanup this memory after usage!
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{hc (class in RNA)@\spxentry{hc}\spxextra{class in RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.hc}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{hc}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The hard constraints data structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The content of this data structure determines the decomposition pattern used in the folding
recursions. Attribute ‘matrix’ is used as source for the branching pattern of the decompositions
during all folding recursions. Any entry in matrix{[}i,j{]} consists of the 6 LSB that allows one to
distinguish the following types of base pairs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
in the exterior loop (RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_EXT\_LOOP)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosing a hairpin (RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_HP\_LOOP)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosing an interior loop (RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosed by an exterior loop (RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP\_ENC)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosing a multi branch loop (RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
enclosed by a multi branch loop (RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP\_ENC)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The four linear arrays ‘up\_xxx’ provide the number of available unpaired nucleotides (including
position i) 3’ of each position in the sequence.

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.fold_compound.hc_init}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.fold\_compound.hc\_init}}}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.hc\_free}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_EXT\_LOOP}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_HP\_LOOP}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_INT\_LOOP}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.CONSTRAINT\_CONTEXT\_MB\_LOOP\_ENC}}

\index{heat\_capacity() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{heat\_capacity()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.heat_capacity}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{heat\_capacity}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{sequence}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{T\_min}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{T\_max}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{100.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{T\_increment}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{1.0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{mpoints}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{2}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the specific heat for an RNA (simplified variant)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Similar to RNA.fold\_compound.heat\_capacity(), this function computes an RNAs specific heat in a given temperature
range from the partition function by numeric differentiation. This simplified version, however, only
requires the RNA sequence as input instead of a RNA.fold\_compound() data structure. The result is
returned as a list of pairs of temperature in C and specific heat in Kcal/(Mol*K).

\sphinxAtStartPar
Users can specify the temperature range for the computation from \sphinxtitleref{T\_min} to \sphinxtitleref{T\_max}, as well as the
increment step size \sphinxtitleref{T\_increment}. The latter also determines how many times the partition function
is computed. Finally, the parameter \sphinxtitleref{mpoints} determines how smooth the curve should be. The
algorithm itself fits a parabola to \(2 \cdot mpoints + 1\) data points to calculate 2nd
derivatives. Increasing this parameter produces a smoother curve.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as overloaded function \sphinxtitleref{heat\_capacity()}. If the optional function
arguments \sphinxtitleref{T\_min}, \sphinxtitleref{T\_max}, \sphinxtitleref{T\_increment}, and \sphinxtitleref{mpoints} are omitted, they default to 0.0,
100.0, 1.0 and 2, respectively. See, e.g.  \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.head\_capacity()}} in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sequence}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The RNA sequence input (must be uppercase)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{T\_min}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Lowest temperature in C

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{T\_max}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Highest temperature in C

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{T\_increment}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Stepsize for temperature incrementation in C (a reasonable choice might be 1C)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mpoints}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The number of interpolation points to calculate 2nd derivative (a reasonable choice might be 2,
min: 1, max: 100)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of pairs of temperatures and corresponding heat capacity or \sphinxstyleemphasis{NULL} upon any failure. The
last entry of the list is indicated by a \sphinxstylestrong{temperature} field set to a value smaller than
\sphinxtitleref{T\_min}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.heat\_capacity() *}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{inverse\_fold() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{inverse\_fold()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{inverse\_fold}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{char * start}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{char const * target}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ char *}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find sequences with predefined structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function searches for a sequence with minimum free energy structure provided in the parameter
‘target’, starting with sequence ‘start’. It returns 0 if the search was successful, otherwise a
structure distance in terms of the energy difference between the search result and the actual target
‘target’ is returned. The found sequence is returned in ‘start’. If give\_up is set to 1, the
function will return as soon as it is clear that the search will be unsuccessful, this speeds up the
algorithm if you are only interested in exact solutions.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{start}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The start sequence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{target}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The target secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The distance to the target in case a search was unsuccessful, 0 otherwise

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find sequence that maximizes probability of a predefined structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function searches for a sequence with maximum probability to fold into the provided structure
‘target’ using the partition function algorithm. It returns \(-kT \cdot \log(p)\) where
\(p\) is the frequency of ‘target’ in the ensemble of possible structures. This is usually much
slower than inverse\_fold().

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{target}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The target secondary structure in dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket notation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{dangles (RNA.md attribute)@\spxentry{dangles}\spxextra{RNA.md attribute}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.md.dangles}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysigline{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{dangles}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Specifies the dangle model used in any energy evaluation (0,1,2 or 3)

\sphinxAtStartPar
If set to 0 no stabilizing energies are assigned to bases adjacent to helices in free ends and
multiloops (so called dangling ends). Normally (dangles = 1) dangling end energies are assigned
only to unpaired bases and a base cannot participate simultaneously in two dangling ends. In the
partition function algorithm RNA.fold\_compound.pf() these checks are neglected. To provide comparability
between free energy minimization and partition function algorithms, the default setting is 2.
This treatment of dangling ends gives more favorable energies to helices directly adjacent to
one another, which can be beneficial since such helices often do engage in stabilizing
interactions through co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking.
If set to 3 co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking is explicitly included for adjacent helices in multiloops. The
option affects only mfe folding and energy evaluation (RNA.mfe() and RNA.eval\_structure()), as
well as suboptimal folding (RNA.subopt()) via re\sphinxhyphen{}evaluation of energies. Co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking with
one intervening mismatch is not considered so far. Note, that some function do not implement all
dangle model but only a subset of (0,1,2,3). In particular, partition function algorithms can
only handle 0 and 2. Read the documentation of the particular recurrences or energy evaluation
function for information about the provided dangle model.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}

\index{move (class in RNA)@\spxentry{move}\spxextra{class in RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.move}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{class\DUrole{w}{ }}}\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{move}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{pos\_5}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{pos\_3}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{0}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Bases: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{object}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
An atomic representation of the transition / move from one structure to its neighbor.

\sphinxAtStartPar
An atomic transition / move may be one of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a \sphinxstylestrong{base pair insertion},

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a \sphinxstylestrong{base pair removal}, or

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
a \sphinxstylestrong{base pair shift} where an existing base pair changes one of its pairing partner.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
These moves are encoded by two integer values that represent the affected 5’ and 3’ nucleotide
positions. Furthermore, we use the following convention on the signedness of these encodings:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
both values are positive for \sphinxstyleemphasis{insertion moves}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
both values are negative for \sphinxstyleemphasis{base pair removals}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
both values have different signedness for \sphinxstyleemphasis{shift moves}, where the positive value indicates the
nucleotide that stays constant, and the others absolute value is the new pairing partner

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A value of 0 in either field is used as list\sphinxhyphen{}end indicator and doesn’t represent any valid move.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compare two moves.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The function compares two moves \sphinxtitleref{m} and \sphinxtitleref{b} and returns whether move \sphinxtitleref{m} is lexicographically
smaller (\sphinxhyphen{}1), larger (1) or equal to move \sphinxtitleref{b}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If any of the moves \sphinxtitleref{m} or \sphinxtitleref{b} is a shift move, this comparison only makes sense in a structure
context. Thus, the third argument with the current structure must be provided.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{b}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const RNA.move() *}}) \textendash{} The second move of the comparison

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{pt}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{const short *}}) \textendash{} The pair table of the current structure that is compatible with both moves (maybe NULL if moves
are guaranteed to be no shifts)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxhyphen{}1 if \sphinxtitleref{m} \textless{} \sphinxtitleref{b}, 1 if \sphinxtitleref{m} \textgreater{} \sphinxtitleref{b}, 0 otherwise

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{warning}{Warning:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, shift moves are not supported!
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function returns 0 (equality) upon any error, e.g. missing input
\end{sphinxadmonition}

parameter \sphinxtitleref{width} specifies the width of the breadth\sphinxhyphen{}first search while the second parameter \sphinxtitleref{type}
allows one to set the type of the returned (re\sphinxhyphen{})folding path.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently, the following return types are available:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of dot\sphinxhyphen{}bracket structures and corresponding free energy (flag:
RNA.PATH\_TYPE\_DOT\_BRACKET)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of transition moves and corresponding free energy changes (flag: RNA.PATH\_TYPE\_MOVES)

\end{itemize}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as overloaded function \sphinxtitleref{path\_options\_findpath()}. The optional
parameter \sphinxtitleref{width} defaults to 10 if omitted, while the optional parameter \sphinxtitleref{type} defaults to
RNA.PATH\_TYPE\_DOT\_BRACKET. See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.path_options_findpath}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.path\_options\_findpath()}}}}} in the
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{type}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} Setting that specifies how the return (re\sphinxhyphen{})folding path should be encoded

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute base pair probabilities using a sliding\sphinxhyphen{}window approach.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a simplified wrapper to RNA.fold\_compound.probs\_window() that given a nucleid acid sequence, a window
size, a maximum base pair span, and a cutoff value computes the pair probabilities for any base pair
in any window. The pair probabilities are returned as a list and the user has to take care to free()
the memory occupied by the list.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sequence}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The nucleic acid input sequence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{window\_size}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The size of the sliding window

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_bp\_span}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The maximum distance along the backbone between two nucleotides that form a base pairs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{cutoff}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} A cutoff value that omits all pairs with lower probability

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A list of base pair probabilities, terminated by an entry with RNA.ep().i and RNA.ep().j set
to 0

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.ep() *}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{pfl\_fold\_up() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{pfl\_fold\_up()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.pfl_fold_up}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{pfl\_fold\_up}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{std::string sequence}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{int ulength}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{int window\_size}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{int max\_bp\_span}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.DoubleDoubleVector}]{\sphinxcrossref{DoubleDoubleVector}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute probability of contiguous unpaired segments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a simplified wrapper to RNA.fold\_compound.probs\_window() that given a nucleic acid sequence, a maximum
length of unpaired segments (\sphinxtitleref{ulength}), a window size, and a maximum base pair span computes the
equilibrium probability of any segment not exceeding \sphinxtitleref{ulength}. The probabilities to be unpaired are
returned as a 1\sphinxhyphen{}based, 2\sphinxhyphen{}dimensional matrix with dimensions \(N \times M\), where \(N\) is
the length of the sequence and \(M\) is the maximum segment length. As an example, the
probability of a segment of size 5 starting at position 100 is stored in the matrix entry
\(X[100][5]\).

\sphinxAtStartPar
It is the users responsibility to free the memory occupied by this matrix.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{sequence}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The nucleic acid input sequence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ulength}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The maximal length of an unpaired segment

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{window\_size}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The size of the sliding window

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_bp\_span}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} The maximum distance along the backbone between two nucleotides that form a base pairs

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The probabilities to be unpaired for any segment not exceeding \sphinxtitleref{ulength}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(list\sphinxhyphen{}like(double))}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function uses default model settings! For custom model settings, we refer to the function
RNA.fold\_compound.probs\_window().
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}

secondary structure) and produces an EPS “dot plot” with filename \sphinxtitleref{‘filename’} where data from
\sphinxtitleref{upper} is placed in the upper\sphinxhyphen{}triangular and data from \sphinxtitleref{lower} is placed in the lower triangular
part of the matrix.
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For default output, provide the flag RNA.PLOT\_PROBABILITIES\_DEFAULT as \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter.
\end{quote}

parameters may be omitted. The default values for these parameters are \sphinxtitleref{lower} = NULL, \sphinxtitleref{auxdata}
= NULL, \sphinxtitleref{options} = RNA.PLOT\_PROBABILITIES\_DEFAULT. See, e.g.  {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.plot_dp_EPS}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.plot\_dp\_EPS()}}}}} in

\index{rotational\_symmetry() (in module RNA)@\spxentry{rotational\_symmetry()}\spxextra{in module RNA}}

\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{api_python:RNA.rotational_symmetry}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{rotational\_symmetry}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{o}{*}\DUrole{n}{args}}}{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Determine the order of rotational symmetry for a NULL\sphinxhyphen{}terminated string of ASCII characters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The algorithm applies a fast search of the provided string within itself, assuming the end of the
string wraps around to connect with it’s start. For example, a string of the form \sphinxtitleref{AABAAB} has
rotational symmetry of order \sphinxtitleref{2}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If the argument \sphinxtitleref{positions} is not \sphinxtitleref{NULL}, the function stores an array of string start positions
for rotational shifts that map the string back onto itself. This array has length of order of
rotational symmetry, i.e. the number returned by this function. The first element \sphinxtitleref{positions\textasciigrave{}{[}0{]}
always contains a shift value of \textasciigrave{}0} representing the trivial rotation.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This function is available as overloaded global function \sphinxtitleref{rotational\_symmetry()}. It merges the
functionalities of RNA.rotational\_symmetry(), RNA.rotational\_symmetry\_pos(),
RNA.rotational\_symmetry\_num(), and RNA.rotational\_symmetry\_pos\_num(). In contrast to our
C\sphinxhyphen{}implementation, this function doesn’t return the order of rotational symmetry as a single
value, but returns a list of cyclic permutation shifts that result in a rotationally symmetric
string. The length of the list then determines the order of rotational symmetry. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.rotational_symmetry}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.rotational\_symmetry()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}} .

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{string}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} A NULL\sphinxhyphen{}terminated string of characters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{positions}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{list\sphinxhyphen{}like(list\sphinxhyphen{}like(unsigned int))}}) \textendash{} A pointer to an (undefined) list of alternative string start positions that lead to an identity
mapping (may be NULL)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The order of rotational symmetry

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{strtrim}}}{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{char * seq\_mutable}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{char const * delimiters=None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{unsigned int keep=0}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{unsigned int options=}}}{{ $\rightarrow$ unsigned int}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Trim a string by removing (multiple) occurences of a particular character.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function removes (multiple) consecutive occurences of a set of characters (\sphinxtitleref{delimiters}) within
an input string. It may be used to remove leading and/or trailing whitespaces or to restrict the
maximum number of consecutive occurences of the delimiting characters \sphinxtitleref{delimiters}. Setting \sphinxtitleref{keep=0}
removes all occurences, while other values reduce multiple consecutive occurences to at most \sphinxtitleref{keep}
delimiters. This might be useful if one would like to reduce multiple whitespaces to a single one,
or to remove empty fields within a comma\sphinxhyphen{}separated value string.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The parameter \sphinxtitleref{delimiters} may be a pointer to a 0\sphinxhyphen{}terminated char string containing a set of any
ASCII character. If \sphinxstyleemphasis{NULL} is passed as delimiter set or an empty char string, all whitespace
characters are trimmed. The \sphinxtitleref{options} parameter is a bit vector that specifies which part of the
string should undergo trimming. The implementation distinguishes the leading (RNA.TRIM\_LEADING),
trailing (RNA.TRIM\_TRAILING), and in\sphinxhyphen{}between (RNA.TRIM\_IN\_BETWEEN) part with respect to the
delimiter set. Combinations of these parts can be specified by using logical\sphinxhyphen{}or operator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The following example code removes all leading and trailing whitespace characters from the input
string:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{\sphinxstylestrong{SWIG Wrapper Notes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since many scripting languages treat strings as immutable objects, this function does not modify
the input string directly. Instead, it returns the modified string as second return value,
together with the number of removed delimiters.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The scripting language interface provides an overloaded version of this function, with default
parameters \sphinxtitleref{delimiters=NULL}, \sphinxtitleref{keep=0}, and \sphinxtitleref{options=RNA.TRIM\_DEFAULT}. See, e.g.
{\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python:RNA.strtrim}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.strtrim()}}}}} in the {\hyperref[\detokenize{api_python::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Python API}}}}.

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{string}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The ‘0’\sphinxhyphen{}terminated input string to trim

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{delimiters}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{string}}) \textendash{} The delimiter characters as 0\sphinxhyphen{}terminated char array (or \sphinxstyleemphasis{NULL})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{keep}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The maximum number of consecutive occurences of the delimiter in the output string

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{options}} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{unsigned int}}) \textendash{} The option bit vector specifying the mode of operation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The number of delimiters removed from the string

\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.TRIM\_LEADING}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.TRIM\_TRAILING}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.TRIM\_IN\_BETWEEN}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.TRIM\_SUBST\_BY\_FIRST}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.TRIM\_DEFAULT}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{RNA.TRIM\_ALL}}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The delimiter always consists of a single character from the set of characters provided. In case of

\chapter{News}
\label{\detokenize{news:news}}\label{\detokenize{news::doc}}

\section{Version 2.6.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-6-0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This version introduces modified nucleotides support and a physics\sphinxhyphen{}based model to
correct for predictions at non\sphinxhyphen{}standard (monovalent) salt concentrations.
At this time we include publically available energy parameters for inosine,
pseudouridine, m6A, 7DA, and purine (a.k.a. nebularine). In addition, we add
stacking parameters for dihydrouridine as predicted by Rosetta/RECESS.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the Changelog for version 2.6.0 for a complete list of new features and bugfixes.


\section{Version 2.5.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-5-0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The all new release of version 2.5 brings multi\sphinxhyphen{}strand interaction prediction! The
new executable tool RNAmultifold is the successor of the RNA\sphinxhyphen{}RNA dimer interaction
prediction tool RNAcofold and effectively lifts the restriction to just two interacting
strands. It follows the same principle of concatenating the RNA strands that shall
form a complex and then predicts MFE and partition function. Along with that, it can
also compute equilibrium concentrations of the complexes formed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the Changelog for version 2.5.0 for a complete list of additions, novel features
and fixed bugs.


\section{Version 2.4.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-4-0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
With version 2.4 sliding\sphinxhyphen{}window structure prediction receives the constraint framework!
Starting with this version, the sliding\sphinxhyphen{}window secondary structure prediction implementations
as available through RNALfold, RNAplfold, and RNALalifold are constraints\sphinxhyphen{}aware. Thus, they
can readily incorporate RNA structure probing data, such as from SHAPE experiments, etc.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the Changelog for version 2.4.0 for a complete list of new features and bugfixes.


\section{Version 2.3.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-3-0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This version introduces the unstructured domain extension of the RNA folding grammar! This
extension adds RNA\sphinxhyphen{}ligand interactions, e.g. RNA\sphinxhyphen{}protein, for unpaired stretches in RNA
secondary structures. The feature is easy to use through the command file interface in RNAfold.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the Changelog for version 2.3.0 for a complete list of new features and bugfixes.


\section{Version 2.2.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-2-0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
After almost a year without a new release, we are happy to announce many new features. This
version officially introduces (generic) hard\sphinxhyphen{} and soft\sphinxhyphen{}constraints for many of the folding
algorithms. Thus, chemical probing constraints, such as derived from SHAPE experiments, can
be easily incorporated into RNAfold, RNAalifold, and RNAsubopt. Furthermore, RNAfold and the
RNAlib interface allow for a simple way to incorporate ligand binding to specific hairpin\sphinxhyphen{} or
interior\sphinxhyphen{}loop motifs. This version also introduces the new v3.0 API of the RNAlib C\sphinxhyphen{}library,
that will eventually replace the current interface in the future.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the Changelog for version 2.2.0 for a complete list of new features and bugfixes.


\section{Version 2.1.9}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-1-9}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is a major bugfix release that changes the way how the ViennaRNA Package handles
dangling end and terminal mismatch contributions for exterior\sphinxhyphen{}, and multibranch loops. We strongly
recommend upgrading your installation to this or a newer version to obtain predictions that are
better comparable to RNAstructure or UNAFold.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please see the Changelog for version 2.1.9 for further details on the actual changes to the
underlying energy parameters.


\section{Version 2.1.7}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-1-7}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a long time, Mac OS X users were not able to correctly build the Perl/Python interface of the
ViennaRNA Package. Starting with v2.1.7, this limitation has been removed, and the interface should
compile and work as expected.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please see the Install Notes for Mac OS X users for further details.


\section{Version 2.1.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-1-0}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Since ViennaRNA Package Version 2.1.0 we have enabled G\sphinxhyphen{}Quadruplex prediction support into
RNAfold, RNAcofold, RNALfold, RNAalifold, RNAeval and RNAplot.

\sphinxAtStartPar
See the changelog for details.


\section{Older news}
\label{\detokenize{news:older-news}}

\section{Version 2.0}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-2-0}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Meanwhile, a lot of changes in the RNAlib have accumulated. See the Reference
Manual and the Changelog for further details

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All algorithms use the Turner’04 nearest neighbor model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The RNAlib provides (OpenMP) threadsafe folding routines per default. This is
enables concurrent calls to the folding routines in parallel. The feature
can be disabled by passing ‘\textendash{}disable\sphinxhyphen{}openmp’ to the configure script

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
serious changes in command line parameters. Everything complies with
GNU standard from now on (short options with preceding ‘\sphinxhyphen{}’, long options
with preceding ‘\textendash{}‘.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
FASTA file support for RNAfold. RNA sequences do not need to be passed
on a single line anymore when a FASTA header is provided.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new program RNA2Dfold computes MFE, partition function and
stochastically sampled secondary structures in a partitioning of the secondary
structure space according to the base pair distance to two reference structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new program PKplex computes…

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new program RNALfoldz computes locally stable secondary structures
together with a z\sphinxhyphen{}score

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new program RNALalifold computes locally stable consensus structures for
alignments

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new program RNAparconv enables the conversion of ‘old’ energy parameter files
(v1.4\sphinxhyphen{}v1.8) to the new format used in version 2.x

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.8}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-8}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
new RNAalifold has better treatment of gaps and ribosum based covariance
scores. Use the \sphinxhyphen{}old switch for compatibility with older RNAalifold
versions.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAplfold \sphinxhyphen{}u  now computes all accessibilities up to a maximum length
(much faster than computing each individually)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ATTENTION: output formats of RNAplfold \sphinxhyphen{}u and or RNAup have been changed\\
Programs parsing RNAplfold and RNAup output will have to be modified.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAfold and RNAalifold compute centroid structures when run with \sphinxhyphen{}p
use the  \sphinxhyphen{}MEA  option to compute Maximum Expected Accuracy structures.

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.7}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-7}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAplfold can now be used to compute accessibilities, i.e. the
probability that a stretch of the RNA remains unpaired (and thus
available for intermolecular interactions).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A new version of RNAup predicts RNA\sphinxhyphen{}RNA interactions takeing into account
the competition between inter\sphinxhyphen{} and intramolecular structure in both
molcules

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Circular RNAs can be treated by RNAfold, RNAalifold, RNAsubopt, and RNAcofold

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAaliduplex predicts RNA\sphinxhyphen{}RNA interactions between two sets of aligned
sequences (inter\sphinxhyphen{}molecular structure only)

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.6}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-6}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The RNAforester program for tree\sphinxhyphen{}alignments of RNA structures is now
distributed with the Vienna RNA package, see the RNAforester
subdirectory for more information. RNAforester was written by Matthias
Hoechsmann \sphinxhref{mailto:mhoechsm@techfak.uni-bielefeld.de}{mhoechsm@techfak.uni\sphinxhyphen{}bielefeld.de}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The Kinfold program for stochastic simulation of folding trajectories is
now included in the package, see the Kinfold subdirectory.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
cofolding of two structures now supports suboptimal folding and
partition function folding.
ATTENTION: Energies of hybrid structures now include the Duplex\sphinxhyphen{}initiation
energy, which was neglected in previous version.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAplfold is a partition function variant of RNALfold. It computes the
mean probability of a (local) base pair averaged over all sequence
windows that contain the pair.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
new utilities to color alignments and consensus structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAfold \sphinxhyphen{}p now computes the centroid structure

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ATTENTION: ensemble diversities in version \textless{}1.6.5 are off by a factor 2

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.5pre}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-5pre}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
ViennaRNA now uses autoconfig generated configure scripts for even better
portability (should compile on any UNIX, Linux, MacOS X, Windows with
Cygwin).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The new RNAalifold program predicts consensus structures for a set of
aligned sequences.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Complete suboptimal folding is now integrated in the library.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Beginning support for co\sphinxhyphen{}folding of two strands: energy\_of\_struct() and
RNAeval can now compute energies of duplex structures.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAcofold predicts hybrid structures of two RNA strands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAduplex predicts hybrid structures, while allowing only inter\sphinxhyphen{}molecular
base pairs (useful for finding potential binding sites)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNALfold predicts locally stable structures in long sequences.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Major changes to Perl module. See the pod documentation (perldoc RNA).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAsubopt can do stochastic backtracking to produce samples of suboptimal
structures with Boltzmann statistics.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
New utilities to rotate secondary structure plots and annotate them with
reliability data.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Various small bug fixes

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.4}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-4}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
New Turner parameters as described in Mathews et.al. JMB v288, 1999.
Small changes to format of parameter files (old param files won’t work!)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mfe and suboptimal folding will produce only structures without isolated
pairs if noLonelyPairs=1 (\sphinxhyphen{}noLP option), for partition function folding
pairs that can only occur as isolated pairs are not formed.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
setting dangles=3 (\sphinxhyphen{}d3 option) will allow co\sphinxhyphen{}axial stacking of adjacent
helices in mfe folding and energy\_of\_struct().

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.3.1}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-3-1}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAheat would produce spikes in the specific heat because dangling end
energies did not go smoothly to 0.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
PS dot plots now have an option to use a log scale (edit \_dp.ps file
and set logscale to true).

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.3}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-3}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Secondary structure plots now use E. Bruccoleri’s naview routines for
layout by default. New utility RNAplot produces secondary structure plots
from structures in bracket notation with several options.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
New \sphinxhyphen{}d2 option in RNAfold and RNAeval sets dangles=2, which makes
energy\_of\_struct() and fold() treat dangling ends as in pf\_fold().
\sphinxhyphen{}noLP option in RNAfold etc sets noLonelyPairs=1, which avoids most
structures containing lonely base pairs (helices of length 1).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
new utility functions pack\_structure() unpack\_structure() make\_pair\_table()
and bp\_distance().  RNAdistance adds bp\_distance() via \sphinxhyphen{}DP switch.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
First release of RNAsubopt for complete suboptimal folding.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
fixed bug in asymmetry penalty for interior loops.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default compilation now uses doubles for partition function folding.

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.2.1}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-2-1}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Fixed bug in version 1.2 of the RNAheat program causing overflow errors
for most input sequences.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The PS\_dot\_plot() and PS\_rna\_plot() routines now return an int. The return
value is 0 if the file could not be written, 1 otherwise.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This version contains the alpha version of a perl5 module, which let’s you
access all the capabilities of the Vienna RNA library from perl scripts.

\end{itemize}


\section{Version 1.2}
\label{\detokenize{news:version-1-2}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
New energy parameters from (Walter et.al 1994).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Energy parameters can be read from file.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
RNAeval and energy\_of\_struct() support logarithmic energy function for
multi\sphinxhyphen{}loops.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
gmlRNA() produces secondary structure drawing in gml (Graph Meta Language).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Many bug fixes.

\end{itemize}

\chapter{How to cite the ViennaRNA Package}
\label{\detokenize{citing:how-to-cite-the-viennarna-package}}\label{\detokenize{citing::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If you use our software and implemented algorithms for your scientific work, you might
want to cite the corresponding publications.


\section{Main References}
\label{\detokenize{citing:main-references}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstyleemphasis{overarching} main publications for the ViennaRNA Package are:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ronny Lorenz, Stephan H. Bernhart, Christian Höner zu Siederdissen, Hakim Tafer, Christoph Flamm, Peter F. Stadler, and Ivo L. Hofacker. ViennaRNA package 2.0. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Algorithms for Molecular Biology}, 6(1):26, 2011. \sphinxhref{https://doi.org/10.1186/1748-7188-6-26}{doi:10.1186/1748\sphinxhyphen{}7188\sphinxhyphen{}6\sphinxhyphen{}26}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
I.L. Hofacker, W. Fontana, P.F. Stadler, L.S. Bonhoeffer, M. Tacker, and P. Schuster. Fast folding and comparison of RNA secondary structures. \sphinxstyleemphasis{Monatshefte für Chemie/Chemical Monthly}, 125(2):167\textendash{}188, 1994. URL: \sphinxurl{https://www.academia.edu/download/48689421/Fast\_Folding\_and\_Comparison\_of\_RNA\_Secon20160908-13624-1yg70az.pdf}.

\end{itemize}


\section{Particular Algorithms and Features}
\label{\detokenize{citing:particular-algorithms-and-features}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To reference particular algorithms used in our sofware, you might want to consider citing
the following publications:


\subsection{Consensus structure prediction}
\label{\detokenize{citing:consensus-structure-prediction}}\begin{itemize}

\chapter{Frequently Asked Questions}
\label{\detokenize{faq:frequently-asked-questions}}\label{\detokenize{faq::doc}}

\section{Missing EXTERN.h}
\label{\detokenize{faq:missing-extern-h}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When compiling from source at the Mac OS X platform, users often encounter
an error message stating that the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTERN.h}} is missing for compilation
of the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Perl 5}} wrapper. This is a known problem and due to the fact that
users are discouraged to use the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Perl 5}} interpreter that is shipped with Mac OS X.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Instead, one should install a more recent version from another source, e.g. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{homebrew}}.
If, however, for any reason you do not want to install your own \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Perl 5}} interpreter
but use the one from Apple, you need to specify its include path to enable building the
ViennaRNA Perl interface. Otherwise, the file \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTERN.h}} will be missing at compile time.
To fix this problem, you first need to find out where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{EXTERN.h}} is located:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }find\PYG{+w}{ }/Library\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }f\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}name\PYG{+w}{ }EXTERN.h
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Then choose the one that corresponds to your default perl interpreter (find out the version
number with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{perl \sphinxhyphen{}v | grep version}}), simply execute the following before running the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./configure}} script, e.g.:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{export} \PYG{n}{CPATH}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{Library}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{Developer}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{CommandLineTools}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{SDKs}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{MacOSX10}\PYG{l+m+mf}{.15}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{sdk}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{System}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{Library}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{Perl}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{l+m+mf}{5.18}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{darwin}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{thread}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{n}{multi}\PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{n}{level}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n}{CORE}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
if your default perl is v5.18 running on MacOSX10.15. Change the paths according to your
current setup. After that, running \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{./configure}} and compilation should run fine.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{See also…}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Related question at stackoverflow: \sphinxurl{https://stackoverflow.com/q/52682304/18609162}
\end{sphinxadmonition}


\section{Linking fails with LTO error}
\label{\detokenize{faq:linking-fails-with-lto-error}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
By default, \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib} is compiled with {\hyperref[\detokenize{configuration:link-time-optimization}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Link Time Optimization}}}}.
This may introduce problems upon linking a third\sphinxhyphen{}party program that was either compiled
with a different compiler or compiler version. As a work\sphinxhyphen{}around solution, we include the
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}fno\sphinxhyphen{}lto}} linker flag in the output of the {\hyperref[\detokenize{linking:the-pkg-config-tool}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{pkg\sphinxhyphen{}config}}}}.
This tells the linker to not perform link time optimization even though LTO code is
included in the library. Usually, this should not affect the runtime of the algorithms
too much.

\sphinxAtStartPar
However, some linkers may not support the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}fno\sphinxhyphen{}lto}} flag and fail at the linker stage.
In addition, if \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib} has been compiled with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clang}}, it may not include the non\sphinxhyphen{}LTO
code required for linking without LTO. To resolve this issue, you may need to deactivate
link time optimization while building \sphinxstyleemphasis{RNAlib}.

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{See also…}

\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{configuration:link-time-optimization}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{std,std-ref}{Link Time Optimization}}}}
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\sphinxstepscope

\section{General Remarks}
\label{\detokenize{contributing:general-remarks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The ViennaRNA Package is developed by humans and consequently may contain bugs that
prevent proper operation of the implemented algorithms. If you think you have found
any of those nasty animals, please help us to improve our software by {\hyperref[\detokenize{contributing:reporting-bugs}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{xref,myst}{reporting the
bug}}}} to us.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The ViennaRNA Package also is open\sphinxhyphen{}source software, which means that everybody can
have a closer look into our implementations to understand and potentially extend
it’s functionality. If you implemented any novel feature into the ViennaRNA
Package that might be of interest to a larger community, please don’t hesitate to ask
for merging of your code into our official source tree. See the {\hyperref[\detokenize{contributing:pull-request-process}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{xref,myst}{Pull Request Process
section}}}} below to find information on how to do that.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Please note that we have a code of conduct. Please follow it in all your interactions
with this project.

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you wish to contribute to this project, please first discuss any proposed changes
with the owners and main developers. You may do that either through making an issue
at \sphinxhref{https://github.com/ViennaRNA/ViennaRNA}{our official GitHub presence},
\sphinxhref{mailto:rna@tbi.univie.ac.at}{by email}, or any other personal communication with the
core developer team.

\sphinxAtStartPar
More importantly, if you wish to contribute any files or software, you need to agree
to our ViennaRNA Package Contributors License Agreement (CLA)! Otherwise, your
contributions can’t be merged into our source tree. {\hyperref[\detokenize{contributing:contributors-license-agreement}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{xref,myst}{See below}}}}
for further information and the full CLA details.


\section{Reporting Bugs}
\label{\detokenize{contributing:reporting-bugs}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Please make an issue at GitHub or notify us by emailing to rna@tbi.univie.ac.at

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
In your report, include as much information as possible, such that we are able
to reproduce it. If possible, find a minimal example that triggers the bug.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Include the version number for the ViennaRNA Package you experience the bug with.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Include at least some minimal information regarding your operating system (Linux,
Mac OS X, Windows, etc.)

\end{enumerate}


\section{Pull Request Process}
\label{\detokenize{contributing:pull-request-process}}\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensure that you have not checked\sphinxhyphen{}in any files that are automatically build!

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When contributing C source code, follow our code formatting guide lines. You
may use the tool \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{uncrustify}} together with our config located in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{misc/uncrustify.cfg}}
to accomplish that.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Only expose symbols (functions, variables, etc.) to the libraries interface that are
absolutely necessary! Hide all other symbols in the corresponding object file(s) by
declaring them as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{static}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the prefixes \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{vrna\_}} for any symbol you add to the API of our library! Preprocessor
macros in header files require the prefix in capital letters, i.e. \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{VRNA\_}}.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use C\sphinxhyphen{}style comments at any place necessary to make sure your implementation can still
be understood and followed in the future.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add test cases for any new implementation! The test suite is located in the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{tests}}
directory and is split into tests for the C\sphinxhyphen{}library, executable programs, and the
individual scripting language interfaces.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Run \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{make check}} to ensure that all other test suites still run properly with your
applied changes!

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When contributing via GitHub, make a personal fork of our project and create a separate
branch for your changes. Then make a pull request to our \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user\sphinxhyphen{}contrib}} branch.
Pull requests to the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{master}} branch will be rejected to keep its history clean.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pull requests that have been successfully merged into the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{user\sphinxhyphen{}contrib}} branch
usually find their way into the next release of the ViennaRNA Package. However, please
note that the core developers may decide to include your changes in a later version.

\end{enumerate}

\chapter{Contributors}
\label{\detokenize{index:contributors}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Over the past decades since the ViennaRNA Package first sprang to life as part
of Ivo L. Hofackers PhD project, several authors contributed more and more
algorithm implementations. In 2008, Ronny Lorenz took over the extensive task
to harmonize and simplify the already existing implementations for the sake
of easier feature addition. This eventually lead to version 2.0 of the ViennaRNA
Package. Since then, he (re\sphinxhyphen{})implemented a large portion of the currently existing
library features, such as the new, generalized constraints framework, RNA folding
grammar domain extensions, and the major part of the scripting language interface.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Below is a list of most people who contributed larger parts of the implementations:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Daniel Wiegreffe (RNAturtle and RNApuzzler secondary structure layouts)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Andreas Gruber (first approach on RNALfold Z\sphinxhyphen{}score filtering)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Juraj Michalik (non\sphinxhyphen{}redundant Boltzmann sampling)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Gregor Entzian (neighbor, walk)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mario Koestl (worked on SWIG interface and related unit testing)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dominik Luntzer (pertubation fold)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stefan Badelt (cofold evaluation, RNAdesign.pl, cofold findpath extensions)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stefan Hammer (parts of SWIG interface and corresponding unit tests)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ronny Lorenz (circfold, version 2.0, generic constraints, grammar extensions, and much more)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Hakim Tafer (RNAplex, RNAsnoop)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ulrike Mueckstein (RNAup)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stephan Bernhart (RNAcofold, RNAplfold, unpaired probabilities, alifold, and so many more)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stefan Wuchty (RNAsubopt)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ivo Hofacker, Peter Stadler, and Christoph Flamm (almost every implementation up to version 1.8.5)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
We also want to thank the following people:
